sec04-card-sec04-F01.expected_back: A license is a privilege you keep only by continuing to show safe driving skill and knowledge, or it may be restricted, suspended or revoked.

sec04-card-sec04-F02.front: What events appear on your Michigan driving record, and who reports them to the Secretary of State?
sec04-card-sec04-F02.expected_back: Your record lists civil or criminal moving violations and crashes, reported to the Secretary of State by police and courts, along with certain drug crimes.

sec04-card-sec04-F03.front: How does Michigan handle crashes and moving convictions you pick up in another state?
sec04-card-sec04-F03.expected_back: Crashes and convictions from other states are reported to Michigan and appear on your record with points assessed under the Michigan system.

sec04-card-sec04-F04.front: How long do ordinary convictions, select actions, and fatal or impaired-driving convictions stay on your record?
sec04-card-sec04-F04.expected_back: Most convictions stay on your record for at least seven years, some convictions and licensing actions for at least ten years, and a fatality or impaired driving conviction stays permanently.

sec04-card-sec04-F05.front: What protects personal details on your driving record, and which lawful uses still get access?
sec04-card-sec04-F05.expected_back: The Driver Privacy Protection Act keeps personal record details private except for permissible uses set by law, such as insurance rating, vehicle recalls and rental car driver checks.

sec04-card-sec04-F06.front: Into what three legal tiers do traffic violations fall, and what typically follows ignoring a ticket?
sec04-card-sec04-F06.expected_back: Traffic violations may be civil infractions, misdemeanors or felonies, and ignoring a ticket usually leads to license suspension.

sec04-card-sec04-F07.front: What two consequences hit if you receive a moving-violation ticket while your license is already suspended?
sec04-card-sec04-F07.expected_back: Moving violation tickets received while suspended bring more suspensions and a reinstatement fee.

sec04-card-sec04-F11.front: Why must you present extenuating ticket circumstances in court rather than to the Secretary of State?
sec04-card-sec04-F11.expected_back: Extenuating circumstances for a ticket must be raised in court, because the Secretary of State cannot set aside a court conviction.

sec04-card-sec04-F08.front: When do Michigan Vehicle Code points post to your record, and how long do they remain active?
sec04-card-sec04-F08.expected_back: Points, whose values are set in the Michigan Vehicle Code, are posted only after a moving violation conviction and stay on the record for two years from the conviction date.

sec04-card-sec04-F09.front: Which two two-year point patterns trigger a mandatory Michigan driver assessment reexamination?
sec04-card-sec04-F09.expected_back: Six or more one-point violations, or twelve or more points, within a two-year period require a driver assessment reexamination.

sec04-card-sec04-F10.front: How do Michigan driving-record points relate to the points auto insurers use to price coverage?
sec04-card-sec04-F10.expected_back: State record points are separate from the points an insurance company uses to set your rate.

sec04-card-sec04-R05.front: Do points on your Michigan state driving record directly set your auto-insurance premium?
sec04-card-sec04-R05.expected_back: Points on your state driving record are not the same as the points an insurer uses for your rate.

sec04-card-sec04-R06.front: Why doesn't your record turn spotless once your points expire at the two-year mark?
sec04-card-sec04-R06.expected_back: Points drop off after two years, but the convictions behind them stay on the record for at least seven years, some for at least ten, and fatal or impaired driving convictions forever.

sec04-card-sec04-R07.front: Over what window are reexamination triggers counted, and what are both point thresholds?
sec04-card-sec04-R07.expected_back: A reexamination is triggered by six or more one-point violations or by twelve or more points, each measured within two years.

sec04-card-sec04-F12.front: Which felony, intoxication, drug, and crash-scene offenses carry Michigan's maximum six points?
sec04-card-sec04-F12.expected_back: Six-point violations include manslaughter, negligent homicide or another vehicle felony, operating while intoxicated or with any Schedule one drug or cocaine, and failing to stop and identify yourself at a crash.

sec04-card-sec04-F13.front: How many points come from reckless driving, chemical-test refusal, fleeing police, or causing injury or death?
sec04-card-sec04-F13.expected_back: Reckless driving, refusing a chemical alcohol test, fleeing or eluding police, and any moving violation causing injury or death also carry six points.

sec04-card-sec04-F14.front: How many points apply when failing to yield injures or kills a responder, road worker, or animal-implement operator?
sec04-card-sec04-F14.expected_back: Failure to yield that causes death or injury to an emergency responder, a construction worker, or a person operating animal husbandry implements carries six points.

sec04-card-sec04-F15.front: Which four offenses—covering racing, alcohol, underage drinking, and heavy speeding—carry four points?
sec04-card-sec04-F15.expected_back: Four-point violations are drag racing, impaired driving, any bodily alcohol content under age twenty-one, and going sixteen miles per hour or more over the limit.

sec04-card-sec04-F16.front: Which six everyday traffic, crossing, bus, and mid-tier speeding violations post three points?
sec04-card-sec04-F16.expected_back: Three-point violations are careless driving, disobeying a signal or stop sign, improper passing, eleven to fifteen miles per hour over the limit, not stopping at a railroad crossing, and not stopping for a school bus or crossing guard.

sec04-card-sec04-F17.front: Which speeding band, alcohol-container, underage breath-test, emergency-yield, and catch-all violations carry two points?
sec04-card-sec04-F17.expected_back: Two-point violations are six to ten miles per hour over the limit, an open alcohol container, a Preliminary Breath Test refusal under twenty-one, failing to yield or use caution for emergency vehicles, and all other moving violations.

sec04-card-sec04-R01.front: How do Michigan points climb across the six-to-ten, eleven-to-fifteen, and sixteen-plus speeding bands?
sec04-card-sec04-R01.expected_back: Speeding points step up by band: six to ten miles per hour over earns two points, eleven to fifteen miles per hour over earns three, and sixteen miles per hour or more over earns four.

sec04-card-sec04-R02.front: How does refusing an official chemical alcohol test compare in points with an under-twenty-one roadside PBT refusal?
sec04-card-sec04-R02.expected_back: Refusing a chemical alcohol test carries six points, while a driver under twenty-one refusing a Preliminary Breath Test gets two points.

sec04-card-sec04-R03.front: How do Michigan's point totals split between operating while intoxicated and impaired driving or underage alcohol?
sec04-card-sec04-R03.expected_back: Operating while intoxicated is a six-point violation, while impaired driving and any bodily alcohol under twenty-one are four-point violations.

sec04-card-sec04-R04.front: How does the point penalty jump when failing to yield to an emergency vehicle injures or kills a responder?
sec04-card-sec04-R04.expected_back: Simply failing to yield to emergency vehicles costs two points, but a failure to yield that kills or injures an emergency responder costs six.

sec04-card-sec04-F18.front: Why do standard servings of beer, wine, and whiskey impair a driver equally?
sec04-card-sec04-F18.expected_back: Beer, wine and whiskey affect you the same way, because a one point five-ounce whiskey shot, a five-ounce wine glass and a twelve-ounce beer can each hold the same amount of alcohol.

sec04-card-sec04-F19.front: Which two mental faculties take a hit from any standard alcoholic drink?
sec04-card-sec04-F19.expected_back: Any standard drink affects your judgment and self-control.

sec04-card-sec04-F20.front: In what three driving-critical ways can even a single drink impair you?
sec04-card-sec04-F20.expected_back: Even one drink can impair driving by slowing reaction time, dulling concentration and causing vision problems.

sec04-card-sec04-F21.front: Do coffee, cold showers, exercise, or fresh air sober you up—or what actually works?
sec04-card-sec04-F21.expected_back: Coffee, cold showers, exercise and fresh air do not sober you up; only time does.

sec04-card-sec04-F22.front: What sober-ride plan should you lock in before any drinking starts?
sec04-card-sec04-F22.expected_back: The best plan is never to drink and drive: choose a sober designated driver in advance, or get a ride, a taxi or public transportation.

sec04-card-sec04-F23.front: How should you step in if an impaired friend tries to drive or invites you to ride along?
sec04-card-sec04-F23.expected_back: Never let an impaired person drive or ride with one; take their keys if needed and offer a place to sleep.

sec04-card-sec04-R10.front: Why is feeling refreshed after coffee, exercise, or fresh air a trap after drinking?
sec04-card-sec04-R10.expected_back: Coffee, a cold shower, exercise or fresh air may feel sobering, but time is the only thing that removes alcohol’s effects.

sec04-card-sec04-F24.front: Can a drug possession, manufacture, or distribution conviction suspend your license even if no car was involved?
sec04-card-sec04-F24.expected_back: Drug convictions require license suspension even if you were not driving, and possession, manufacture or distribution alone can trigger it.

sec04-card-sec04-F25.front: With zero prior drug violations, how long is the license suspension and hard no-restricted-license period?
sec04-card-sec04-F25.expected_back: With no prior drug violations the suspension lasts six months, and no restricted license is issued for the first thirty days.

sec04-card-sec04-F26.front: What suspension and hard lockout apply if you have a prior drug conviction within seven years?
sec04-card-sec04-F26.expected_back: One or more prior drug convictions within seven years means a one-year suspension with no restricted license for the first sixty days.

sec04-card-sec04-F27.front: How much is the drug-suspension reinstatement fee, and does it bundle with other reinstatement fees?
sec04-card-sec04-F27.expected_back: The drug suspension reinstatement fee is one hundred twenty-five dollars, separate from any other reinstatement fee.

sec04-card-sec04-R08.front: How do suspension length and restricted-license wait double from a first drug offense to a seven-year repeat?
sec04-card-sec04-R08.expected_back: A first drug offense means a six-month suspension with no restricted license for thirty days, while a repeat within seven years means one year with none for sixty days.

sec04-card-sec04-F28.front: Why is driving high illegal even where adult marijuana possession is legal?
sec04-card-sec04-F28.expected_back: Even where marijuana is legal, driving while impaired by it is illegal and unsafe because it distorts your sense of time, space and speed.

sec04-card-sec04-F29.front: How much total marijuana—and concentrate inside that cap—may an adult twenty-one or older legally transport?
sec04-card-sec04-F29.expected_back: Adults twenty-one or older may legally transport up to two point five ounces of marijuana, with no more than fifteen grams as concentrate.

sec04-card-sec04-F30.front: Which five land, air, snow, trail, or water craft are illegal to operate or consume marijuana on while impaired?
sec04-card-sec04-F30.expected_back: It is illegal to operate or be in physical control of a motor vehicle, aircraft, snowmobile, off-road vehicle or motorboat while under the influence of marijuana, or to consume it while doing so.

sec04-card-sec04-F31.front: May drivers or passengers smoke marijuana inside a car on public roads, or carry it into Canada?
sec04-card-sec04-F31.expected_back: Drivers and passengers may not smoke marijuana in a vehicle’s passenger area on a public way, and taking marijuana into Canada is illegal.

sec04-card-sec04-F32.front: What four clues and tests do officers combine to evaluate driver impairment?
sec04-card-sec04-F32.expected_back: Officers judge impairment from your driving, their observations, and standardized and non-standardized field sobriety tests, and may request a chemical test.

sec04-card-sec04-F33.front: When do you agree to Michigan's implied-consent chemical testing, and what happens if you refuse?
sec04-card-sec04-F33.expected_back: Under the implied consent law, every driver agrees to chemical testing by applying for or renewing a license, and refusing the test brings a license suspension.

sec04-card-sec04-F34.front: What jail time, fine, record points, and minor-passenger rule apply to marijuana-impaired driving?
sec04-card-sec04-F34.expected_back: Driving under the influence of marijuana carries the same penalties as alcohol, including up to ninety-three days in jail, up to a five hundred dollars fine, suspension and six points, with tougher penalties when minors are in the vehicle.

sec04-card-sec04-R09.front: How does adult legal marijuana transport coexist with Michigan's impaired-driving penalties?
sec04-card-sec04-R09.expected_back: Carrying up to two point five ounces of marijuana is legal for adults twenty-one or older, yet driving under its influence carries the same penalties as drunk driving.

sec04-card-sec04-F35.front: Which four categories of safety or record trouble allow the Secretary of State to call you in for reexamination?
sec04-card-sec04-F35.expected_back: The Secretary of State may reexamine you for health concerns, violating license restrictions, crash involvement or a poor driving record.

sec04-card-sec04-F36.front: After how few violations can probationary and GDL teen drivers be called in for reexamination?
sec04-card-sec04-F36.expected_back: Probationary and GDL drivers may face a reexamination after just one or two violations.

sec04-card-sec04-F37.front: What does a driver assessment reexamination evaluate, and what licensing controls can it impose?
sec04-card-sec04-F37.expected_back: A reexamination reviews your driving and sets licensing controls such as restrictions, suspensions, revocations or a mix of them.

sec04-card-sec04-F38.front: Which health conditions, fatal-crash findings, and conviction types serve as legal grounds for reexamination?
sec04-card-sec04-F38.expected_back: Legal grounds for reexamination include unfitness or an unsafe physical, visual or mental condition, a fatal crash where the report shows negligence or drinking, and conviction for violating license restrictions.

sec04-card-sec04-F39.front: Alongside twelve points in two years, what two-year crash count allows a driver reexamination?
sec04-card-sec04-F39.expected_back: Three or more injury or property-damage crashes in two years, or twelve or more points in two years, also allow a reexamination.

sec04-card-sec04-F40.front: What happens during your meeting with a driver analyst if licensing controls are placed on your card?
sec04-card-sec04-F40.expected_back: A driver analyst reviews your record with you, and if your license is restricted, suspended or revoked you are told your appeal rights and reinstatement steps.

sec04-card-sec04-F41.front: Which exams and updated professional records can a medical reexamination require?
sec04-card-sec04-F41.expected_back: A medical reexamination may require vision, written and on-road tests and current medical, vision or psychological information.

sec04-card-sec04-F42.front: Which official Michigan web address gathers driver education, GDL rules, parent coaching, and teen risk tools?
sec04-card-sec04-F42.expected_back: Michigan.gov slash NewDrivers collects driver education, GDL, parent coaching and teen risk resources.

sec04-card-sec04-R11.front: How do reexamination thresholds compare between regular full-license holders and probationary or GDL drivers?
sec04-card-sec04-R11.expected_back: Ordinary drivers face reexamination at twelve points or three crashes in two years, while probationary and GDL drivers may be called in after one or two violations.

sec05-card-sec05-F01.front: Roughly how many yearly crash deaths do federal officials link to distraction, and across which three distraction types?
sec05-card-sec05-F01.expected_back: Federal highway safety officials estimate at least three thousand four hundred deaths each year from crashes where a manual, visual or cognitive distraction pulled the driver's focus from controlling the vehicle.

sec05-card-sec05-F02.front: Why might federal crash-death statistics actually undercount distracted driving?
sec05-card-sec05-F02.expected_back: That yearly death estimate may understate the problem, because it is hard to prove a distraction and its part in a crash.

sec05-card-sec05-F03.front: Under what careless or reckless standards can Michigan prosecute a distracted driver?
sec05-card-sec05-F03.expected_back: A distracted driver who drives carelessly or negligently in a way likely to endanger people or property, or with willful or wanton disregard for their safety, can be prosecuted under Michigan law.

sec05-card-sec05-F06.front: Which three body or mental channels do distractions hijack, and why does multitasking fail behind the wheel?
sec05-card-sec05-F06.expected_back: Anything that pulls your eyes from the road, your hands from the wheel or your mind from driving is a hazard, because the brain cannot fully attend to two activities at once.

sec05-card-sec05-F07.front: At sixty-five miles per hour, how far does your car roll during the quarter-second brain switch between tasks?
sec05-card-sec05-F07.expected_back: In the roughly quarter second the brain needs to switch between two tasks, a car going sixty-five miles per hour travels twenty-four feet.

sec05-card-sec05-R10.front: Why does even tapping a radio knob carry real risk at sixty-five miles per hour?
sec05-card-sec05-R10.expected_back: At sixty-five miles per hour a car covers twenty-four feet in the quarter second it takes to shift attention, so even tuning a radio carries risk.

sec05-card-sec05-F08.front: How should you handle maps or directions before pulling out—with a passenger versus solo?
sec05-card-sec05-F08.expected_back: Before driving, ask a front-seat passenger to handle maps or navigation, or plan your route in advance if you drive alone.

sec05-card-sec05-F09.front: How well should you know your cabin climate and audio controls before driving?
sec05-card-sec05-F09.expected_back: Learn your vehicle's controls well enough to adjust temperature or radio settings without looking away from the road.

sec05-card-sec05-F10.front: When do playlist picks, radio presets, and personal grooming belong?
sec05-card-sec05-F10.expected_back: Set radio presets and choose a playlist before you leave, and finish any grooming before starting out or after arriving.

sec05-card-sec05-F11.front: Why must children be buckled and comfortable before you start driving?
sec05-card-sec05-F11.expected_back: Make sure children are comfortable and buckled before the trip, since tending to them while driving is a serious distraction.

sec05-card-sec05-F12.front: How should you treat phones and electronics while moving, and what if a call cannot wait?
sec05-card-sec05-F12.expected_back: While driving, avoid phones, texting devices and navigation or other electronic systems, and if you must call, park safely first.

sec05-card-sec05-F13.front: Which reading, writing, and conversation habits should you keep out of the driver's seat?
sec05-card-sec05-F13.expected_back: Do not take notes, read, look up numbers or get into stressful or confrontational conversations while driving.

sec05-card-sec05-F14.front: What rules apply if you snack or sip in the car, or notice fatigue and daydreaming?
sec05-card-sec05-F14.expected_back: If you eat while driving, pick easy-to-handle food and keep drinks secured in cup holders, and take a break if you feel tired or lost in thought.

sec05-card-sec05-F04.front: What everyday phone actions are illegal while driving in Michigan, and when may you break that rule?
sec05-card-sec05-F04.expected_back: Holding a phone while driving is illegal in Michigan, which covers reading, texting, and making or answering a call, with exceptions for reporting crashes, crimes or other emergencies.

sec05-card-sec05-F05.front: What civil fines hit a first handheld-phone violation versus any repeat violation?
sec05-card-sec05-F05.expected_back: The hand-held phone fine is one hundred dollars for a first offense and two hundred fifty dollars for each later violation.

sec05-card-sec05-F15.front: Who is covered by Michigan's general cell-phone law, and where does it ban holding or using mobile devices?
sec05-card-sec05-F15.expected_back: Michigan's general cell phone law, MCL two hundred fifty-seven.602b, bars every driver from holding or using a mobile electronic device such as a phone or tablet while operating a vehicle on a public road or other public venue.

sec05-card-sec05-F16.front: Which four call, text, video, and social-media actions are explicitly barred on mobile devices while driving?
sec05-card-sec05-F16.expected_back: Banned uses include sending or receiving calls, sending, receiving or reading texts, viewing, recording or transmitting video, and reading or posting to social media.

sec05-card-sec05-F17.front: Which responders may any driver—including teens—text or call to report medical, crash, hazard, fire, or hazmat emergencies?
sec05-card-sec05-F17.expected_back: Any driver, including a teen, may use a device to text nine-one-one or call police, a health-care provider, the fire department or another emergency service to report a medical emergency, crash, serious road hazard, fire or hazardous materials incident.

sec05-card-sec05-F18.front: Beyond crashes and fires, what two live threats let you legally use a phone to alert authorities?
sec05-card-sec05-F18.expected_back: The emergency exception also covers reporting a reckless or apparently impaired driver, or a crime in progress.

sec05-card-sec05-R04.front: How much does a second or third handheld-phone ticket cost compared with your first?
sec05-card-sec05-R04.expected_back: A first hand-held phone offense costs one hundred dollars, and every later one costs two hundred fifty dollars.

sec05-card-sec05-F19.front: Under Kelsey's Law, what phone restriction applies to Level one and Level two GDL teen drivers?
sec05-card-sec05-F19.expected_back: Kelsey's Law, MCL two hundred fifty-seven.602c, bars teens holding a GDL Level one or Level two license from making or receiving non-emergency phone calls.

sec05-card-sec05-F20.front: Under what condition may GDL Level three teens and adult drivers use GPS navigation?
sec05-card-sec05-F20.expected_back: GDL Level three teens and all other drivers may use GPS or navigation as long as they do not type information in by hand.

sec05-card-sec05-F21.front: How much finger contact is permitted when using voice-operated or hands-free features?
sec05-card-sec05-F21.expected_back: Voice-operated or hands-free use is allowed if your hands stop after a single press, tap or swipe to start or end a function or pick a contact, or after using the vehicle's built-in interface.

sec05-card-sec05-F22.front: How does Michigan law treat continuous-recording dash cams and properly used windshield or dash mounts?
sec05-card-sec05-F22.expected_back: A dash cam that continuously records or broadcasts video, and a mounted device used in an already exempt way, are also allowed.

sec05-card-sec05-R01.front: How do hands-free call rules change when a Michigan teen advances from GDL Level two to Level three?
sec05-card-sec05-R01.expected_back: Teens with a Level one or Level two license may not make or take non-emergency calls even hands-free under Kelsey's Law, while Level three teens follow the same hands-free rules as adult drivers.

sec05-card-sec05-R02.front: Why can an eligible driver tap once to answer hands-free yet not type an address into GPS?
sec05-card-sec05-R02.expected_back: Using GPS is allowed only when you do not type in information by hand, whereas a single tap to start or end a hands-free call is allowed.

sec05-card-sec05-R03.front: Who can use Michigan's emergency phone exception, and does it excuse calling parents or friends?
sec05-card-sec05-R03.expected_back: The emergency exception lets any driver, teens included, contact police, fire, health-care or other emergency services, but it does not cover ordinary personal calls.

sec05-card-sec05-F23.front: Under Click It or Ticket, does an officer need another violation before stopping an unbuckled car?
sec05-card-sec05-F23.expected_back: Under Click It or Ticket, an officer may stop a vehicle simply because the driver or passengers are not properly buckled.

sec05-card-sec05-F24.front: Which seats require belts for adults versus passengers younger than sixteen in Michigan?
sec05-card-sec05-F24.expected_back: Michigan requires the driver and every front-seat passenger to wear a seat belt, and every passenger under sixteen to be buckled in any seat.

sec05-card-sec05-F26.front: More than how many lives per year do federal officials credit seat belts with saving?
sec05-card-sec05-F26.expected_back: Federal safety officials report seat belts save more than thirteen thousand lives a year, and buckling up is the most effective single step to protect yourself in a crash.

sec05-card-sec05-F27.front: Do air bags replace seat belts, and where should your shoulder and lap straps cross your body?
sec05-card-sec05-F27.expected_back: Air bags do not replace a seat belt; wear the shoulder belt across the middle of the chest away from the neck and the lap belt low across the hips below the stomach.

sec05-card-sec05-F28.front: What document must a driver carry if medically excused from wearing a seat belt?
sec05-card-sec05-F28.expected_back: A driver excused from wearing a seat belt for a medical reason must carry a doctor's statement.

sec05-card-sec05-R05.front: How does Michigan's mandatory belt rule change at age sixteen for back-seat passengers?
sec05-card-sec05-R05.expected_back: Every passenger under sixteen must be buckled in any seat, while for riders sixteen and older the handbook's belt rule names only the driver and front-seat passengers.

sec05-card-sec05-R09.front: Why must you still position your chest and hip straps properly in an air-bag-equipped car?
sec05-card-sec05-R09.expected_back: Air bags add protection but never replace a belt, which belongs across the middle of the chest and low on the hips.

sec05-card-sec05-F25.front: Which age or height threshold requires a child to use an approved car seat or booster in any seat?
sec05-card-sec05-F25.expected_back: Children under eight, or shorter than four feet nine inches, must ride in an approved car seat or booster seat in every seating position.

sec05-card-sec05-F29.front: When does Michigan law allow leaving a booster, and why are parents urged to prioritize height?
sec05-card-sec05-F29.expected_back: A child rides in a car seat or booster until reaching eight years old or four feet nine inches, whichever comes first, and parents are urged to go by height because a belt may not fit a small child.

sec05-card-sec05-F30.front: Which three authorities govern how a child restraint is installed and buckled?
sec05-card-sec05-F30.expected_back: The child must be secured following the restraint and vehicle makers' instructions and federal safety standards.

sec05-card-sec05-F31.front: Is removing a baby from a car seat to nurse allowed while the vehicle is moving?
sec05-card-sec05-F31.expected_back: Taking a child out of a car seat to nurse while the vehicle is moving is prohibited.

sec05-card-sec05-F32.front: Where must children younger than four ride, and what is the sole multi-child exception?
sec05-card-sec05-F32.expected_back: Children under four must ride in a rear seat when the vehicle has one, unless every rear seat is already filled by children under four.

sec05-card-sec05-F33.front: Under what single air-bag condition may a rear-facing infant seat ride in the front passenger seat?
sec05-card-sec05-F33.expected_back: A rear-facing child seat may go in the front only when the front passenger air bag is turned off.

sec05-card-sec05-F35.front: What two belt-sharing or lap mistakes must you avoid with children, and when should kids buckle?
sec05-card-sec05-F35.expected_back: Never hold a child on your lap or share one seat belt between a child and another passenger, and have children buckle up before you start the engine.

sec05-card-sec05-R06.front: Must a child hit both age eight and four feet nine inches to exit a booster under Michigan law?
sec05-card-sec05-R06.expected_back: A child leaves the car seat or booster at age eight or at four feet nine inches, whichever comes first, though the handbook suggests going by height.

sec05-card-sec05-R07.front: How does the under-four back-seat rule pair with placing a rear-facing seat up front?
sec05-card-sec05-R07.expected_back: Children under four belong in the rear seat, while a rear-facing seat may sit in front only if the passenger air bag is deactivated.

sec05-card-sec05-F34.front: Above what speed is riding in an open pickup bed banned for anyone under eighteen, and which uses are exempt?
sec05-card-sec05-F34.expected_back: No one under eighteen may ride in an open pickup bed above fifteen miles per hour, except for farm, construction, military, parade and authorized emergency or rescue uses.

sec05-card-sec05-F36.front: Where can parents get hands-on help checking or installing a child car seat?
sec05-card-sec05-F36.expected_back: Help installing a car seat is available from community agencies such as local health departments, and a certified technician can be found at cert.safekids.org under Find a Tech.

sec05-card-sec05-F37.front: Why does the handbook warn against buying or using secondhand child safety seats?
sec05-card-sec05-F37.expected_back: Avoid secondhand car seats, which may not meet federal standards, may not work properly, or may be missing parts or instructions.

sec05-card-sec05-R08.front: How does Michigan's pickup-bed age cutoff differ from its all-seat mandatory seat-belt cutoff?
sec05-card-sec05-R08.expected_back: Riders under eighteen may not ride in an open pickup bed above fifteen miles per hour, which is a different age line from the under-sixteen seat belt rule.

sec10-card-sec10-F01.front: Why does sign silhouette matter in Michigan, and how many basic shapes does the handbook teach?
sec10-card-sec10-F01.expected_back: A sign's shape hints at its meaning, and the handbook teaches nine basic shapes to recognize.

sec10-card-sec10-F02.front: Which commands belong to the eight-sided octagon and the downward-pointing triangle?
sec10-card-sec10-F02.expected_back: The eight-sided octagon means STOP, and the triangle means YIELD.

sec10-card-sec10-F03.front: What categories do a four-sided diamond and a five-sided pentagon identify?
sec10-card-sec10-F03.expected_back: A diamond shape marks a warning sign, and a five-sided pentagon marks a school sign.

sec10-card-sec10-F04.front: Which specific highway zone uses a sideways pennant-shaped sign?
sec10-card-sec10-F04.expected_back: A pennant shape warns of a no-passing zone.

sec10-card-sec10-F05.front: How does a horizontal rectangle's message differ from a vertical rectangle's message?
sec10-card-sec10-F05.expected_back: A horizontal rectangle gives directions, while a vertical rectangle states a law.

sec10-card-sec10-F06.front: Which two distinct sign shapes both warn of a railroad crossing?
sec10-card-sec10-F06.expected_back: Both the round sign and the crossbuck mean a railroad crossing.

sec10-card-sec10-R22.front: Both warn of hazards—so what separates a pennant shape from a diamond shape?
sec10-card-sec10-R22.expected_back: The pennant shape is tied to no-passing zones, while the diamond is the general warning shape.

sec10-card-sec10-R23.front: What single road hazard links the circular sign shape and the crossbuck together?
sec10-card-sec10-R23.expected_back: Two different shapes, the round sign and the crossbuck, both stand for a railroad crossing, so either one means look for trains.

sec10-card-sec10-F08.front: What three commands or restrictions does red convey on a traffic sign?
sec10-card-sec10-F08.expected_back: Red on a sign means stop, prohibited or forbidden.

sec10-card-sec10-F09.front: How do blue highway signs and green highway signs split motorist information?
sec10-card-sec10-F09.expected_back: Blue signs point to services and hospitality, and green signs give directions and guidance.

sec10-card-sec10-F10.front: Both call for caution—how does yellow sign color differ from orange sign color?
sec10-card-sec10-F10.expected_back: Yellow signs give caution or a general warning, while orange signals caution for construction or maintenance.

sec10-card-sec10-F11.front: What legal role do black-and-white traffic signs play along Michigan roads?
sec10-card-sec10-F11.expected_back: Black and white signs are regulatory, telling you what is legally allowed or prohibited.

sec10-card-sec10-F12.front: What does fluorescent yellow-green warn of compared with fluorescent pink?
sec10-card-sec10-F12.expected_back: Fluorescent yellow-green warns of schools, pedestrians or bicycles, and fluorescent pink marks an incident, emergency or unplanned event.

sec10-card-sec10-F13.front: What kind of destinations do brown roadside guide signs point toward?
sec10-card-sec10-F13.expected_back: Brown signs point out places of recreation or cultural interest.

sec10-card-sec10-F14.front: What laws do regulatory signs set, and what shape and color combinations do they usually take?
sec10-card-sec10-F14.expected_back: Regulatory signs set specific laws on traffic speed and movement and are usually rectangles in white and black, red, white and black, or red and white.

sec10-card-sec10-R24.front: How do Michigan's three warning colors—yellow, orange, and fluorescent pink—divide up road hazards?
sec10-card-sec10-R24.memory_hook: Yellow permanent, orange work, pink incidents
sec10-card-sec10-R24.expected_back: Yellow is the general caution color, but orange is caution reserved for construction or maintenance, and fluorescent pink is for incidents and unplanned events.

sec10-card-sec10-R25.front: Can you match blue, green, and brown guide signs to their three traveler topics?
sec10-card-sec10-R25.memory_hook: Blue services, green routes, brown parks
sec10-card-sec10-R25.expected_back: Blue signs mean services, green signs mean directions, and brown signs mean recreation or culture.

sec10-card-sec10-F07.front: Which four levels of highway networks do numbered route markers identify?
sec10-card-sec10-F07.expected_back: Route markers identify the federal, state and county road systems: interstate freeway, U.S. highway, state highway and county route signs.

sec10-card-sec10-F15.front: What has happened when an Incident Ahead sign appears, and what do follow-up signs provide?
sec10-card-sec10-F15.expected_back: An Incident Ahead sign means an emergency or other unplanned event has disrupted traffic, and the signs that follow guide you around or through the area.

sec10-card-sec10-F16.front: What information do a blue gas-pump panel and a green Exit gore panel give freeway drivers?
sec10-card-sec10-F16.expected_back: A gas pump sign shows where gas stations are, and an Exit sign shows where the freeway exit is.

sec10-card-sec10-F21.front: What does a green destination sign listing town names—like Brookfield and Onondaga—tell you?
sec10-card-sec10-F21.expected_back: A destination guide sign such as Brookfield and Onondaga tells you which way to go to reach those communities.

sec10-card-sec10-F22.front: Who may park in a stall marked by a sign bearing the wheelchair symbol?
sec10-card-sec10-F22.expected_back: A parking sign with a wheelchair symbol reserves the space for people with disabilities.

sec10-card-sec10-F23.front: What road network does an M-numbered route marker—such as M-thirty-two—identify?
sec10-card-sec10-F23.expected_back: A state route marker identifies a state highway, such as M-thirty-two.

sec10-card-sec10-F24.front: What kind of restriction can a Parking Permitted sign place on legal street parking?
sec10-card-sec10-F24.expected_back: A parking permitted sign can limit the stay, such as two-hour parking between eight thirty a.m. and five thirty p.m.

sec10-card-sec10-F36.front: What do a blue Rest Area sign and a pentagon School Crossing sign each point out?
sec10-card-sec10-F36.expected_back: A Rest Area sign points to public restrooms, and a School Crossing sign warns of a crossing for children ahead.

sec10-card-sec10-F25.front: What two obligations must you fulfill at every red octagonal stop sign before moving on?
sec10-card-sec10-F25.expected_back: At a stop sign, stop completely and yield to traffic and pedestrians before going on.

sec10-card-sec10-F26.front: What speed and priority actions does a red-and-white triangular yield sign require?
sec10-card-sec10-F26.expected_back: At a yield sign, slow down and let vehicles crossing your path go first.

sec10-card-sec10-F27.front: What maneuvers do No Turn On Red and red-circle slash turn signs prohibit?
sec10-card-sec10-F27.expected_back: No Turn On Red forbids turning on a red light, and separate signs prohibit right turns or U-turns.

sec10-card-sec10-F28.front: What do lane-use turn signs and a Center Lane Left Turn Only sign assign?
sec10-card-sec10-F28.expected_back: Lane-use signs show which lanes may turn left, and a Center Lane Left Turn Only sign reserves the middle lane for left turns.

sec10-card-sec10-F18.front: How does traffic move across all lanes where a One Way sign is posted?
sec10-card-sec10-F18.expected_back: A One Way sign means traffic in every lane moves in the same direction.

sec10-card-sec10-F19.front: What legal rule does a Speed Limit fifty sign establish on that roadway stretch?
sec10-card-sec10-F19.expected_back: A Speed Limit fifty sign sets the legal maximum on that stretch at fifty miles per hour

sec10-card-sec10-R10.front: Why are Roundabout Ahead, Stop Ahead, and Yield Ahead diamonds posted upstream?
sec10-card-sec10-R10.expected_back: Roundabout Ahead, Stop Ahead and Yield Ahead signs warn that a roundabout, a stop sign or a yield sign is coming up.

sec10-card-sec10-F30.front: On which side of a median island or roadway obstruction must you pass at a Keep Left sign?
sec10-card-sec10-F30.expected_back: A Keep Left sign means traffic should go only to the left of a road feature or obstruction.

sec10-card-sec10-F31.front: What simple command does a square Do Not Enter sign enforce?
sec10-card-sec10-F31.expected_back: A Do Not Enter sign means you may not drive into that area.

sec10-card-sec10-F32.front: Who may use a freeway median strip marked Authorized Vehicles Only—and how must everyday drivers reverse direction?
sec10-card-sec10-F32.expected_back: Authorized Vehicles Only marks a freeway emergency crossover reserved for police, emergency or maintenance vehicles; to reverse direction, exit and re-enter the freeway the other way.

sec10-card-sec10-F33.front: What dangerous situation has already happened if you face a Wrong Way sign, and what must you do?
sec10-card-sec10-F33.expected_back: A Wrong Way sign means you have entered a lane of oncoming traffic and must get out as quickly and safely as possible.

sec10-card-sec10-F34.front: What vehicles are barred wherever a No Trucks sign stands?
sec10-card-sec10-F34.expected_back: A No Trucks sign bars trucks from the posted area.

sec10-card-sec10-R05.front: When a yellow Obstacle in Roadway diamond shows arrows splitting left and right, where may you pass?
sec10-card-sec10-R05.expected_back: An Obstacle in Roadway sign means a traffic island or obstruction is ahead and you may pass on either side.

sec10-card-sec10-R27.front: How does your position differ when facing Do Not Enter versus facing Wrong Way?
sec10-card-sec10-R27.expected_back: Wrong Way means you are already in an oncoming lane, while Do Not Enter forbids going into the area in the first place.

sec10-card-sec10-F29.front: What does Do Not Pass forbid, and what does Pass With Care on the right announce?
sec10-card-sec10-F29.expected_back: A Do Not Pass sign prohibits passing, and a Pass With Care sign on the right marks the end of that no-passing zone, so pass when safe.

sec10-card-sec10-F35.front: When a number plaque under a railroad crossbuck displays three tracks, what lies at the grade crossing?
sec10-card-sec10-F35.expected_back: The railroad crossbuck pictured in the sign challenge warns that a crossing made up of three tracks is ahead.

sec10-card-sec10-F37.front: What top speed defines vehicles wearing a rear orange slow-moving triangle, and what examples use it?
sec10-card-sec10-F37.expected_back: The orange slow-moving vehicle triangle is mounted on the back of vehicles that do not travel faster than twenty-five miles per hour, such as Amish buggies and farm combines, so drive with care around them.

sec10-card-sec10-R03.front: What hazard ahead does a warning sign bearing the letters R-R announce?
sec10-card-sec10-R03.expected_back: A sign marked RR warns that a railroad crossing is ahead.

sec10-card-sec10-R08.front: Which side of the highway mounts the yellow No Passing Zone pennant, and what does it warn?
sec10-card-sec10-R08.expected_back: The yellow No Passing Zone pennant sits on the left side of the road and warns that passing would be hazardous.

sec10-card-sec10-R26.front: How do Do Not Pass and right-side Pass With Care work together along a two-lane highway?
sec10-card-sec10-R26.expected_back: Do Not Pass and Pass With Care work as a pair: the first forbids passing, and the second, posted on the right after it, ends the no-passing zone.

sec10-card-sec10-F17.front: Why does a Bridge Ices Before Road sign matter when normal pavement still feels dry and grippy?
sec10-card-sec10-F17.expected_back: Bridge Ices Before Road warns that a bridge may be icy even when the road is clear.

sec10-card-sec10-F20.front: How must you drive—and whom must you obey—where a School Children Present sign stands?
sec10-card-sec10-F20.expected_back: A School Children Present sign means children are nearby, so drive carefully and follow a school crossing guard's directions.

sec10-card-sec10-R01.front: How does a Road Turns Left diamond differ from a Road Curves Ahead reverse-curve diamond?
sec10-card-sec10-R01.expected_back: A Road Turns Left sign warns of a sharp turn or curve to the left, while a Road Curves Ahead sign warns of a sharp curve left and then right.

sec10-card-sec10-R02.front: What does a small speed plaque—like thirty-five miles per hour—mounted beneath a Winding Curve Ahead sign advise?
sec10-card-sec10-R02.expected_back: A Winding Curve Ahead sign with a speed plaque tells you to limit your speed, in the handbook example to thirty-five miles per hour

sec10-card-sec10-R04.front: What do Watch for Bicyclists and Watch for Pedestrians warning diamonds alert you to?
sec10-card-sec10-R04.expected_back: Watch for Bicyclists and Watch for Pedestrians signs mean those road users may be nearby, so drive carefully.

sec10-card-sec10-R06.front: What measurement does a Maximum Height sign—such as twelve feet six inches—display?
sec10-card-sec10-R06.expected_back: A Maximum Height sign gives the clearance under a bridge or structure, such as twelve feet six inches.

sec10-card-sec10-R07.front: How fast should you take a freeway off-ramp marked Exit twenty-five miles per hour?
sec10-card-sec10-R07.expected_back: An Exit twenty-five miles per hour sign means you should take the exit at no more than twenty-five miles per hour

sec10-card-sec10-R09.front: How does a cross-shaped Intersection Ahead symbol differ from a Side Road Ahead symbol?
sec10-card-sec10-R09.expected_back: An Intersection Ahead sign warns of a crossing road, while a Side Road Ahead sign warns of a road joining from the right.

sec10-card-sec10-R11.front: What lies ahead when you pass an orange Road Work Ahead diamond?
sec10-card-sec10-R11.expected_back: The orange Road Work Ahead sign means crews are working in the area, so drive with care.

sec10-card-sec10-R15.front: What terrain does a Hill sign warn of, and what two actions should drivers—especially heavy trucks—take?
sec10-card-sec10-R15.expected_back: A Hill sign warns of a steep downgrade; every vehicle, especially a large truck, should check its brakes and gear down if needed.

sec10-card-sec10-R16.front: When does the pavement hazard marked by a Slippery When Wet sign kick in?
sec10-card-sec10-R16.expected_back: Slippery When Wet warns that the road surface becomes slick in bad weather.

sec10-card-sec10-R18.front: What kind of crossing does a combined Bicyclists and Pedestrians sign identify?
sec10-card-sec10-R18.expected_back: A Bicyclists and Pedestrians sign marks a nearby shared crossing for both groups.

sec10-card-sec10-R12.front: From which side will vehicles blend in when you pass a Merging Traffic diamond?
sec10-card-sec10-R12.expected_back: A Merging Traffic sign means traffic will merge from the right.

sec10-card-sec10-R13.front: Which lane is disappearing at a Lane Ends Merge Left sign, and who holds right-of-way during the merge?
sec10-card-sec10-R13.expected_back: A Lane Ends Merge Left sign means the right lane is ending, so merge left and yield to traffic already in the left lane.

sec10-card-sec10-R14.front: What highway transition do Divided Highway Ends and Two-Way Traffic signs announce?
sec10-card-sec10-R14.expected_back: A Divided Highway Ends sign means the divided road becomes two lanes of traffic, and a Two-Way Traffic sign means two-way traffic begins, so keep right.

sec10-card-sec10-R17.front: How much distance remains before the right lane disappears at Michigan's Right Lane Ends notice?
sec10-card-sec10-R17.expected_back: A Right Lane Ends sign gives notice that the right lane ends in five hundred feet, so prepare to merge left.

sec10-card-sec10-R19.front: Which two paint colors form standard lane markings, and what three jobs do they perform?
sec10-card-sec10-R19.expected_back: Pavement markings are white or yellow, and they warn, regulate and inform drivers.

sec10-card-sec10-R20.front: What traffic flow do white lane lines—and specifically broken white lines—separate?
sec10-card-sec10-R20.expected_back: White lines divide lanes of traffic moving in the same direction, and broken white lines separate lanes on roads with more than one lane moving the same way.

sec10-card-sec10-R21.front: What lane-keeping rule applies to a broken white line versus a double yellow line?
sec10-card-sec10-R21.expected_back: Never straddle a broken white line or cross a double yellow line.

sec13-card-sec13-F01.front: Alongside vehicle controls and traffic laws, what five personal traits does safe driving require?
sec13-card-sec13-F01.expected_back: Safe driving takes more than vehicle basics and memorized rules; it also needs good judgment, reflexes, experience, patience and common sense.

sec13-card-sec13-F02.front: Through what three practice stages does a teen driver develop real road skill and confidence?
sec13-card-sec13-F02.expected_back: A teen's skill and confidence grow through practice, first on the driver education range, then with a parent, guardian or designated licensed adult twenty-one or older, and later alone once licensed.

sec13-card-sec13-F03.front: What mental habit can dull hazard awareness even among experienced middle-aged drivers?
sec13-card-sec13-F03.expected_back: Experienced middle-aged drivers can become complacent, and driving on autopilot leaves them less tuned to the risks around them.

sec13-card-sec13-F04.front: How can older drivers sharpen changing driving skills, and which two national programs does Michigan highlight?
sec13-card-sec13-F04.expected_back: Older drivers can improve through added training, and AAA RoadWise Driver and AARP Driver Safety offer refresher courses, listed at Michigan.gov slash AgingDriver.

sec13-card-sec13-F05.front: Which reckless traffic maneuvers and hostile signals characterize aggressive drivers?
sec13-card-sec13-F05.expected_back: Aggressive drivers run stop signs and red lights, speed, tailgate, weave, pass illegally on the right, and may gesture, yell, honk or flash their headlights.

sec13-card-sec13-F06.front: What dangerous escalation can happen if you retaliate against an aggressive driver, and what makes it road rage?
sec13-card-sec13-F06.expected_back: Answering aggression in kind can escalate into road rage, where a weapon or the vehicle itself is used to attack another driver.

sec13-card-sec13-F07.front: What percentage of all traffic fatalities have federal safety officials linked to aggressive driving behaviors?
sec13-card-sec13-F07.expected_back: Federal highway safety officials have estimated that aggressive driving behaviors cause sixty-six percent of all traffic fatalities.

sec13-card-sec13-F08.front: How should you respond when another motorist merges or turns poorly in front of you?
sec13-card-sec13-F08.expected_back: Merge smoothly, and when another driver merges or turns badly, slow down, give room, and back off rather than trying to prove you are right.

sec13-card-sec13-F09.front: What should you do if someone tailgates you while you are passing in the left lane, and why?
sec13-card-sec13-F09.expected_back: If someone tailgates you while you pass in the left lane, move back right when safe and let faster traffic go, since a backed-up left lane tempts aggressive drivers to take risks.

sec13-card-sec13-F10.front: How should you handle a tailgater on an ordinary road, and why is putting them ahead safer?
sec13-card-sec13-F10.expected_back: If another driver tailgates you, pull over and let them pass so the unsafe driver is ahead where you can see them.

sec13-card-sec13-F11.front: What rule applies to angry hand gestures—and how should you respond if another driver gestures after your mistake?
sec13-card-sec13-F11.expected_back: Never gesture at other drivers in anger, and if you made a mistake and someone gestures, signal that you are sorry.

sec13-card-sec13-F12.front: What four actions protect you when an aggressive driver tries to confront you on the road?
sec13-card-sec13-F12.expected_back: When confronted by an aggressive driver, get out of the way, avoid eye contact, ignore gestures or insults, and call police to report them when safe.

sec13-card-sec13-F13.front: How should you handle the scene if an aggressive driver crashes farther up the road ahead of you?
sec13-card-sec13-F13.expected_back: If an aggressive driver crashes farther ahead, stop a safe distance from the scene, wait for police and report what you saw.

sec13-card-sec13-F14.front: Which roadway location accounts for more traffic deaths and serious injuries than any other?
sec13-card-sec13-F14.expected_back: Intersection crashes cause more traffic deaths and serious injuries than crashes on any other part of the road.

sec13-card-sec13-F15.front: What elements must you scan approaching an intersection, and what rule applies whenever another driver's move looks uncertain?
sec13-card-sec13-F15.expected_back: Approaching an intersection, check oncoming and cross traffic, pedestrians, signals, signs, markings, road condition and blind areas, and let others go first whenever you are unsure what they will do.

sec13-card-sec13-F16.front: Why should you look twice specifically for motorcycles, bicycles, and mopeds at intersections?
sec13-card-sec13-F16.expected_back: Look twice for motorcycles, bicycles and mopeds at intersections because their speed and distance are hard to judge.

sec13-card-sec13-F17.front: How should you handle an intersection where trees, buildings, or winter snowbanks block your cross-traffic view?
sec13-card-sec13-F17.expected_back: When trees, buildings or snow piles block your view at an intersection, creep forward slowly until you can see past them.

sec13-card-sec13-F18.front: How do freeways move traffic, and which six road users or small vehicles are barred from using them?
sec13-card-sec13-F18.expected_back: Freeways carry one-direction traffic with no stops or intersections, and pedestrians, motorcycles of one hundred twenty-four cubic centimeters or less, mopeds, bicycles, ATVs and slow-moving vehicles are banned from them.

sec13-card-sec13-F19.front: Why must you scan carefully for Do Not Enter, Wrong Way, and speed signs at freeway interchanges?
sec13-card-sec13-F19.expected_back: Entrance ramps often sit beside exit ramps, so watch for Do Not Enter, Wrong Way and speed limit signs.

sec13-card-sec13-F20.front: What steps take you smoothly from the acceleration lane onto the freeway—and whom must you yield to?
sec13-card-sec13-F20.expected_back: Use the acceleration lane to reach freeway speed, signal, check mirrors and glance over your shoulder, then merge into a safe gap, yielding to freeway traffic and not counting on others to let you in.

sec13-card-sec13-F24.front: How should freeway drivers respond near entrance merge signs, and what sudden exit mistake should they watch for?
sec13-card-sec13-F24.expected_back: Merge signs near entrances warn of entering traffic; adjust speed or change lanes safely to help them merge, and watch for drivers who brake or swerve suddenly toward an exit.

sec13-card-sec13-F26.front: Under Michigan's merge law, which driver holds the legal duty to yield and adjust speed when entering or leaving a freeway?
sec13-card-sec13-F26.expected_back: Michigan's merge law, MCL two hundred fifty-seven point six four nine(seven), means the merging driver must yield to traffic close enough to be an immediate hazard and adjust speed and position to merge safely, whether entering or leaving the freeway.

sec13-card-sec13-R19.front: Between the merging ramp driver and existing freeway traffic, who must adjust speed and lane placement?
sec13-card-sec13-R19.expected_back: The merging driver, not freeway traffic, must adjust speed and placement to merge safely.

sec13-card-sec13-F21.front: On a freeway with two lanes in your direction, when may you legally use the left lane?
sec13-card-sec13-F21.expected_back: On a two-lane freeway keep right except to pass, exit left, let a vehicle merge, in heavy congestion, or when emergency vehicles or construction workers are on the shoulders.

sec13-card-sec13-F22.front: Which lanes may you use when a freeway has three or more lanes in your direction, and what if you drive near minimum speed?
sec13-card-sec13-F22.expected_back: With three or more lanes in your direction you may use any lane, but stay with the slower traffic if driving at or near the minimum speed.

sec13-card-sec13-F23.front: How many occupants do high-occupancy vehicle lanes require during peak hours—and who can use them off-peak or anytime?
sec13-card-sec13-F23.expected_back: HOV lanes require two or more occupants during peak hours such as rush hour, are open to everyone outside those hours, and motorcycles may use them any time.

sec13-card-sec13-F25.front: When is stopping on a freeway permitted, and how must you pull off?
sec13-card-sec13-F25.expected_back: Stop on a freeway only in an emergency, and then use hazard flashers, slow gradually and pull completely off the pavement.

sec13-card-sec13-F27.front: Where should you begin braking when exiting a freeway, and why must you respect the ramp speed sign?
sec13-card-sec13-F27.expected_back: To exit, check traffic and signal into the deceleration lane, and do not slow down until you are fully in that lane, then obey the ramp speed limit since many ramps curve sharply.

sec13-card-sec13-F28.front: What must you never do if you miss your freeway exit—including at paved median crossovers—and what is the right move?
sec13-card-sec13-F28.expected_back: If you miss your exit, never back up, turn around or use the median crossover, which is only for emergency and MDOT vehicles; go to the next exit and come back.

sec13-card-sec13-R17.front: How does Michigan's lane-selection rule change when a freeway expands from two lanes to three or more in your direction?
sec13-card-sec13-R17.expected_back: On a two-lane freeway you keep right except in listed cases, but with three or more lanes any lane is allowed unless you are near the minimum speed.

sec13-card-sec13-R18.front: During what time window do HOV occupancy limits apply, and which vehicle type is exempt at all hours?
sec13-card-sec13-R18.expected_back: HOV restrictions apply only during peak hours, and motorcycles are exempt at all times.

sec13-card-sec13-F29.front: Why does freeway driving trigger drowsiness and highway hypnosis so easily?
sec13-card-sec13-F29.expected_back: Fatigue is one of the biggest freeway dangers, since the steady hum of wind, tires and engine can make you sleepy or hypnotized.

sec13-card-sec13-F30.front: Why avoid trusting coffee or stay-awake pills on long drives, and what break schedule works instead?
sec13-card-sec13-F30.expected_back: Do not rely on coffee or stay-awake drugs; if tired, take a ten-minute break at least every two hours or let someone else drive.

sec13-card-sec13-F31.front: How should you use your eyes if you must continue driving briefly while feeling tired until reaching a stop?
sec13-card-sec13-F31.expected_back: If you must keep driving while tired, keep moving your eyes across the road, check mirrors, and look near, far, left and right.

sec13-card-sec13-F32.front: In what traffic and road setting does cruise control work best, and how high should you set it?
sec13-card-sec13-F32.expected_back: Cruise control works best in rural areas with light traffic; set it at or below the speed limit.

sec13-card-sec13-F33.front: How do pressing the gas pedal versus pressing the brake pedal affect active cruise control?
sec13-card-sec13-F33.expected_back: Pressing the accelerator does not cancel cruise control, but pressing the brake pedal does.

sec13-card-sec13-F34.front: Under which four traffic, ramp, weather, or towing conditions should you keep cruise control switched off?
sec13-card-sec13-F34.expected_back: Avoid cruise control in heavy traffic, near many ramps, on roads slick with rain, snow or ice, and when towing heavy loads, since constant resetting distracts you.

sec13-card-sec13-R20.front: What happens to your cruise-control setting if you tap the accelerator compared with tapping the brake?
sec13-card-sec13-R20.expected_back: Tapping the accelerator leaves cruise control on, but touching the brake turns it off.

sec13-card-sec13-R01.front: What three emergency responses help you survive an oncoming vehicle drifting into your lane?
sec13-card-sec13-R01.expected_back: If an oncoming vehicle is in your lane, tap the horn if there is time, brake hard without locking the wheels if you lack anti-lock brakes, and look for an escape route on the right edge.

sec13-card-sec13-R02.front: Why should you avoid swerving into the left lane to dodge an oncoming car in your lane?
sec13-card-sec13-R02.expected_back: Avoid swerving left from an oncoming vehicle, because its driver may notice you and return to the proper lane; stop in your lane only if there is room and you cannot pull off.

sec13-card-sec13-R03.front: When stopping in time is impossible, how should you steer around a vehicle ahead?
sec13-card-sec13-R03.expected_back: If you cannot stop before hitting another vehicle, steer around it, turning no more than you need.

sec13-card-sec13-R12.front: Which two abrupt driver inputs cause most skids on slick roads, and how can you feel surface grip early?
sec13-card-sec13-R12.expected_back: Most skids come from turning too fast or stopping suddenly on slippery pavement, so test the brakes lightly to feel the road.

sec13-card-sec13-R14.front: What sequence of pedal and steering moves recovers your car from a skid—including any counter-skid?
sec13-card-sec13-R14.expected_back: In a skid, lift off the accelerator, point the front wheels only where you want to go, expect a secondary skid the other way, steer again, then straighten the wheels.

sec13-card-sec13-R15.front: How does emergency braking with anti-lock brakes differ from threshold braking without anti-lock?
sec13-card-sec13-R15.expected_back: Anti-lock brakes need hard, firm pressure from the start held until you stop, and vibration or pulsing is normal, while without anti-lock you brake just short of locking and release and reapply if the wheels lock, called threshold or controlled braking.

sec13-card-sec13-R16.front: How should you apply the brake pedal to slow and stop under normal dry-road conditions?
sec13-card-sec13-R16.expected_back: Under normal conditions, a steady, firm push on the brake pedal is how you slow and stop.

sec13-card-sec13-R13.front: Why must standard brakes stay unlocked during a hard stop, and how do full anti-lock brakes let you steer?
sec13-card-sec13-R13.expected_back: With standard brakes, steady pressure without locking the wheels keeps them turning so you can steer, while with full anti-lock brakes you keep pressing and steer.

sec13-card-sec13-R04.front: Which fluids should you inspect before Michigan winter arrives, including a smart windshield-washer upgrade?
sec13-card-sec13-R04.expected_back: Pre-winter maintenance is the best way to travel safely: check power steering, brake, washer and oil fluids, keep antifreeze strong and fresh, and consider washer fluid with antifreeze.

sec13-card-sec13-R05.front: How should you adjust trip time, speed, and gap in fog, rain, or snow—and what freezes first?
sec13-card-sec13-R05.expected_back: In fog, rain or snow leave extra time, drive slower and increase following distance, and remember bridges and underpasses freeze before the road in cold weather.

sec13-card-sec13-R06.front: When during a rainfall is pavement slickest, why, and how much following distance should you leave?
sec13-card-sec13-R06.expected_back: Roads are slickest in the first half hour of rain because oil from vehicles has not yet washed off, so slow down, take extra care at intersections, and allow at least twice the normal following distance.

sec13-card-sec13-R07.front: Why must you test your brakes after driving through deep puddles or heavy downpours, and how do you dry them?
sec13-card-sec13-R07.expected_back: After deep water or heavy rain, test your brakes, which may pull or fail to hold, and press gently while driving slowly until they work normally.

sec13-card-sec13-R08.front: What happens to your tires during hydroplaning, and which three factors make it much more likely?
sec13-card-sec13-R08.expected_back: Hydroplaning happens when tires ride on top of water and can cost you control; worn tires, low pressure and too much speed make it more likely.

sec13-card-sec13-R09.front: Why must you never drive around flood barricades—and why avoid deep standing water even without barricades?
sec13-card-sec13-R09.expected_back: Never drive around barricades closing a flooded road, since debris, power lines or a washed-out road may be hidden; without barricades, consider another route, and deep water can damage the engine.

sec13-card-sec13-R10.front: Which headlights belong on in fog, and what should you do if visibility drops to zero?
sec13-card-sec13-R10.expected_back: Drive slowly in fog with low-beam headlights, ready to stop, and if you cannot see at all, pull off, turn on the four-way flashers and wait.

sec13-card-sec13-R11.front: How should you adjust speed and braking on snow and ice—and what winter crossing hazard does Michigan highlight?
sec13-card-sec13-R11.expected_back: On ice and snow drive slowly, slow down gradually, and listen and watch for snowmobiles and trail crossing signs, since stopping power is reduced.

sec02-card-sec02-F01.front: How many driver-education segments and licensing tiers make up Michigan's Graduated Driver Licensing, and when does GDL end?
sec02-card-sec02-F01.expected_back: Graduated Driver Licensing combines two driver education segments with requirements for three license levels, adds privileges at each level, and ends when you turn eighteen.

sec02-card-sec02-F02.front: What is the earliest age you may begin driver-education Segment one, and whose permission is required?
sec02-card-sec02-F02.expected_back: You may start driver education Segment one at fourteen years, eight months old with a parent’s or guardian’s permission.

sec02-card-sec02-F03.front: How many classroom, behind-the-wheel, and observation hours are required in driver-education Segment one?
sec02-card-sec02-F03.expected_back: Segment one takes at least twenty-four hours in the classroom, at least six hours behind the wheel and at least four hours observing from a training vehicle.

sec02-card-sec02-F04.front: What minimum percentage score is required to pass the Segment one state exam?
sec02-card-sec02-F04.expected_back: Finishing Segment one also requires a score of at least seventy percent on the Segment one state exam.

sec02-card-sec02-F12.front: What logged driving hours—including night hours—and Level one holding period are required before starting Segment two?
sec02-card-sec02-F12.expected_back: To enter Segment two you need a log showing at least thirty supervised hours, at least two of them at night, and at least three consecutive months holding the Level one license.

sec02-card-sec02-F13.front: How many classroom hours does Segment two include, and what score passes its state exam?
sec02-card-sec02-F13.expected_back: Segment two includes at least six hours of classroom instruction, and its state exam must be passed with at least seventy percent.

sec02-card-sec02-R10.front: What passing score do the Segment one and Segment two driver-education state exams have in common?
sec02-card-sec02-R10.expected_back: The Segment one and Segment two driver education state exams share the same minimum score of seventy percent.

sec02-card-sec02-F05.front: What minimum age, office accompaniment, and screening apply to getting a Level one Learner's License?
sec02-card-sec02-F05.expected_back: The Level one Learner’s License needs a minimum age of fourteen years, nine months, an office visit together with a parent or legal guardian, and passing the vision and health standards.

sec02-card-sec02-F06.front: Alongside your Segment one certificate, which four identity and residency proofs must you bring for Level one?
sec02-card-sec02-F06.expected_back: For Level one you bring the Segment one Certificate of Completion plus proof of a valid Social Security number or an ineligibility letter, U.S. citizenship or legal presence, identity and Michigan residency.

sec02-card-sec02-F07.front: What convenience do teens issued a photo hard card at Level one get at Level two and at age eighteen?
sec02-card-sec02-F07.expected_back: A teen given a photo hard card for Level one skips the office visit for Level two, and the regular operator’s license is mailed when that teen turns eighteen.

sec02-card-sec02-F08.front: Who must sit in the front passenger seat whenever a Level one driver is behind the wheel?
sec02-card-sec02-F08.expected_back: With a Level one license you may drive only when a licensed parent, guardian, or designated licensed adult aged twenty-one or older sits in the front seat beside you.

sec02-card-sec02-F09.front: What written proof must a designated adult aged twenty-one or older have to supervise a Level one driver?
sec02-card-sec02-F09.expected_back: A designated adult supervising a Level one driver needs a signed authorization letter from the parent or guardian.

sec02-card-sec02-F10.front: How many total supervised hours—and how many night hours—must a Level one driver log before taking the skills test?
sec02-card-sec02-F10.expected_back: A Level one driver keeps a supervised driving log and must reach at least fifty hours, ten of them at night, before the driving skills test.

sec02-card-sec02-F11.front: What restriction does Kelsey's Law place on a Level one learner behind the wheel?
sec02-card-sec02-F11.expected_back: Kelsey’s Law bars a Level one driver from using a cell phone while driving.

sec02-card-sec02-R01.front: How far apart are the minimum age to begin Segment one and the minimum age to receive a Level one license?
sec02-card-sec02-R01.expected_back: Segment one can begin at fourteen years, eight months, but the Level one Learner’s License cannot be issued until fourteen years, nine months, so the two ages differ by one month.

sec02-card-sec02-R08.front: What three requirements must a non-parent adult meet to supervise a Level one teen legally?
sec02-card-sec02-R08.expected_back: A supervising adult who is not the parent or guardian must be licensed, at least twenty-one, and carry the parent’s signed authorization letter.

sec02-card-sec02-F14.front: What four age, coursework, logged-hour, and holding-time rules must a teen satisfy before taking the driving skills test?
sec02-card-sec02-F14.expected_back: To take the driving skills test you must be at least fifteen, have finished Segment two, have the fifty supervised hours with ten at night, and have held Level one for at least six months.

sec02-card-sec02-F15.front: Which documents must you bring to your driving skills test, and who administers the test in Michigan?
sec02-card-sec02-F15.expected_back: At the skills test you show the completed log, your Level one license, the Segment two certificate, and insurance and registration for the test vehicle, and approved driver testing businesses give the test.

sec02-card-sec02-R02.front: How do the supervised driving hours required to enter Segment two compare with those required for the skills test?
sec02-card-sec02-R02.expected_back: The Segment two log needs thirty supervised hours with two at night, while the skills test needs the full fifty hours with ten at night.

sec02-card-sec02-F16.front: What age, Level one holding time, and clean-record window are required for a Level two Intermediate License?
sec02-card-sec02-F16.expected_back: The Level two Intermediate License requires age sixteen, at least six months on Level one, and a record clear of violations, at-fault crashes and suspensions for the ninety days before you apply.

sec02-card-sec02-F17.front: How do teens who hold a Level one photo hard card advance to Level two once qualified?
sec02-card-sec02-F17.expected_back: Hard-card teens who meet the Level two requirements and have passed the skills test move up to Level two automatically.

sec02-card-sec02-F18.front: What must teens holding a paper Level one credential do—and bring—to move up to Level two?
sec02-card-sec02-F18.expected_back: Paper-card teens must visit an office with their Level one license, Segment two certificate, Driving Skills Test Certificate and the Social Security, legal presence, identity and residency documents described in form SOS-four hundred twenty-eight.

sec02-card-sec02-F19.front: During what nighttime hours may a Level two driver not drive solo, and what exceptions allow driving then?
sec02-card-sec02-F19.expected_back: A Level two driver may not drive from ten p.m. to five a.m. unless a parent, guardian or designated licensed adult aged twenty-one or older is along, or the trip is for work, to or from work, or to or from an authorized activity.

sec02-card-sec02-F20.front: How many passengers under twenty-one may ride with a Level two driver, and what four exceptions lift that cap?
sec02-card-sec02-F20.expected_back: A Level two driver may carry at most one passenger under twenty-one, unless a parent, guardian or designated adult aged twenty-one or older rides along, the passengers are immediate family, or the trip is for work or an authorized activity.

sec02-card-sec02-F21.front: When may a Level two driver use a phone under Kelsey's Law, and what penalties can a violation bring?
sec02-card-sec02-F21.expected_back: Kelsey’s Law forbids a Level two driver from using a phone except in an emergency, and a violation could bring a civil infraction with fines, community service or both.

sec02-card-sec02-R03.front: How many months on Level one are required before Segment two versus before the skills test and Level two?
sec02-card-sec02-R03.expected_back: Segment two requires three consecutive months on the Level one license, while the skills test and Level two each require at least six months on Level one.

sec02-card-sec02-R06.front: How does the clock for Level two's driving curfew differ from the clock for its young-passenger cap?
sec02-card-sec02-R06.expected_back: The Level two night limit runs from ten p.m. to five a.m., while the passenger limit applies at any hour and allows only one passenger under twenty-one.

sec02-card-sec02-R07.front: Does carrying immediate family members excuse a Level two driver from the ten p.m. to five a.m. night limit?
sec02-card-sec02-R07.expected_back: Immediate family passengers are an exception to the Level two passenger limit, but they are not listed as an exception to the night driving limit.

sec02-card-sec02-R09.front: How does advancing to Level two differ between hard-card teens and paper-card teens?
sec02-card-sec02-R09.expected_back: Hard-card teens advance to Level two automatically, while paper-card teens must bring their documents to a Secretary of State office.

sec02-card-sec02-F22.front: What age, Level two time, and clean-driving window are required for a Level three Full License?
sec02-card-sec02-F22.expected_back: The Level three Full License requires age seventeen, at least six months on Level two, and twelve consecutive months with no moving violation, at-fault crash, suspension or GDL restriction violation.

sec02-card-sec02-F23.front: How is a Level three license issued and priced, what state limits remain, and can parents hold it back?
sec02-card-sec02-F23.expected_back: Level three is issued automatically and free once the requirements are met with parental authorization, carries no state restrictions, and may be delayed at a parent’s or guardian’s request.

sec02-card-sec02-R04.front: How does the clean-record window for entering Level two compare with the clean-record and holding rules for Level three?
sec02-card-sec02-R04.expected_back: Applying for GDL Level two requires ninety days free of violations, at-fault crashes, and suspensions, whereas GDL Level three requires holding Level two at least six months and driving twelve consecutive months without a moving violation, at-fault crash, suspension, or GDL restriction violation.

sec02-card-sec02-R05.front: What are the minimum ages for the driving skills test, Level two, and Level three?
sec02-card-sec02-R05.expected_back: The minimum ages climb by level: fifteen for the skills test, sixteen for Level two, and seventeen for Level three.

sec02-card-sec02-F24.front: What two major steps must a never-licensed applicant aged eighteen or older complete to earn a Michigan license?
sec02-card-sec02-F24.expected_back: Anyone eighteen or older who has never been licensed must apply for a temporary instruction permit at a Secretary of State office and pass a skills test given by a driver testing business.

sec02-card-sec02-F25.front: Which four document proofs must first-time adult applicants bring, and how can they shorten their counter visit?
sec02-card-sec02-F25.expected_back: Adult first-time applicants bring four proofs, covering identity, Michigan residency, U.S. citizenship or legal presence, and a valid Social Security number, and pre-applying at Michigan.gov slash SOS speeds up the visit.

sec02-card-sec02-F26.front: How much does the written knowledge test cost at a Secretary of State office versus online from home?
sec02-card-sec02-F26.expected_back: The written knowledge test is free at every Secretary of State office, or you can take an online version at home for a six dollars and fifty cents convenience fee.

sec02-card-sec02-F27.front: Which three steps must an adult finish before the temporary instruction permit is issued?
sec02-card-sec02-F27.expected_back: Your TIP is issued after three steps: passing the written knowledge and vision tests, paying the TIP fee, and having your photo taken.

sec02-card-sec02-F28.front: How long must an adult practice with a licensed adult before the skills test, and when does the license arrive afterward?
sec02-card-sec02-F28.expected_back: You must practice with a licensed adult for at least thirty days before the skills test, and after you pass, the license should arrive by mail in about three weeks.

sec02-card-sec02-R11.front: How does an adult TIP holder's pre-test practice requirement differ in measurement from a GDL teen's requirement?
sec02-card-sec02-R11.expected_back: Adults must practice at least thirty days on a TIP before the skills test, a count of days, whereas the teen log counts supervised hours.

sec02-card-sec02-R13.front: When do you pay the six-dollar-and-fifty-cent fee on Michigan's written knowledge test?
sec02-card-sec02-R13.expected_back: The written knowledge test costs nothing at an office, and only the optional online version at home carries the six dollars and fifty cents convenience fee.

sec02-card-sec02-F29.front: For what two statutory purposes does the Secretary of State collect Social Security numbers?
sec02-card-sec02-F29.expected_back: The Secretary of State collects Social Security numbers under state and federal law to verify citizenship or legal presence and to help with child support collection.

sec02-card-sec02-F30.front: What document must an applicant without a Social Security number present, and how recent must it be?
sec02-card-sec02-F30.expected_back: If you have no Social Security number, you must present an ineligibility letter from the Social Security Administration that is no more than sixty days old.

sec02-card-sec02-F31.front: Which official documents are accepted to prove United States citizenship or legal presence?
sec02-card-sec02-F31.expected_back: Accepted proof of legal presence includes a certified birth certificate with a raised seal from a U.S. government unit or territory, a valid unexpired U.S. passport, a citizenship or naturalization certificate, a Permanent Resident Card, or an Employment Authorization Card.

sec02-card-sec02-F32.front: What personal details must match across your application documents, and how do you bridge any name change?
sec02-card-sec02-F32.expected_back: Your first and last names and birth date should match across documents, and every name change needs legal proof such as an original marriage license, divorce decree or court order.

sec02-card-sec02-F33.front: What rule governs copies or faxes for identity proof, and might one document not be enough?
sec02-card-sec02-F33.expected_back: Identity proof must be original documents, photocopies and faxes are refused, and you may need more than one document.

sec02-card-sec02-F34.front: How long after expiration can an out-of-state or Canadian driver's license still count as identity proof?
sec02-card-sec02-F34.expected_back: Out-of-state and Canadian applicants may use their own license as identity proof as long as it has been expired for less than four years.

sec02-card-sec02-F35.front: How many residency documents are required, and what date limit applies to utility, credit, or bank statements?
sec02-card-sec02-F35.expected_back: Residency proof takes at least two documents, such as a utility bill, credit card bill or account statement from the last ninety days, a pay stub, an earnings statement, a mortgage or lease, or an insurance policy.
