sec07-card-sec07-F03.question_text: What warning do flashing yellow overhead lights on a school bus send?
sec07-card-sec07-F03.teaching_text: Speeding up to beat overhead yellow flashers risks catching red lights just as students step toward the curb.

sec07-card-sec07-F04.question_text: How far back must you stop when a school bus flashes red overhead lights, and when may you roll again?
sec07-card-sec07-F04.teaching_text: Holding at least twenty feet away creates a safe crossing buffer until the red flashers shut off or the bus leaves.

sec07-card-sec07-R01.question_text: How do yellow hazard lights, yellow overhead lights, and red overhead lights on a school bus differ in meaning?
sec07-card-sec07-R01.teaching_text: Keep hazard flashers separate from roof-mounted warning lights so you know caution from stopping twenty feet back.

sec07-card-sec07-F05.question_text: When making a right turn — including turning right at a red light — what duty do you owe other vehicles?
sec07-card-sec07-F05.teaching_text: Even after halting at a red bulb, pulling into cross traffic without yielding causes right-angle collisions.

sec07-card-sec07-F06.question_text: Whether exiting a driveway or alley or finishing at a green light, what rule governs turning left across traffic?
sec07-card-sec07-F06.teaching_text: Crossing opposing lanes from an alley, driveway, or green-light intersection always puts the burden of yielding on you.

sec07-card-sec07-F07.question_text: When a left turn on a red light is legal, what right-of-way duty applies toward other vehicles?
sec07-card-sec07-F07.teaching_text: Turning against a red signal never grants priority over cross-street or turning vehicles already holding the lane.

sec07-card-sec07-F08.question_text: Before turning left on red from one one-way street onto another one-way street, what stop and scan must you make?
sec07-card-sec07-F08.teaching_text: Since the target one-way street flows right-to-left across your bow, oncoming gaps arrive exclusively from your right.

sec07-card-sec07-F09.question_text: In Michigan, what three steps are required to turn left on red from a two-way street onto a one-way street?
sec07-card-sec07-F09.teaching_text: Besides cross traffic from the right, opposing drivers turning right onto that same one-way street hold priority.

sec07-card-sec07-F10.question_text: Right after your traffic signal turns green, whom must you let go before pulling into the intersection?
sec07-card-sec07-F10.teaching_text: Launching blindly on green risks T-boning drivers who entered legally on yellow and are still clearing the box.

sec07-card-sec07-F11.question_text: When may you turn left on a green ball, and what should you do if the signal turns red while you are already in the intersection?
sec07-card-sec07-F11.teaching_text: Once oncoming cars clear — or if red catches you mid-box — complete your turn promptly and safely instead of reversing.

sec07-card-sec07-R05.question_text: Which two traffic streams still outrank you even when your signal is green?
sec07-card-sec07-R05.teaching_text: Written tests punish assuming green means automatic priority over lingering cross traffic or straight-through oncoming cars.

sec07-card-sec07-F12.question_text: How must you handle a stop sign or flashing red signal, and what three stopping-point options apply?
sec07-card-sec07-F12.teaching_text: Use the painted line or crosswalk first, or stop before entering the intersection where cross traffic becomes visible.

sec07-card-sec07-F13.question_text: Who goes first at a four-way stop, and how is a simultaneous arrival tie broken?
sec07-card-sec07-F13.teaching_text: Arrival order sets priority first, and only when two cars halt together does the left driver yield right.

sec07-card-sec07-F14.question_text: What three rules govern an intersection when its traffic signal is malfunctioning?
sec07-card-sec07-F14.teaching_text: Treat a broken traffic light like an all-way stop by halting, letting earlier arrivals clear, and yielding right on ties.

sec07-card-sec07-F15.question_text: What must you do before completing a turn at a flashing yellow arrow?
sec07-card-sec07-F15.teaching_text: Unlike a solid green arrow, a flashing yellow arrow warns that oncoming traffic still has a green light.

sec07-card-sec07-F16.question_text: At a T-intersection with no signs or signals, which road holds the right of way?
sec07-card-sec07-F16.teaching_text: Because the terminating street ends at the junction, drivers on the continuous through road hold right of way.

sec07-card-sec07-F17.question_text: What three actions should you take as you approach a YIELD sign?
sec07-card-sec07-F17.teaching_text: Easing off the pedal early lets you scan intersecting lanes and brake smoothly if a safe gap disappears.

sec07-card-sec07-R02.question_text: At a four-way stop, why doesn't the car on the right always go first?
sec07-card-sec07-R02.teaching_text: Whoever arrives and stops first wins outright, reserving the yield-to-the-right rule strictly for tied arrivals.

sec07-card-sec07-R03.question_text: Which everyday intersection control matches how you handle a malfunctioning traffic signal?
sec07-card-sec07-R03.teaching_text: Failing to halt at a blacked-out or glitching light risks high-speed broadside crashes from perpendicular lanes.

sec07-card-sec07-R04.question_text: How does your stopping requirement differ between a flashing yellow arrow and a flashing red signal?
sec07-card-sec07-R04.teaching_text: Stopping unnecessarily on a clear flashing yellow arrow surprises drivers behind you, while rolling a flashing red breaks stop law.

sec07-card-sec07-R06.question_text: Which driver must yield at an unsigned T-intersection?
sec07-card-sec07-R06.teaching_text: Even if you approach from the right on the dead-end stem, continuous through-road traffic takes precedence.

sec07-card-sec07-F18.question_text: Around construction zones and stopped service trucks with flashing lights, whom must you be ready to yield to?
sec07-card-sec07-F18.teaching_text: Crews around garbage, utility, or road-maintenance trucks step out unpredictably near live traffic lanes.

sec07-card-sec07-F19.question_text: Where and how must you stop when an emergency vehicle approaches running red or blue lights and a siren?
sec07-card-sec07-F19.teaching_text: Stopping inside an intersection blocks turning fire rigs, so pull to the right edge clear of corners until waved on or passed.

sec07-card-sec07-F20.question_text: What two adjustments let you blend safely into traffic at a MERGE sign?
sec07-card-sec07-F20.teaching_text: Matching pace while yielding to vehicles already in the travel lane prevents abrupt braking on ramps.

sec07-card-sec07-F27.question_text: Which three emergency vehicles are the only ones that outrank a Michigan funeral procession?
sec07-card-sec07-F27.teaching_text: Every ordinary motorist yields to a flagged funeral procession, leaving only fire, ambulance, and police units ahead of it.

sec07-card-sec07-F28.question_text: What color flag and symbol design must vehicles in a Michigan funeral procession display?
sec07-card-sec07-F28.teaching_text: Look for bright fluorescent orange flags carrying a cross, star of David, or crescent and star marking the line.

sec07-card-sec07-F29.question_text: What penalty hits if you cut through a funeral procession, and are oncoming drivers required to pull over?
sec07-card-sec07-F29.teaching_text: Slicing between flagged procession cars draws a civil infraction ticket, though meeting one never legally forces pulling over.

sec07-card-sec07-R10.question_text: Put Michigan's funeral procession rules together — whom do they yield to, what is forbidden, and what is optional?
sec07-card-sec07-R10.teaching_text: Test distractors often claim you must pull to the curb, when the law actually forbids cutting through the line.

sec07-card-sec07-F21.question_text: Does a green traffic light excuse you from yielding to a pedestrian in an intersection or midblock marked crosswalk?
sec07-card-sec07-F21.teaching_text: Whether painted at a corner or midblock, a marked crosswalk obligates you to yield even under a green bulb.

sec07-card-sec07-F22.question_text: Which two vulnerable pedestrian groups get explicit right-of-way protection in Michigan?
sec07-card-sec07-F22.teaching_text: Slow early near active school-zone crosswalks and give extra time to walkers with sight, hearing, or mobility impairments.

sec07-card-sec07-F23.question_text: At intersections with or without traffic lights, what rule applies toward pedestrians whenever you turn?
sec07-card-sec07-F23.teaching_text: Drivers scanning vehicle gaps during turns often overlook pedestrians stepping off the corner right beside them.

sec07-card-sec07-F24.question_text: At stop signs, flashing red lights, and flashing yellow intersections, what duty applies toward pedestrians?
sec07-card-sec07-F24.teaching_text: Flashing yellow cautions and red stop controls alike require letting crossing pedestrians clear your path.

sec07-card-sec07-F25.question_text: Where no traffic signals or signs exist, when does a pedestrian in an unmarked crosswalk hold the right of way?
sec07-card-sec07-F25.teaching_text: Even without white paint at an uncontrolled corner, a walker on your half of the street owns priority.

sec07-card-sec07-F26.question_text: Which pedestrians keep the right of way after a signal changes — or when you emerge from an alley, driveway, building, or private road?
sec07-card-sec07-F26.teaching_text: Anyone who entered before the light changed or crosses in front of a driveway or alley entrance comes first.

sec07-card-sec07-R11.question_text: If your signal turns green while a pedestrian is still walking across the crosswalk, who yields?
sec07-card-sec07-R11.teaching_text: Honking or creeping at someone finishing their crossing violates pedestrian right-of-way law despite your green light.

sec07-card-sec07-F30.question_text: What sightline and oncoming-traffic gap are required before passing on a two-lane highway?
sec07-card-sec07-F30.teaching_text: Misjudging closing speed on two-lane highways leaves nowhere to go if oncoming headlights close the gap.

sec07-card-sec07-F31.question_text: What visual check in your mirror tells you it is safe to merge back right after passing a vehicle?
sec07-card-sec07-F31.teaching_text: Cutting back before both headlights of the passed car fill your center mirror risks clipping their front bumper.

sec07-card-sec07-F32.question_text: When passing on a two-lane road, how far away from an oncoming vehicle must you already be back in your lane?
sec07-card-sec07-F32.teaching_text: Two cars approaching at highway speed cover two hundred feet in roughly a second, leaving zero margin closer.

sec07-card-sec07-F33.question_text: What three passing precautions apply to towing trailers, passing multiple cars, and following another passer?
sec07-card-sec07-F33.teaching_text: Leapfrogging one car at a time without tailgating another passer ensures you always have a gap back right.

sec07-card-sec07-F34.question_text: Why does passing in a three-lane road's center lane demand extreme care, and when is passing or merging there completely banned?
sec07-card-sec07-F34.teaching_text: Opposing traffic can enter an unmarked third lane head-on, and left-turn-only markings forbid passing or merging altogether.

sec07-card-sec07-F35.question_text: How must you respond when another driver is overtaking and passing your vehicle?
sec07-card-sec07-F35.teaching_text: Accelerating alongside a passing driver traps them in the oncoming lane and invites a multi-car head-on crash.

sec07-card-sec07-F36.question_text: Even when passing on the right is otherwise allowed, what surface may you never use to do it?
sec07-card-sec07-F36.teaching_text: Dropping wheels onto gravel or paved shoulders to squeeze past right kicks up debris and hits stopped cars.

sec07-card-sec07-F37.question_text: List the four roadway or traffic situations where Michigan allows passing on the right?
sec07-card-sec07-F37.teaching_text: Paved width around a left-turning car, multi-lane one-way or two-way roads, or widened passing lanes make right passes legal.

sec07-card-sec07-R08.question_text: What separates a legal pass on the right from an illegal one?
sec07-card-sec07-R08.teaching_text: Having paved lane space makes the listed cases lawful, whereas leaving the main roadway or riding the shoulder breaks the law.

sec07-card-sec07-F38.question_text: Which center-line marking, roadside signs, and terrain features ban passing?
sec07-card-sec07-F38.teaching_text: Solid yellow on your side, posted no-passing signs, or blind hills and curves all hide deadly oncoming traffic.

sec07-card-sec07-F39.question_text: Within one hundred feet of which junctions, crossings, or view-blocking structures is passing illegal?
sec07-card-sec07-F39.teaching_text: Pulling left near intersections, tracks, or view-blocking bridges, viaducts, and tunnels leaves zero reaction room.

sec07-card-sec07-F40.question_text: What oncoming-traffic, visibility, or three-lane marking conditions make passing illegal?
sec07-card-sec07-F40.teaching_text: Fog, glare, close headlights, or a center left-turn-only lane each eliminate safe passing space.

sec07-card-sec07-F41.question_text: Around crosswalks, construction zones, and school buses, which three situations strictly forbid passing?
sec07-card-sec07-F41.teaching_text: Whipping around a car stopped at a crosswalk or a red-flashing school bus strikes hidden pedestrians mid-stride.

sec07-card-sec07-R07.question_text: Keep Michigan's two passing numbers straight — what requires two hundred feet and what requires one hundred feet?
sec07-card-sec07-R07.teaching_text: Exam questions love swapping the two-hundred-foot oncoming return buffer with the one-hundred-foot intersection and rail ban.

sec07-card-sec07-R09.question_text: When does the center lane of a three-lane road flip from cautious passing to a total passing and merging ban?
sec07-card-sec07-R09.teaching_text: Once pavement arrows or signs dedicate that middle lane to left turns only, using it to pass or merge is illegal.

sec11-card-sec11-F01.question_text: What do solid white fog lines mark, and is crossing them to pass ever legal?
sec11-card-sec11-F01.teaching_text: Fog lines keep tires on asphalt in storms or glare, and using the shoulder to pass is illegal.

sec11-card-sec11-F02.question_text: Where do single solid white lines separate same-direction lanes, and how should you treat them?
sec11-card-sec11-F02.teaching_text: Sharp bends and freeway acceleration or deceleration ramps paint solid white stripes to discourage dangerous last-second lane swaps.

sec11-card-sec11-F03.question_text: What does a double solid white line divide, and what is the rule on crossing it?
sec11-card-sec11-F03.teaching_text: Whereas single solid white strongly discourages lane shifts, parallel double white stripes forbid crossing between same-way paths.

sec11-card-sec11-F04.question_text: In what two painted patterns—and at what street locations—do white crosswalk markings appear?
sec11-card-sec11-F04.teaching_text: Watching for both transverse border lines and ladder-style stripes spots walker zones at corners and midblock crossings.

sec11-card-sec11-F05.question_text: Where must your front bumper stop relative to a painted crosswalk line?
sec11-card-sec11-F05.teaching_text: Rolling onto crosswalk paint forces walking families and wheelchair users out toward live cross traffic.

sec11-card-sec11-F06.question_text: What is an intersection stop line, and whom does stopping behind it protect?
sec11-card-sec11-F06.teaching_text: Halting behind that thick white bar keeps your hood clear of both crossing pedestrians and turning cross traffic.

sec11-card-sec11-F07.question_text: Where must you stop when an intersection has neither a stop line nor a painted crosswalk?
sec11-card-sec11-F07.teaching_text: Stop short of the intersecting roadway first, then verify clear views in every direction before pulling out.

sec11-card-sec11-F08.question_text: What do wide white pavement arrows govern across multi-lane approaches?
sec11-card-sec11-F08.teaching_text: Turning right from an unarrowed inner lane cuts straight across outer lanes permitted to continue straight.

sec11-card-sec11-F09.question_text: Which road users are allowed to travel inside a marked and signed bicycle lane?
sec11-card-sec11-F09.teaching_text: Motor vehicles treating bike lanes as extra right-turn pockets or shoulders crowd unprotected riders.

sec11-card-sec11-F10.question_text: What does bright green pavement paint inside a bicycle lane warn drivers to watch for?
sec11-card-sec11-F10.teaching_text: Intersections and busy driveways use green blocks where turning cars cross straight-riding cyclists.

sec11-card-sec11-F11.question_text: Which six motor-vehicle actions—moving or stopped—are illegal inside a Michigan bike lane?
sec11-card-sec11-F11.teaching_text: Even brief delivery stops, waiting pull-overs, right turns, or passes force cyclists abruptly into fast traffic.

sec11-card-sec11-F12.question_text: What do shared-lane pavement markings indicate, and how must motorists respond around them?
sec11-card-sec11-F12.teaching_text: Sharrows guide bike positioning on streets without separate bike lanes, reminding drivers cyclists hold full legal rights.

sec11-card-sec11-F13.question_text: What traffic relationship do yellow lines mark, and what three styles appear on Michigan roads?
sec11-card-sec11-F13.teaching_text: Seeing yellow paint beside your left door always warns oncoming traffic travels on the other side.

sec11-card-sec11-F14.question_text: What passing rule applies along a two-way road marked with a single broken yellow centerline?
sec11-card-sec11-F14.teaching_text: Dashed yellow paint permits overtaking only after you confirm plenty of clear sightline and opposing space.

sec11-card-sec11-F15.question_text: May you cross the centerline to pass when a solid yellow stripe sits on your side?
sec11-card-sec11-F15.teaching_text: Engineers paint solid yellow on your side wherever curves or crests hide approaching headlights.

sec11-card-sec11-F16.question_text: Which stripe color marks the left pavement edge on a four-lane divided highway or one-way street?
sec11-card-sec11-F16.teaching_text: Keeping yellow on your left and white on your right instantly confirms you are traveling the right direction.

sec11-card-sec11-F17.question_text: What does a double solid yellow centerline forbid—and for which turns may you legally cross it?
sec11-card-sec11-F17.teaching_text: Double yellow bars overtaking both ways yet still allows turning across into driveways, crossroads, or parking spots.

sec11-card-sec11-F18.question_text: How are the outer and inner yellow stripes arranged on a shared center left-turn lane?
sec11-card-sec11-F18.teaching_text: Both travel directions may enter that middle lane solely to slow and complete left turns.

sec11-card-sec11-F19.question_text: Why is using a center left-turn-only lane to pass slower traffic or merge onto a road illegal?
sec11-card-sec11-F19.teaching_text: Drivers from both directions enter that middle strip simultaneously, turning through cruising into head-on traps.

sec11-card-sec11-R16.question_text: Can you combine the exact stripe pattern of a center turn lane with what maneuvers it allows versus bans?
sec11-card-sec11-R16.teaching_text: Memorize solid outer, broken inner, left turns both ways, and zero passing or merging for test day.

sec11-card-sec11-R17.question_text: How do broken yellow, solid-on-your-side yellow, and double solid yellow compare for passing?
sec11-card-sec11-R17.teaching_text: Wait—check whichever stripe sits closest to your left tires before pulling out to overtake.
sec11-card-sec11-R17.must_match_memory_hook: Broken yes, solid yours, double both

visual_sync.text_span: Broken yes, solid yours, double both

sec11-card-sec11-R18.question_text: What core traffic separation stays true across solid, broken, and center-lane yellow markings alike?
sec11-card-sec11-R18.teaching_text: Whether single, double, or framing a turn lane, yellow always warns opposing traffic uses the far side.

sec11-card-sec11-F20.question_text: How does an indirect Michigan Left replace a direct left turn on divided boulevards?
sec11-card-sec11-F20.teaching_text: Used across Michigan since the late nineteen sixties, routing turns through median crossovers cuts intersection T-bone crashes.

sec11-card-sec11-F21.question_text: How many cars turn at once in a single-lane Michigan Left crossover, and why is the pavement built so wide?
sec11-card-sec11-F21.teaching_text: Crowding side-by-side in an extra-wide single crossover risks getting crushed by swinging tractor-trailers or campers.

sec11-card-sec11-F22.question_text: Which three markings allow two vehicles to turn side by side in a Michigan Left—and how do you treat unmarked ones?
sec11-card-sec11-F22.teaching_text: Unless pavement arrows, ONLY stencils, and solid white lane dividers appear together, always queue single file.

sec11-card-sec11-F23.question_text: Starting on the main divided highway, what step-by-step path completes a Michigan Left onto the cross street?
sec11-card-sec11-F23.teaching_text: Driving past the cross street first lets you U-turn cleanly at the median and turn right from the curb lane.

sec11-card-sec11-F24.question_text: Starting on a side road, how do you execute a Michigan Left onto the divided highway?
sec11-card-sec11-F24.teaching_text: Turning right first blends with one direction of traffic before weaving left to the median U-turn.

sec11-card-sec11-R19.question_text: Why must you never pull alongside another car inside an unpainted Michigan Left crossover that looks two cars wide?
sec11-card-sec11-R19.teaching_text: That generous asphalt width accommodates long semi-truck wheelbases rather than two side-by-side passenger cars.

sec11-card-sec11-F25.question_text: At which two roadway features do painted yield lines appear, and where do you stop when yielding?
sec11-card-sec11-F25.teaching_text: Stopping short of the shark-tooth line keeps your bumper out of circulating roundabout lanes and pedestrian paths.

sec11-card-sec11-F26.question_text: What does a row of white triangles painted across your travel lane tell you to do?
sec11-card-sec11-F26.teaching_text: Shark-tooth yield triangles sit upstream from crosswalks so stopped cars leave clear sightlines for adjacent lanes.

sec11-card-sec11-F27.question_text: What boundary do dashed white lines painted across a roundabout approach lane mark?
sec11-card-sec11-F27.teaching_text: Waiting behind those entry dashes keeps your front fender clear of vehicles already circling inside.

sec11-card-sec11-F28.question_text: Is cutting across a gas station or store parking lot to skip a red light legal in Michigan?
sec11-card-sec11-F28.teaching_text: Speeding diagonally across public or private parking aisles ambushes backing shoppers and pedestrians to dodge a light.

sec11-card-sec11-R20.question_text: How do painted white triangles across a lane differ in meaning from dashed white lines at a roundabout?
sec11-card-sec11-R20.teaching_text: Pointed shark teeth mark pedestrian yield points, whereas rectangular white dashes trace the circulatory roadway boundary.

sec11-card-sec11-F29.question_text: Where does the red lens sit on standard vertical Michigan signals, and where must you stop?
sec11-card-sec11-F29.teaching_text: Consistent top placement lets color-blind drivers read red reliably while keeping bumpers clear of crosswalks.

sec11-card-sec11-F30.question_text: What does a steady yellow traffic light require in Michigan—and what if stopping safely is impossible?
sec11-card-sec11-F30.teaching_text: Michigan treats yellow as a required stop whenever safe, forbidding gas-pedal sprints if you must roll cautiously clear.

sec11-card-sec11-F31.question_text: Before accelerating on a fresh green light, what must you verify inside the intersection?
sec11-card-sec11-F31.teaching_text: Late red-light runners and slow pedestrians may still occupy the box right after your lens turns green.

sec11-card-sec11-F32.question_text: How must drivers handle a completely dark, non-working traffic light when no officer directs the corner?
sec11-card-sec11-F32.teaching_text: Treating power-outage intersections like all-way stops prevents high-speed broadsides when drivers assume mainline priority.

sec11-card-sec11-R02.question_text: At a steady red light, what must follow your complete stop before moving on green or turning right on red?
sec11-card-sec11-R02.teaching_text: Stopping is only half the rule—scanning curbs and cross lanes prevents clipping walkers or fast crossers.

sec11-card-sec11-R03.question_text: How do you treat an overhead flashing red traffic light?
sec11-card-sec11-R03.teaching_text: A flashing red lens acts identically to a stop sign—never roll through without halting completely.

sec11-card-sec11-R04.question_text: What does an overhead flashing yellow intersection beacon instruct you to do?
sec11-card-sec11-R04.teaching_text: Cross-street drivers usually face flashing red, yet careless pull-outs still demand alert scanning both directions.

sec11-card-sec11-R15.question_text: How does a steady yellow light on a doghouse signal differ from a flashing yellow intersection beacon?
sec11-card-sec11-R15.teaching_text: Steady yellow announces an imminent red stop, whereas flashing yellow warns mainline traffic to roll through alertly.

sec11-card-sec11-F33.question_text: Which five signal lenses make up a cluster-style doghouse turn signal?
sec11-card-sec11-F33.teaching_text: Pairing standard red, yellow, and green balls with dedicated yellow and green arrows manages shared turn phases.

sec11-card-sec11-F34.question_text: On a doghouse signal, how does turning on a lit green arrow differ from turning on a plain green ball?
sec11-card-sec11-F34.teaching_text: A green arrow halts opposing lanes for a protected turn, while a plain green ball demands yielding first.

sec11-card-sec11-R01.question_text: How should you respond to a yellow ball or yellow arrow on a doghouse signal depending on your position?
sec11-card-sec11-R01.teaching_text: Approaching drivers stop for incoming red, while drivers already waiting inside complete their turn once oncoming clears.

sec11-card-sec11-R05.question_text: Even though oncoming cars are stopped during a steady green arrow, whom must turning drivers still yield to?
sec11-card-sec11-R05.teaching_text: Protected turn phases stop opposing bumpers yet can still overlap pedestrians finishing their crossing.

sec11-card-sec11-R06.question_text: How many lenses build Michigan's flashing-yellow-arrow left-turn head, and why did federal studies back it?
sec11-card-sec11-R06.teaching_text: Replacing ambiguous green balls with flashing yellow arrows cuts permissive left-turn misjudgments and keeps intersections moving.

sec11-card-sec11-R07.question_text: May you turn after stopping at a solid red arrow?
sec11-card-sec11-R07.teaching_text: Unlike a circular red light where turns on red may apply, a solid red arrow bars turning completely.

sec11-card-sec11-R08.question_text: What transition does a solid yellow left-turn arrow announce for approaching versus waiting cars?
sec11-card-sec11-R08.teaching_text: Stop short if still approaching, or finish turning cleanly if already positioned inside without conflicting traffic.

sec11-card-sec11-R09.question_text: Why must you yield before turning left on a flashing yellow arrow, and what three groups do you check?
sec11-card-sec11-R09.teaching_text: Opposing lanes hold a full green light, so wait for a safe gap free of cars, bikes, and walkers.

sec11-card-sec11-R10.question_text: What does a solid green arrow grant on a four-lens head, and why might the signal skip that phase?
sec11-card-sec11-R10.teaching_text: Camera or pavement sensors skip the protected left arrow when nobody waits in the pocket, keeping cross-street flow brisk.

sec11-card-sec11-R11.question_text: What do pedestrian signal heads regulate, and what extra timer feature do many include?
sec11-card-sec11-R11.teaching_text: Visual numbers and audible tones tell walkers whether enough clearance time remains before cross traffic starts.

sec11-card-sec11-R12.question_text: What does a steady WALK or walking-person symbol mean, and what changes once it starts flashing?
sec11-card-sec11-R12.teaching_text: Drivers must yield throughout, while walkers already in the street finish crossing as the countdown flashes.

sec11-card-sec11-R13.question_text: What does DONT WALK or a red raised hand tell pedestrians—and what duty remains on drivers?
sec11-card-sec11-R13.teaching_text: Even if someone steps out late against a raised hand, motorists must always yield rather than strike a pedestrian.

sec11-card-sec11-R14.question_text: What is a Pedestrian Hybrid Beacon designed to do, and how many steps make up its sequence?
sec11-card-sec11-R14.teaching_text: Midblock HAWK-style beacons stay dark until triggered, stepping through six phases to halt drivers for walkers.

sec09-card-sec09-F01.question_text: If a railroad crossing posts an octagon stop sign and zero trains are visible, what must you still do?
sec09-card-sec09-F01.teaching_text: Treating a trackside stop sign like a yield sign gets drivers ticketed and blindsided by quiet fast trains.

sec09-card-sec09-F02.question_text: Unless posted signs say otherwise, which four vehicle categories must stop and check for trains even without a stop sign or signal?
sec09-card-sec09-F02.teaching_text: Expect heavy tankers, hazmat haulers, school buses, and passenger-for-hire rigs to brake to a halt ahead of unguarded tracks.

sec09-card-sec09-F03.question_text: What makes a railroad crossing passive, and which static warnings mark it instead?
sec09-card-sec09-F03.teaching_text: Without gates or flashers to alert you, advance signs, road markings, crossbucks, and yield or stop signs carry the whole warning.

sec09-card-sec09-F04.question_text: What five habits keep you alive when crossing a passive railroad crossing?
sec09-card-sec09-F04.teaching_text: Scanning both ways and verifying every parallel track is clear beats trying to outrun a locomotive.

sec09-card-sec09-F05.question_text: Which four automated warning devices can an active railroad crossing combine to announce an approaching train?
sec09-card-sec09-F05.teaching_text: Active crossings trigger automated motion, light, message, or sound warnings whenever track sensors detect an approaching train.

sec09-card-sec09-R07.question_text: What is the core difference between a passive railroad crossing and an active railroad crossing?
sec09-card-sec09-R07.teaching_text: Knowing whether a crossing activates lights and gates or relies strictly on fixed signs sets how hard you must look.

sec09-card-sec09-F06.question_text: Which active crossing triggers require an immediate stop, and what gate-dodging moves are strictly forbidden?
sec09-card-sec09-F06.teaching_text: Weaving around, under, or through a moving or lowered gate gambles your life against a fast-closing train.

sec09-card-sec09-F07.question_text: Once the caboose or last railcar clears a crossing, what three conditions must be met before you pull forward?
sec09-card-sec09-F07.teaching_text: A second train traveling the opposite direction on an adjacent track can hide right behind the departing cars.

sec09-card-sec09-F08.question_text: Along with expecting a train, looking both ways, and never stopping on rails, what transmission habit should you avoid while crossing?
sec09-card-sec09-F08.teaching_text: Missing a manual shift midway across steel rails can stall your engine right inside the danger zone.

sec09-card-sec09-F09.question_text: How should you adjust your speed when crossing railroad tracks on a snow-covered road?
sec09-card-sec09-F09.teaching_text: Creeping too slowly over raised snowy rails lets your drive tires spin out and bog down on the crossing.

sec09-card-sec09-F10.question_text: When traffic ahead is backed up beyond a railroad crossing, how much clearance past the far rail must fit your vehicle before you start across?
sec09-card-sec09-F10.teaching_text: Starting across without room to clear the far rail by six feet traps your rear bumper inside train overhang.

sec09-card-sec09-F11.question_text: Roughly how many seconds pass between crossing lights, gates, or a train horn activating and the train reaching the crossing?
sec09-card-sec09-F11.teaching_text: Twenty seconds vanishes almost instantly if a car hesitates or stalls while trying to beat lowering gates.

sec09-card-sec09-R08.question_text: Pair Michigan's far-side track clearance distance with the warning countdown once crossing signals activate?
sec09-card-sec09-R08.teaching_text: Having only twenty seconds once bells start is exactly why you never enter without six feet of far-side room.

sec09-card-sec09-F12.question_text: If your vehicle stalls on the tracks while gates are active or a train is visibly approaching, what two steps come in exact order?
sec09-card-sec09-F12.teaching_text: Never waste seconds cranking the starter or phoning inside the car before getting every passenger far from the rails.

sec09-card-sec09-F13.question_text: If your car gets stuck on tracks with zero train in sight and inactive signals, whom do you call after evacuating everyone?
sec09-card-sec09-F13.teaching_text: Phoning the railroad number on the blue Emergency Notification Sign with the crossing ID alerts dispatchers to halt trains.

sec09-card-sec09-F14.question_text: What character pattern makes up the crossing ID on the blue sign, how can railroad officials respond, and whom do you call next?
sec09-card-sec09-F14.teaching_text: That six-digit, one-letter code pinpoints your exact crossing so rail dispatchers can slow, stop, or reroute trains before you call nine-one-one.

sec09-card-sec09-F15.question_text: What two pieces of information appear on a grade crossing's Emergency Notification System sign, and what two problems do they report?
sec09-card-sec09-F15.teaching_text: Every crossing posts a direct phone line and its US DOT number for reporting track emergencies or broken warning gear.

sec09-card-sec09-R06.question_text: After evacuating a stalled car on the tracks, what decides whether your very first phone call goes to nine-one-one or to the blue railroad sign number?
sec09-card-sec09-R06.teaching_text: Active gates or an approaching train demand immediate nine-one-one response, whereas silent clear tracks give railroad dispatchers time to stop trains.

sec09-card-sec09-F16.question_text: What four actions must you complete every single time you park and leave a vehicle?
sec09-card-sec09-F16.teaching_text: Relying on the transmission pawl alone without setting the parking brake or pulling keys invites rollaways and theft.

sec09-card-sec09-F17.question_text: Before swinging open a street-side vehicle door, what mirror check and approaching traffic must you look for?
sec09-card-sec09-F17.teaching_text: Flinging a car door open into a bike lane or travel lane causes severe dooring crashes with cyclists and motorcyclists.

sec09-card-sec09-F18.question_text: Why does reaching across with your right hand to open the driver's door improve safety?
sec09-card-sec09-F18.teaching_text: Reaching with your far hand naturally pivots your torso so your eyes sweep over your left shoulder for cyclists.

sec09-card-sec09-F19.question_text: When walking along the street back to your parked car's driver door, which direction should you face?
sec09-card-sec09-F19.teaching_text: Keeping approaching cars in front of your eyes lets you step clear if a distracted driver drifts close.

sec09-card-sec09-F20.question_text: Which way must you turn your front wheels when parking downhill with a curb, uphill with a curb, and on a hill with no curb?
sec09-card-sec09-F20.teaching_text: Angling tires properly lets the curb chock a rolling car — or steers curbless rollaways off the travel lane.

sec09-card-sec09-F21.question_text: Why must you always set the parking brake on a hill instead of relying on the transmission?
sec09-card-sec09-F21.teaching_text: Gravity on a steep grade stresses internal transmission gears that were never engineered to hold stationary vehicle weight.

sec09-card-sec09-R04.question_text: Contrast your front-wheel direction when parked downhill against a curb versus uphill against a curb?
sec09-card-sec09-R04.teaching_text: Uphill-away lets the back of the front tire catch the curb if the car rolls backward.

sec09-card-sec09-F22.question_text: After signaling and checking mirrors for a passenger-side parallel spot, where and at what side-by-side gap do you line up?
sec09-card-sec09-F22.teaching_text: Pulling even with the forward car two to five feet out gives your rear bumper clean swing clearance.

sec09-card-sec09-F23.question_text: Once lined up beside the front car, how do you initiate backing and where must you look?
sec09-card-sec09-F23.teaching_text: Checking traffic behind first, then easing back while scanning mirrors and over your right shoulder prevents bumper taps.

sec09-card-sec09-F24.question_text: Which two steering inputs create the S-turn that tucks and straightens your car into a parallel space?
sec09-card-sec09-F24.teaching_text: Turning right angles the tail toward the curb, and countersteering once mostly inside swings the nose straight.

sec09-card-sec09-F25.question_text: Within what distance range from the curb must you center and finish a parallel park — and what final check comes before exiting?
sec09-card-sec09-F25.teaching_text: Tucking centered within six to twelve inches keeps your street-side fenders clear while a traffic scan protects your door.

sec09-card-sec09-R05.question_text: Keep the two parallel-parking numbers straight — what is your starting side gap versus your finished curb distance?
sec09-card-sec09-R05.teaching_text: Start feet away from the forward car, then finish inches from the curb.

sec09-card-sec09-F26.question_text: Why shouldn't you assume a driver walking without a cane or wheelchair is misusing a disability parking space?
sec09-card-sec09-F26.teaching_text: Severe heart, lung, or neurological conditions limit walking distance without requiring visible mobility aids.

sec09-card-sec09-F27.question_text: Does every disability plate or placard grant free metered parking in Michigan, or what specific credential is required?
sec09-card-sec09-F27.teaching_text: Standard disability plates or placards open accessible spaces, whereas free parking demands the stricter yellow sticker on a placard.

sec09-card-sec09-F28.question_text: What combination of occupant condition and displayed credential makes parking in a disability space legal?
sec09-card-sec09-F28.teaching_text: Both pieces must be present together — an occupant with a qualifying mobility or vision disability plus a valid plate or placard.

sec09-card-sec09-F29.question_text: Even with a valid disability placard hanging from the mirror, which two situations make using a disability space off-limits?
sec09-card-sec09-F29.teaching_text: Running inside solo while the placard holder stays in the car — or borrowing their car alone — misuses accessible parking.

sec09-card-sec09-F30.question_text: Why are van-accessible disability spaces wider, and what blue-painted or sloped areas must you never block?
sec09-card-sec09-F30.teaching_text: Parking on blue-striped aisles or blocking curb cuts traps wheelchair lift users outside or inside their vans.

sec09-card-sec09-R09.question_text: Separate what a regular disability plate or placard allows from what the yellow placard sticker adds?
sec09-card-sec09-R09.teaching_text: Exam questions test whether you know ordinary placards still pay meters unless they carry the yellow free-parking sticker.

sec09-card-sec09-F31.question_text: How can local city parking ordinances compare with Michigan state law, and where are drivers notified?
sec09-card-sec09-F31.teaching_text: Watch city-limit signs when entering a town because municipalities can enforce tighter parking rules than state baselines.

sec09-card-sec09-F32.question_text: Who is legally responsible for paying an illegal parking ticket on an owned vehicle versus a leased vehicle?
sec09-card-sec09-F32.teaching_text: Parking citations attach to the registered owner — or to the lessee on a leased car — regardless of who drove.

sec09-card-sec09-F33.question_text: Along with obeying no-stopping, no-standing, and no-parking signs, how far must you stay when parking near a fire or crash?
sec09-card-sec09-F33.teaching_text: Pulling over closer than five hundred feet to watch a fire or wreck clogs lanes needed by incoming rescue rigs.

sec09-card-sec09-F37.question_text: Which building exits, access lanes, and corner sightlines are illegal to block with a parked vehicle?
sec09-card-sec09-F37.teaching_text: Parking across driveways, alleys, theaters, emergency exits, fire escapes, or corner sightlines traps people and blinds turning drivers.

sec09-card-sec09-F38.question_text: What maximum curb distance and vehicle direction rule govern street parking?
sec09-card-sec09-F38.teaching_text: Parking wider than twelve inches out or facing against oncoming traffic forces you across opposing lanes.

sec09-card-sec09-F40.question_text: What parking bans apply to bridges, overpasses, tunnels, and rural highway lanes where a shoulder exists?
sec09-card-sec09-F40.teaching_text: Narrow spans and high-speed rural travel lanes leave zero room to swerve around a stationary car.

sec09-card-sec09-F41.question_text: Which pedestrian paths, driveways, junctions, and cycling lanes may you never park on or inside?
sec09-card-sec09-F41.teaching_text: Blocking sidewalks, driveways, intersections, crosswalks, or marked bike lanes shoves walkers and cyclists into live car traffic.

sec09-card-sec09-F43.question_text: What is the legal status of double parking beside a parked car, blocking a rural mailbox, or parking at a transit stop?
sec09-card-sec09-F43.teaching_text: Even a quick two-minute hazard-light stop beside a parked car, rural mailbox, or bus zone draws a citation.

sec09-card-sec09-R10.question_text: If a friend borrows a leased car and parks it illegally, whom does the ticket hold responsible?
sec09-card-sec09-R10.teaching_text: Liability follows the leaseholder rather than chasing down whichever friend left the car in a no-parking zone.

sec09-card-sec09-F34.question_text: How many feet of clear curb space must you leave on either side of a fire hydrant?
sec09-card-sec09-F34.teaching_text: Pumper trucks need unobstructed fifteen-foot hose angles to hook up fast during a structure fire.

sec09-card-sec09-F35.question_text: How far must you park from a fire station driveway on the same side of the street — and on the opposite side when marked?
sec09-card-sec09-F35.teaching_text: Long ladder trucks need a wide turning sweep across the whole street when rolling out under sirens.

sec09-card-sec09-F36.question_text: Within how many feet of the nearest rail of a railroad crossing is parking illegal?
sec09-card-sec09-F36.teaching_text: Parked cars closer than fifty feet hide approaching trains and crossing flashers from moving drivers.

sec09-card-sec09-F39.question_text: How far back must you park from a stop sign, traffic light, flashing beacon, or warning sign?
sec09-card-sec09-F39.teaching_text: Tall SUVs or vans parked within thirty feet screen vital stop, beacon, and warning signs from approaching lanes.

sec09-card-sec09-F42.question_text: How far must you park from a marked crosswalk versus an intersection that has no crosswalk?
sec09-card-sec09-F42.teaching_text: Marked pedestrian crossings get an extra five-foot sightline cushion beyond the fifteen-foot plain-intersection rule.

sec09-card-sec09-R01.question_text: Match fifteen, twenty, thirty, and fifty feet to a hydrant, same-side fire station driveway, stop sign or signal, and railroad rail?
sec09-card-sec09-R01.teaching_text: Climbing that clean number ladder keeps hydrant, fire-station, signal, and rail distances locked in for exam day.

sec09-card-sec09-R02.question_text: Why does the fire station driveway parking ban jump from twenty feet on the same side to seventy-five feet across the street?
sec09-card-sec09-R02.teaching_text: Fire engines swing wide across opposing curb space on exit, so marked opposite curbs require seventy-five feet.

sec09-card-sec09-R03.question_text: Compare the no-parking buffer at a marked crosswalk against an unmarked plain intersection?
sec09-card-sec09-R03.teaching_text: Adding painted crosswalk lines bumps the required corner parking buffer up from fifteen feet to twenty feet.

sec01-card-sec01-F01.question_text: What two conditions must you meet to count as a Michigan resident for licensing?
sec01-card-sec01-F01.teaching_text: Having a local mailing address alone falls short unless you both live in Michigan and document lawful presence.

sec01-card-sec01-F02.question_text: May the Secretary of State issue a first-time driver's license or state ID card to a non-resident?
sec01-card-sec01-F02.teaching_text: Visiting relatives or studying briefly without legal Michigan residency bars you from receiving an original state card.

sec01-card-sec01-F03.question_text: How soon must a new Michigan resident title and register their vehicle, and what document do they surrender?
sec01-card-sec01-F03.teaching_text: Michigan gives zero grace-month delay on vehicle registration once you move in with an out-of-state title.

sec01-card-sec01-F04.question_text: How long may a newcomer keep driving on another state's license, and what comes next?
sec01-card-sec01-F04.teaching_text: Once you establish Michigan residency, continuing to rely on your former state's plastic stops being valid.

sec01-card-sec01-F05.question_text: What happens to your driving history from your former home state when you move to Michigan?
sec01-card-sec01-F05.teaching_text: Moving across state lines never wipes old tickets clean because Michigan pulls and absorbs your prior history.

sec01-card-sec01-F06.question_text: What must you resolve first if your out-of-state driver's license is currently suspended or revoked?
sec01-card-sec01-F06.teaching_text: National driver checks block your Michigan application at the counter until every out-of-state suspension is settled.

sec01-card-sec01-F07.question_text: What happens to your out-of-state license once Michigan accepts your application, and why?
sec01-card-sec01-F07.teaching_text: Staff punch or invalidate your old card before handing it back so nobody carries two active licenses.

sec01-card-sec01-R02.question_text: Does your out-of-state license expire when your new Michigan card arrives in the mail or earlier?
sec01-card-sec01-R02.teaching_text: Exam traps suggest waiting for mail delivery, yet your old card loses validity the moment Michigan accepts your application.

sec01-card-sec01-R03.question_text: How does a new resident's deadline for vehicle title and registration compare with applying for a Michigan license?
sec01-card-sec01-R03.teaching_text: Keep those two timelines straight since car paperwork happens right away while your license switches once residency is established.

sec01-card-sec01-F09.question_text: When is an applicant who has never held any license refused a Michigan license over prior tickets?
sec01-card-sec01-F09.teaching_text: Driving unlicensed and catching two moving convictions inside three years locks you out when you finally apply.

sec01-card-sec01-F10.question_text: At most how many convictions within the preceding three years may appear on your record when applying for a license?
sec01-card-sec01-F10.teaching_text: Carrying more than a single conviction inside the three-year pre-application window blocks license issuance.

sec01-card-sec01-R01.question_text: How do the never-licensed refusal threshold and the general applicant conviction cap fit together over three years?
sec01-card-sec01-R01.teaching_text: Both rules draw the exact same line from opposite sides—one conviction passes while two moving convictions trigger refusal.

sec01-card-sec01-F08.question_text: What three factors shape Michigan's licensing rules, and what extra steps can chauffeur or commercial licenses add?
sec01-card-sec01-F08.teaching_text: Stepping beyond a basic car into paid or heavy-truck driving adds specialized exams and possible background checks.

sec01-card-sec01-F11.question_text: What official name does Michigan give its standard everyday driver's license?
sec01-card-sec01-F11.teaching_text: Unless you drive commercially or for hire as a chauffeur, Michigan classifies your regular car credential as an operator's license.

sec01-card-sec01-F12.question_text: What minimum age and exam apply to a chauffeur's license, and which driving jobs require holding one?
sec01-card-sec01-F12.teaching_text: Being hired primarily to drive ten-thousand-pound trucks, carry paying riders or cargo, or drive buses requires a chauffeur's credential.

sec01-card-sec01-F13.question_text: Which four vehicle weights, passenger capacities, or cargo types require a commercial driver's license?
sec01-card-sec01-F13.teaching_text: Watch that exact twenty-six thousand one pound mark—not twenty-six thousand flat—alongside sixteen-person buses and placarded hazmat.

sec01-card-sec01-F14.question_text: What clean-record window and age limits separate intrastate Michigan commercial driving from interstate or hazmat driving?
sec01-card-sec01-F14.teaching_text: Any suspension inside the prior thirty-six months disqualifies you, and crossing state lines or hauling hazmat waits until twenty-one.

sec01-card-sec01-R04.question_text: How does the single-vehicle weight trigger for a chauffeur's license compare with a commercial driver's license?
sec01-card-sec01-R04.teaching_text: Driving a twelve-thousand-pound delivery van for work needs a chauffeur's card, whereas commercial status starts above twenty-six thousand pounds.

sec01-card-sec01-R05.question_text: What changes for a Michigan commercial driver between age eighteen and age twenty-one?
sec01-card-sec01-R05.teaching_text: Under-twenty-one commercial drivers must keep every route inside Michigan and avoid placarded hazardous cargo.

sec01-card-sec01-F17.question_text: Does a valid operator's or chauffeur's license cover moped riding—and what if your driver's license is suspended?
sec01-card-sec01-F17.teaching_text: You cannot dodge a driver's license suspension or revocation by applying for a separate moped credential.

sec01-card-sec01-F18.question_text: How can an unlicensed teen qualify for a standalone moped license, and which three tests are required?
sec01-card-sec01-F18.teaching_text: Fifteen-year-olds without a car permit can ride mopeds legally after parental sign-off and passing vision, knowledge, and sign exams.

sec01-card-sec01-F19.question_text: What two routes earn a CY motorcycle endorsement, and which riders are required to take the education course?
sec01-card-sec01-F19.teaching_text: Adults can test directly unless they fail skills twice, whereas sixteen- and seventeen-year-olds must pass rider education.

sec01-card-sec01-F20.question_text: What does a CY three W restriction limit a rider to, and what two ways can you earn it?
sec01-card-sec01-F20.teaching_text: Earning your endorsement on a three-wheeler restricts you from hopping onto a standard two-wheeled motorcycle.

sec01-card-sec01-F21.question_text: Which towing setup requires Michigan's recreational double R endorsement, and what test unlocks it?
sec01-card-sec01-F21.teaching_text: Towing a boat or utility trailer behind a fifth-wheel camper demands passing the double R knowledge test first.

sec01-card-sec01-F22.question_text: What does a farmer endorsement authorize, and which two written tests may be required?
sec01-card-sec01-F22.teaching_text: Qualifying agricultural haulers move equipment, livestock, and produce after clearing general knowledge and combination-vehicle exams when required.

sec01-card-sec01-R06.question_text: How do Michigan's moped rules differ between someone holding a valid driver's license and an unlicensed teen?
sec01-card-sec01-R06.teaching_text: Active driver's licenses already include moped privileges, while unlicensed teens must be fifteen with parent consent and three passed exams.

sec01-card-sec01-R07.question_text: How does a full CY endorsement differ from a CY three W restriction on a Michigan license?
sec01-card-sec01-R07.teaching_text: Check whether the credential carries the three W restriction before riding a two-wheeled bike.

sec01-card-sec01-R08.question_text: For which two groups of motorcycle applicants does rider education shift from optional to mandatory?
sec01-card-sec01-R08.teaching_text: Skipping the course works only for adults who pass their motorcycle skills test within two tries.

sec01-card-sec01-F15.question_text: Which borders and travel modes does a Michigan enhanced driver's license cover—and does it count as REAL ID?
sec01-card-sec01-F15.teaching_text: Enhanced cards cover land and sea re-entry from Canada, Mexico, Bermuda, and the Caribbean—never international air flights—while satisfying REAL ID.

sec01-card-sec01-F23.question_text: Beginning May seven, two thousand twenty-five, which trips and facilities require a REAL ID-compliant document?
sec01-card-sec01-F23.teaching_text: Without a compliant card or passport at airport security or military gates, standard state plastic gets turned away.

sec01-card-sec01-F24.question_text: Which state and federal credentials count as REAL ID-compliant, and where are acceptable air-travel IDs listed?
sec01-card-sec01-F24.teaching_text: Travelers holding a valid United States passport or passport card already own federal flight identification listed by TSA.

sec01-card-sec01-F25.question_text: Which corner markings show a Michigan card is REAL ID compliant—and how do starless enhanced cards work?
sec01-card-sec01-F25.teaching_text: Older enhanced licenses without the corner star already meet federal rules and pick up the star at renewal.

sec01-card-sec01-F26.question_text: Is upgrading to a REAL ID mandatory for every Michigan resident, and when might you skip it?
sec01-card-sec01-F26.teaching_text: Nobody forces a REAL ID upgrade if you never fly domestically, avoid restricted federal sites, or carry a passport.

sec01-card-sec01-F27.question_text: How does the cost of converting to a REAL ID at renewal compare with converting mid-cycle?
sec01-card-sec01-F27.teaching_text: Timing your REAL ID upgrade with regular license renewal saves paying an extra duplicate-card fee.

sec01-card-sec01-F28.question_text: What phrase is printed on a standard non-REAL ID Michigan card, and what everyday uses does it still cover?
sec01-card-sec01-F28.teaching_text: Seeing Not for Federal Identification on your license never limits lawful driving, car rentals, check cashing, or age-restricted purchases.

sec01-card-sec01-R09.question_text: Between a starless enhanced card and a standard card marked Not for Federal Identification, which satisfies REAL ID?
sec01-card-sec01-R09.teaching_text: Both cards let you drive legally, yet only the enhanced credential clears federal airport and base checkpoints.

sec01-card-sec01-R10.question_text: When does adding REAL ID to your Michigan credential trigger a duplicate card fee?
sec01-card-sec01-R10.teaching_text: Applying between renewal cycles orders an early replacement card, which triggers the standard duplicate charge.

sec01-card-sec01-F29.question_text: Which four document categories must a newcomer bring once Michigan residency is established?
sec01-card-sec01-F29.teaching_text: Missing any one of those four document pillars stalls your newcomer conversion at the Secretary of State counter.

sec01-card-sec01-F30.question_text: What screening always follows newcomer document approval, and what extra steps might apply?
sec01-card-sec01-F30.teaching_text: Every newcomer completes vision screening, while knowledge exams, instruction permits, and road tests depend on where your old license came from.

sec01-card-sec01-F31.question_text: Valid licenses from which jurisdictions convert straight to a Michigan license without knowledge tests, permits, or road tests?
sec01-card-sec01-F31.teaching_text: Reciprocity agreements let drivers from other states, Canada, Germany, and South Korea swap active licenses with vision screening alone.

sec01-card-sec01-F32.question_text: What happens when a newcomer presents any expired foreign license or an out-of-state license expired four years or more?
sec01-card-sec01-F32.teaching_text: Reciprocity disappears once a foreign card expires or an out-of-state license sits expired for four full years.

sec01-card-sec01-F33.question_text: What final steps happen at the counter, and how long does mail delivery of your new Michigan license take?
sec01-card-sec01-F33.teaching_text: Michigan mails permanent photo cards in roughly three weeks rather than printing hard plastic over the counter.

sec01-card-sec01-F16.question_text: What are the three tiers of Michigan's Graduated Driver Licensing system for teens under eighteen?
sec01-card-sec01-F16.teaching_text: Driver education feeds under-eighteen teens step by step from supervised learning through intermediate limits to full privileges.

sec01-card-sec01-F34.question_text: Who must complete Michigan's Graduated Driver Licensing program, and which newcomers under eighteen are excused?
sec01-card-sec01-F34.teaching_text: Holding a valid out-of-state license for more than twelve months exempts a transferring teen from starting Michigan GDL.

sec01-card-sec01-R11.question_text: How does conversion for active Canadian, German, South Korean, or state licenses contrast with expired foreign or long-lapsed state cards?
sec01-card-sec01-R11.teaching_text: Check both origin and expiration date because an expired German card or four-year-expired state card still triggers full testing.

sec01-card-sec01-R12.question_text: What exact out-of-state licensing history excuses a newcomer under eighteen from Graduated Driver Licensing?
sec01-card-sec01-R12.teaching_text: An out-of-state learner's permit or a license held only six months will not waive Michigan's GDL requirements.

sec04-card-sec04-F01.question_text: How do you keep your Michigan driver's license, and what three actions can hit it if you slip?
sec04-card-sec04-F01.teaching_text: Treat driving as an earned privilege; unsafe habits can leave your license restricted, suspended, or revoked.

sec04-card-sec04-F02.question_text: What events appear on your Michigan driving record, and who reports them to the Secretary of State?
sec04-card-sec04-F02.teaching_text: Police agencies and courts feed civil or criminal moving violations, crashes, and certain drug convictions onto your file.

sec04-card-sec04-F03.question_text: How does Michigan handle crashes and moving convictions you pick up in another state?
sec04-card-sec04-F03.teaching_text: Crossing state lines never hides a speeding ticket; out-of-state convictions come home and score under Michigan's point chart.

sec04-card-sec04-F04.question_text: How long do ordinary convictions, select actions, and fatal or impaired-driving convictions stay on your record?
sec04-card-sec04-F04.teaching_text: Most convictions linger at least seven years—some ten—while fatal or impaired-driving convictions never leave your record.

sec04-card-sec04-F05.question_text: What protects personal details on your driving record, and which lawful uses still get access?
sec04-card-sec04-F05.teaching_text: Federal privacy rules block casual snooping while allowing insurers, safety recalls, and rental counters permissible access.

sec04-card-sec04-F06.question_text: Into what three legal tiers do traffic violations fall, and what typically follows ignoring a ticket?
sec04-card-sec04-F06.teaching_text: Letting even a minor civil ticket sit unpaid or unanswered routinely snowballs into a suspended license.

sec04-card-sec04-F07.question_text: What two consequences hit if you receive a moving-violation ticket while your license is already suspended?
sec04-card-sec04-F07.teaching_text: Getting caught driving on a suspended license stacks fresh suspension time on top of mandatory reinstatement fees.

sec04-card-sec04-F11.question_text: Why must you present extenuating ticket circumstances in court rather than to the Secretary of State?
sec04-card-sec04-F11.teaching_text: Once a court enters a conviction, the Secretary of State has zero legal power to overturn it.

sec04-card-sec04-F08.question_text: When do Michigan Vehicle Code points post to your record, and how long do they remain active?
sec04-card-sec04-F08.teaching_text: Points attach only after a moving-violation conviction and count for two years measured from conviction day.

sec04-card-sec04-F09.question_text: Which two two-year point patterns trigger a mandatory Michigan driver assessment reexamination?
sec04-card-sec04-F09.teaching_text: Racking up twelve total points—or six separate one-point tickets—inside two years lands you in a state assessment.

sec04-card-sec04-F10.question_text: How do Michigan driving-record points relate to the points auto insurers use to price coverage?
sec04-card-sec04-F10.teaching_text: Auto insurers run their own internal pricing formulas rather than copying Secretary of State record points.

sec04-card-sec04-R05.question_text: Do points on your Michigan state driving record directly set your auto-insurance premium?
sec04-card-sec04-R05.teaching_text: Do not confuse state licensing points with insurance-company rating points—each system tracks drivers independently.

sec04-card-sec04-R06.question_text: Why doesn't your record turn spotless once your points expire at the two-year mark?
sec04-card-sec04-R06.teaching_text: Active points vanish after two years, yet the underlying conviction remains visible seven, ten, or infinite years.

sec04-card-sec04-R07.question_text: Over what window are reexamination triggers counted, and what are both point thresholds?
sec04-card-sec04-R07.teaching_text: Even tiny one-point violations add up to a reexamination if six hit within twenty-four months.

sec04-card-sec04-F12.question_text: Which felony, intoxication, drug, and crash-scene offenses carry Michigan's maximum six points?
sec04-card-sec04-F12.teaching_text: Vehicle felonies, operating intoxicated or with Schedule One drugs or cocaine, and fleeing a crash each cost six points.

sec04-card-sec04-F13.question_text: How many points come from reckless driving, chemical-test refusal, fleeing police, or causing injury or death?
sec04-card-sec04-F13.teaching_text: Picking up just two six-point convictions hits Michigan's twelve-point reexamination mark without any extra tickets.

sec04-card-sec04-F14.question_text: How many points apply when failing to yield injures or kills a responder, road worker, or animal-implement operator?
sec04-card-sec04-F14.teaching_text: Failing to yield jumps straight to six points whenever emergency crews, construction workers, or animal-implement operators get hurt.

sec04-card-sec04-F15.question_text: Which four offenses—covering racing, alcohol, underage drinking, and heavy speeding—carry four points?
sec04-card-sec04-F15.teaching_text: Any bodily alcohol under twenty-one lands in the same four-point bracket as drag racing and sixteen-plus speeding.

sec04-card-sec04-F16.question_text: Which six everyday traffic, crossing, bus, and mid-tier speeding violations post three points?
sec04-card-sec04-F16.teaching_text: Blowing a stop sign, railroad crossing, or school bus posts three points—matching careless driving and eleven-to-fifteen over.

sec04-card-sec04-F17.question_text: Which speeding band, alcohol-container, underage breath-test, emergency-yield, and catch-all violations carry two points?
sec04-card-sec04-F17.teaching_text: Two points cover six-to-ten over, open alcohol containers, under-twenty-one PBT refusals, emergency yield slips, and other moving violations.

sec04-card-sec04-R01.question_text: How do Michigan points climb across the six-to-ten, eleven-to-fifteen, and sixteen-plus speeding bands?
sec04-card-sec04-R01.teaching_text: Memorize the clean step-up—six-to-ten costs two points, eleven-to-fifteen costs three, and sixteen-plus costs four.

sec04-card-sec04-R02.question_text: How does refusing an official chemical alcohol test compare in points with an under-twenty-one roadside PBT refusal?
sec04-card-sec04-R02.teaching_text: Do not mix up station chemical testing at six points with a roadside Preliminary Breath Test refusal under twenty-one at two.

sec04-card-sec04-R03.question_text: How do Michigan's point totals split between operating while intoxicated and impaired driving or underage alcohol?
sec04-card-sec04-R03.teaching_text: Operating while intoxicated hits the top six-point tier, whereas impaired driving and under-twenty-one alcohol post four.

sec04-card-sec04-R04.question_text: How does the point penalty jump when failing to yield to an emergency vehicle injures or kills a responder?
sec04-card-sec04-R04.teaching_text: Ordinary failure to yield to flashing responders costs two points, jumping to six if any responder is hurt or killed.

sec04-card-sec04-F18.question_text: Why do standard servings of beer, wine, and whiskey impair a driver equally?
sec04-card-sec04-F18.teaching_text: Switching from whiskey shots to twelve-ounce beers or five-ounce wines puts the exact same pure alcohol into your bloodstream.

sec04-card-sec04-F19.question_text: Which two mental faculties take a hit from any standard alcoholic drink?
sec04-card-sec04-F19.teaching_text: Before your speech slurs or balance wobbles, alcohol quietly erodes sound judgment and impulse control.

sec04-card-sec04-F20.question_text: In what three driving-critical ways can even a single drink impair you?
sec04-card-sec04-F20.teaching_text: Waiting until you feel buzzed ignores slower brake reactions, weaker concentration, and degraded visual tracking after drink one.

sec04-card-sec04-F21.question_text: Do coffee, cold showers, exercise, or fresh air sober you up—or what actually works?
sec04-card-sec04-F21.teaching_text: Caffeine and cold water only create a wide-awake impaired driver while your liver processes alcohol on its own clock.

sec04-card-sec04-F22.question_text: What sober-ride plan should you lock in before any drinking starts?
sec04-card-sec04-F22.teaching_text: Lining up a designated driver, rideshare, taxi, or transit ahead of time removes impaired late-night judgment.

sec04-card-sec04-F23.question_text: How should you step in if an impaired friend tries to drive or invites you to ride along?
sec04-card-sec04-F23.teaching_text: Stepping up to take a friend's keys and offer a couch saves lives on both sides of the windshield.

sec04-card-sec04-R10.question_text: Why is feeling refreshed after coffee, exercise, or fresh air a trap after drinking?
sec04-card-sec04-R10.teaching_text: Feeling brisk in cold night air masks unchanged blood alcohol—only elapsed hours restore safe driving fitness.

sec04-card-sec04-F24.question_text: Can a drug possession, manufacture, or distribution conviction suspend your license even if no car was involved?
sec04-card-sec04-F24.teaching_text: Michigan mandates license suspension on qualifying drug convictions even when the offense happened miles away from any vehicle.

sec04-card-sec04-F25.question_text: With zero prior drug violations, how long is the license suspension and hard no-restricted-license period?
sec04-card-sec04-F25.teaching_text: A first drug conviction suspends driving for six months and bars even a restricted license for the opening thirty days.

sec04-card-sec04-F26.question_text: What suspension and hard lockout apply if you have a prior drug conviction within seven years?
sec04-card-sec04-F26.teaching_text: A second drug conviction inside seven years doubles both penalties to a one-year suspension and sixty un-restricted-ineligible days.

sec04-card-sec04-F27.question_text: How much is the drug-suspension reinstatement fee, and does it bundle with other reinstatement fees?
sec04-card-sec04-F27.teaching_text: Expect a standalone one-hundred-twenty-five-dollar fee on top of any other reinstatement charges owed.

sec04-card-sec04-R08.question_text: How do suspension length and restricted-license wait double from a first drug offense to a seven-year repeat?
sec04-card-sec04-R08.teaching_text: Both numbers double cleanly—six months becomes one year, and the thirty-day hard wait becomes sixty days.

sec04-card-sec04-F28.question_text: Why is driving high illegal even where adult marijuana possession is legal?
sec04-card-sec04-F28.teaching_text: THC warps how you judge gap timing, lane position, and closing speed—making impaired driving illegal everywhere.

sec04-card-sec04-F29.question_text: How much total marijuana—and concentrate inside that cap—may an adult twenty-one or older legally transport?
sec04-card-sec04-F29.teaching_text: Adults twenty-one and up cap legal transport at two and a half ounces total, including at most fifteen concentrate grams.

sec04-card-sec04-F30.question_text: Which five land, air, snow, trail, or water craft are illegal to operate or consume marijuana on while impaired?
sec04-card-sec04-F30.teaching_text: Michigan's marijuana operating ban reaches beyond cars to aircraft, snowmobiles, off-road vehicles, and motorboats.

sec04-card-sec04-F31.question_text: May drivers or passengers smoke marijuana inside a car on public roads, or carry it into Canada?
sec04-card-sec04-F31.teaching_text: Smoking cannabis in the passenger cabin on public ways is illegal, and crossing into Canada with any remains a border crime.

sec04-card-sec04-F32.question_text: What four clues and tests do officers combine to evaluate driver impairment?
sec04-card-sec04-F32.teaching_text: Officers weigh lane cues, face-to-face observations, standardized and non-standardized field tests, plus chemical testing.

sec04-card-sec04-F33.question_text: When do you agree to Michigan's implied-consent chemical testing, and what happens if you refuse?
sec04-card-sec04-F33.teaching_text: Applying for or renewing a Michigan license pre-commits you to chemical testing—refusing suspends your license automatically.

sec04-card-sec04-F34.question_text: What jail time, fine, record points, and minor-passenger rule apply to marijuana-impaired driving?
sec04-card-sec04-F34.teaching_text: Drugged driving matches alcohol DUI—up to ninety-three jail days, five hundred dollars, suspension, six points, and harsher penalties with minors aboard.

sec04-card-sec04-R09.question_text: How does adult legal marijuana transport coexist with Michigan's impaired-driving penalties?
sec04-card-sec04-R09.teaching_text: Just like carrying sealed beer home from a store, legal adult transport never legalizes driving under the influence.

sec04-card-sec04-F35.question_text: Which four categories of safety or record trouble allow the Secretary of State to call you in for reexamination?
sec04-card-sec04-F35.teaching_text: State analysts step in whenever medical fitness, broken license restrictions, crash patterns, or mounting points raise red flags.

sec04-card-sec04-F36.question_text: After how few violations can probationary and GDL teen drivers be called in for reexamination?
sec04-card-sec04-F36.teaching_text: New and GDL drivers do not get twelve points of slack—one or two tickets can trigger an assessment.

sec04-card-sec04-F37.question_text: What does a driver assessment reexamination evaluate, and what licensing controls can it impose?
sec04-card-sec04-F37.teaching_text: Analysts review your safety record and can apply restrictions, a suspension, a revocation, or a combined action.

sec04-card-sec04-F38.question_text: Which health conditions, fatal-crash findings, and conviction types serve as legal grounds for reexamination?
sec04-card-sec04-F38.teaching_text: Unsafe physical, visual, or mental conditions, negligent or alcohol-linked fatal crashes, and restriction convictions all trigger review.

sec04-card-sec04-F39.question_text: Alongside twelve points in two years, what two-year crash count allows a driver reexamination?
sec04-card-sec04-F39.teaching_text: Three crashes involving injury or property damage inside twenty-four months trigger review even below twelve points.

sec04-card-sec04-F40.question_text: What happens during your meeting with a driver analyst if licensing controls are placed on your card?
sec04-card-sec04-F40.teaching_text: After reviewing your history together, the analyst outlines both how to appeal and how to earn reinstatement.

sec04-card-sec04-F41.question_text: Which exams and updated professional records can a medical reexamination require?
sec04-card-sec04-F41.teaching_text: Medical reviews can test vision, rules, and on-road driving alongside fresh medical, eye, or psychological evaluations.

sec04-card-sec04-F42.question_text: Which official Michigan web address gathers driver education, GDL rules, parent coaching, and teen risk tools?
sec04-card-sec04-F42.teaching_text: Bookmarking Michigan dot gov slash NewDrivers puts GDL timelines and parent-teen coaching checklists in one official hub.

sec04-card-sec04-R11.question_text: How do reexamination thresholds compare between regular full-license holders and probationary or GDL drivers?
sec04-card-sec04-R11.teaching_text: Full-license motorists get until twelve points or three two-year wrecks, whereas probationary or GDL teens get flagged after one or two tickets.

sec05-card-sec05-F01.question_text: Roughly how many yearly crash deaths do federal officials link to distraction, and across which three distraction types?
sec05-card-sec05-F01.teaching_text: Pulling hands off the wheel, eyes off traffic, or thoughts off driving claims at least three thousand four hundred lives yearly.

sec05-card-sec05-F02.question_text: Why might federal crash-death statistics actually undercount distracted driving?
sec05-card-sec05-F02.teaching_text: Unlike blood alcohol, a momentary glance or daydream leaves little physical proof at a wreck scene.

sec05-card-sec05-F03.question_text: Under what careless or reckless standards can Michigan prosecute a distracted driver?
sec05-card-sec05-F03.teaching_text: Endangering people or property carelessly—or showing willful, wanton disregard—opens distracted drivers to Michigan prosecution.

sec05-card-sec05-F06.question_text: Which three body or mental channels do distractions hijack, and why does multitasking fail behind the wheel?
sec05-card-sec05-F06.teaching_text: Your brain cannot give full attention to two tasks simultaneously, turning split focus into delayed hazard reactions.

sec05-card-sec05-F07.question_text: At sixty-five miles per hour, how far does your car roll during the quarter-second brain switch between tasks?
sec05-card-sec05-F07.teaching_text: Simply shifting mental gears at freeway pace rolls more than a full car length before you even react.

sec05-card-sec05-R10.question_text: Why does even tapping a radio knob carry real risk at sixty-five miles per hour?
sec05-card-sec05-R10.teaching_text: Every attention shift eats twenty-four feet at sixty-five, proving quick cabin tweaks are never zero-cost.

sec05-card-sec05-F08.question_text: How should you handle maps or directions before pulling out—with a passenger versus solo?
sec05-card-sec05-F08.teaching_text: Hand navigation duties to your front passenger—or study your route before shifting out of Park when solo.

sec05-card-sec05-F09.question_text: How well should you know your cabin climate and audio controls before driving?
sec05-card-sec05-F09.teaching_text: Fumbling across unfamiliar touchscreens or knobs steals crucial seconds of forward sightline in moving traffic.

sec05-card-sec05-F10.question_text: When do playlist picks, radio presets, and personal grooming belong?
sec05-card-sec05-F10.teaching_text: Lock in playlists before rolling and save mirrors for traffic—never mascara, hair, or shaving on the move.

sec05-card-sec05-F11.question_text: Why must children be buckled and comfortable before you start driving?
sec05-card-sec05-F11.teaching_text: Twisting backward to hand snacks or fix straps mid-drive pulls eyes, hands, and focus off traffic simultaneously.

sec05-card-sec05-F12.question_text: How should you treat phones and electronics while moving, and what if a call cannot wait?
sec05-card-sec05-F12.teaching_text: Leave phones, texters, and screens alone in motion—pull into a safe parking spot first whenever calling is urgent.

sec05-card-sec05-F13.question_text: Which reading, writing, and conversation habits should you keep out of the driver's seat?
sec05-card-sec05-F13.teaching_text: Jotting notes, looking up numbers, or battling through emotional arguments hijacks mental bandwidth needed for sudden hazards.

sec05-card-sec05-F14.question_text: What rules apply if you snack or sip in the car, or notice fatigue and daydreaming?
sec05-card-sec05-F14.teaching_text: Spilled drinks and messy wrappers cause panic swerves, while fatigue or zoned-out thoughts call for an immediate rest break.

sec05-card-sec05-F04.question_text: What everyday phone actions are illegal while driving in Michigan, and when may you break that rule?
sec05-card-sec05-F04.teaching_text: Holding a phone to talk, read, or text is illegal unless reporting a crash, crime, or true emergency.

sec05-card-sec05-F05.question_text: What civil fines hit a first handheld-phone violation versus any repeat violation?
sec05-card-sec05-F05.teaching_text: Getting caught holding your phone costs one hundred dollars the first time and jumps to two hundred fifty thereafter.

sec05-card-sec05-F15.question_text: Who is covered by Michigan's general cell-phone law, and where does it ban holding or using mobile devices?
sec05-card-sec05-F15.teaching_text: Michigan's hands-free law covers all drivers using phones or tablets on public roads and other public driving venues.

sec05-card-sec05-F16.question_text: Which four call, text, video, and social-media actions are explicitly barred on mobile devices while driving?
sec05-card-sec05-F16.teaching_text: Calling, texting, watching or filming video, and scrolling or posting social feeds all violate Michigan's device ban.

sec05-card-sec05-F17.question_text: Which responders may any driver—including teens—text or call to report medical, crash, hazard, fire, or hazmat emergencies?
sec05-card-sec05-F17.teaching_text: Even GDL teens may use a phone to reach nine-one-one, police, fire, or medical teams during real emergencies.

sec05-card-sec05-F18.question_text: Beyond crashes and fires, what two live threats let you legally use a phone to alert authorities?
sec05-card-sec05-F18.teaching_text: Calling in a weaving impaired driver or a crime unfolding in front of you falls inside Michigan's emergency shield.

sec05-card-sec05-R04.question_text: How much does a second or third handheld-phone ticket cost compared with your first?
sec05-card-sec05-R04.teaching_text: Every repeat handheld-phone stop after your one-hundred-dollar first ticket carries a two-hundred-fifty-dollar fine.

sec05-card-sec05-F19.question_text: Under Kelsey's Law, what phone restriction applies to Level one and Level two GDL teen drivers?
sec05-card-sec05-F19.teaching_text: Kelsey's Law bans GDL Level one and Level two teens from placing or answering everyday phone calls behind the wheel.
