sec05-card-sec05-F20.question_text: Under what condition may GDL Level three teens and adult drivers use GPS navigation?
sec05-card-sec05-F20.teaching_text: Glancing at pre-set turn prompts is legal for Level three and adult drivers, provided nobody types destinations manually.

sec05-card-sec05-F21.question_text: How much finger contact is permitted when using voice-operated or hands-free features?
sec05-card-sec05-F21.teaching_text: Hands-free stays legal only when your hand leaves the device after one quick tap or swipe—or via built-in dash controls.

sec05-card-sec05-F22.question_text: How does Michigan law treat continuous-recording dash cams and properly used windshield or dash mounts?
sec05-card-sec05-F22.teaching_text: Passive dash cameras recording the road ahead and mounted devices running hands-free exemptions remain completely legal.

sec05-card-sec05-R01.question_text: How do hands-free call rules change when a Michigan teen advances from GDL Level two to Level three?
sec05-card-sec05-R01.teaching_text: Kelsey's Law blocks even hands-free social calls on Level one and two, whereas Level three unlocks adult hands-free rules.

sec05-card-sec05-R02.question_text: Why can an eligible driver tap once to answer hands-free yet not type an address into GPS?
sec05-card-sec05-R02.teaching_text: One quick tap keeps eyes forward, whereas pecking street letters on glass turns into illegal manual entry.

sec05-card-sec05-R03.question_text: Who can use Michigan's emergency phone exception, and does it excuse calling parents or friends?
sec05-card-sec05-R03.teaching_text: Teens and adults alike can dial police, fire, or medics in danger, yet routine check-in calls stay illegal.

sec05-card-sec05-F23.question_text: Under Click It or Ticket, does an officer need another violation before stopping an unbuckled car?
sec05-card-sec05-F23.teaching_text: Michigan enforces seat belts as a primary offense—missing a belt by itself gives police grounds to pull you over.

sec05-card-sec05-F24.question_text: Which seats require belts for adults versus passengers younger than sixteen in Michigan?
sec05-card-sec05-F24.teaching_text: Every driver and front passenger must buckle up, and riders under sixteen must buckle in both front and back.

sec05-card-sec05-F26.question_text: More than how many lives per year do federal officials credit seat belts with saving?
sec05-card-sec05-F26.teaching_text: Clicking a seat belt remains the single highest-impact crash survival step, saving over thirteen thousand lives annually.

sec05-card-sec05-F27.question_text: Do air bags replace seat belts, and where should your shoulder and lap straps cross your body?
sec05-card-sec05-F27.teaching_text: Air bags need belts holding you in position—route straps mid-chest clear of your neck and low over hip bones.

sec05-card-sec05-F28.question_text: What document must a driver carry if medically excused from wearing a seat belt?
sec05-card-sec05-F28.teaching_text: Claiming a medical reason verbally at a traffic stop will not work without carrying your doctor's signed statement.

sec05-card-sec05-R05.question_text: How does Michigan's mandatory belt rule change at age sixteen for back-seat passengers?
sec05-card-sec05-R05.teaching_text: Anyone under sixteen must buckle in every row, whereas the statute's sixteen-and-older mandate names driver and front seats.

sec05-card-sec05-R09.question_text: Why must you still position your chest and hip straps properly in an air-bag-equipped car?
sec05-card-sec05-R09.teaching_text: Unbelted riders slide forward into exploding air bags; chest and hip straps keep crash forces on strong bone.

sec05-card-sec05-F25.question_text: Which age or height threshold requires a child to use an approved car seat or booster in any seat?
sec05-card-sec05-F25.teaching_text: Adult seat belts ride dangerously across small necks and stomachs until kids clear four feet nine inches or age eight.

sec05-card-sec05-F29.question_text: When does Michigan law allow leaving a booster, and why are parents urged to prioritize height?
sec05-card-sec05-F29.teaching_text: Legally whichever milestone arrives first counts, yet waiting for four feet nine inches ensures adult straps fit safely.

sec05-card-sec05-F30.question_text: Which three authorities govern how a child restraint is installed and buckled?
sec05-card-sec05-F30.teaching_text: Loose or misrouted tethers fail in crashes, so follow both manuals alongside federal safety standards.

sec05-card-sec05-F31.question_text: Is removing a baby from a car seat to nurse allowed while the vehicle is moving?
sec05-card-sec05-F31.teaching_text: Pull over and park first—an unrestrained infant cannot be held safely in arms during sudden braking.

sec05-card-sec05-F32.question_text: Where must children younger than four ride, and what is the sole multi-child exception?
sec05-card-sec05-F32.teaching_text: Toddlers under four must sit in back unless other children under four already occupy every available rear position.

sec05-card-sec05-F33.question_text: Under what single air-bag condition may a rear-facing infant seat ride in the front passenger seat?
sec05-card-sec05-F33.teaching_text: A deploying front air bag strikes the back of a rear-facing shell with lethal force unless deactivated.

sec05-card-sec05-F35.question_text: What two belt-sharing or lap mistakes must you avoid with children, and when should kids buckle?
sec05-card-sec05-F35.teaching_text: Sharing one strap crushes a child against an adult in impact; buckle every child individually before starting the engine.

sec05-card-sec05-R06.question_text: Must a child hit both age eight and four feet nine inches to exit a booster under Michigan law?
sec05-card-sec05-R06.teaching_text: Exam questions test 'whichever comes first' for the legal cutoff while noting height best guarantees safe belt geometry.

sec05-card-sec05-R07.question_text: How does the under-four back-seat rule pair with placing a rear-facing seat up front?
sec05-card-sec05-R07.teaching_text: Keep under-fours in back whenever space exists, and never place a rear-facing carrier up front with an active air bag.

sec05-card-sec05-F34.question_text: Above what speed is riding in an open pickup bed banned for anyone under eighteen, and which uses are exempt?
sec05-card-sec05-F34.teaching_text: Above fifteen miles per hour, minors under eighteen cannot ride in open truck beds outside farm, construction, military, parade, or rescue work.

sec05-card-sec05-F36.question_text: Where can parents get hands-on help checking or installing a child car seat?
sec05-card-sec05-F36.teaching_text: Health departments and certified technicians listed at cert dot safekids dot org verify tight, recall-free installations.

sec05-card-sec05-F37.question_text: Why does the handbook warn against buying or using secondhand child safety seats?
sec05-card-sec05-F37.teaching_text: Used seats can hide crash damage, outdated safety standards, or missing straps and instruction manuals.

sec05-card-sec05-R08.question_text: How does Michigan's pickup-bed age cutoff differ from its all-seat mandatory seat-belt cutoff?
sec05-card-sec05-R08.teaching_text: Do not swap these teen cutoffs—all-row belt law runs under sixteen, while open pickup-bed limits run under eighteen.

sec10-card-sec10-F01.question_text: Why does sign silhouette matter in Michigan, and how many basic shapes does the handbook teach?
sec10-card-sec10-F01.teaching_text: Recognizing those nine silhouettes lets you read faded, snow-covered, or backlit panels before lettering comes into focus.

sec10-card-sec10-F02.question_text: Which commands belong to the eight-sided octagon and the downward-pointing triangle?
sec10-card-sec10-F02.teaching_text: Giving STOP and YIELD unique silhouettes ensures drivers never confuse intersection priority from behind or in snow.

sec10-card-sec10-F03.question_text: What categories do a four-sided diamond and a five-sided pentagon identify?
sec10-card-sec10-F03.teaching_text: A house-like five-sided outline flags school zones and child crossings instantly, separate from general diamond hazards.

sec10-card-sec10-F04.question_text: Which specific highway zone uses a sideways pennant-shaped sign?
sec10-card-sec10-F04.teaching_text: Spotting that sideways pennant ahead down the left roadside stops risky two-lane passes before blind hills.

sec10-card-sec10-F05.question_text: How does a horizontal rectangle's message differ from a vertical rectangle's message?
sec10-card-sec10-F05.teaching_text: Wide overhead boards point toward towns and exits, whereas upright panels post enforceable speed, turn, and parking laws.

sec10-card-sec10-F06.question_text: Which two distinct sign shapes both warn of a railroad crossing?
sec10-card-sec10-F06.teaching_text: A round yellow disc gives early advance warning upstream before the white X crossbuck marks the tracks themselves.

sec10-card-sec10-R22.question_text: Both warn of hazards—so what separates a pennant shape from a diamond shape?
sec10-card-sec10-R22.teaching_text: Diamonds cover curves, deer, and intersections broadly, while the pennant has one job—marking no-passing stretches.

sec10-card-sec10-R23.question_text: What single road hazard links the circular sign shape and the crossbuck together?
sec10-card-sec10-R23.teaching_text: Either silhouette tells you steel rails lie ahead so you start scanning and listening immediately.

sec10-card-sec10-F08.question_text: What three commands or restrictions does red convey on a traffic sign?
sec10-card-sec10-F08.teaching_text: Red never offers optional advice—it signals mandatory stops, wrong-way danger, or banned maneuvers.

sec10-card-sec10-F09.question_text: How do blue highway signs and green highway signs split motorist information?
sec10-card-sec10-F09.teaching_text: Blue boards point tired travelers toward gas, food, lodging, and hospitals while green panels steer exits and mileage.

sec10-card-sec10-F10.question_text: Both call for caution—how does yellow sign color differ from orange sign color?
sec10-card-sec10-F10.teaching_text: Permanent curves and merges wear yellow, whereas temporary roadwork and maintenance zones always switch to orange.

sec10-card-sec10-F11.question_text: What legal role do black-and-white traffic signs play along Michigan roads?
sec10-card-sec10-F11.teaching_text: Speed limits, lane assignments, and turn rules appear in crisp black and white because ignoring them earns citations.

sec10-card-sec10-F12.question_text: What does fluorescent yellow-green warn of compared with fluorescent pink?
sec10-card-sec10-F12.teaching_text: Bright yellow-green highlights walkers, bikes, and schoolchildren, while hot coral-pink marks sudden crashes or emergency detours.

sec10-card-sec10-F13.question_text: What kind of destinations do brown roadside guide signs point toward?
sec10-card-sec10-F13.teaching_text: Campgrounds, state parks, boat launches, and historic landmarks use brown panels so tourists spot them cleanly.

sec10-card-sec10-F14.question_text: What laws do regulatory signs set, and what shape and color combinations do they usually take?
sec10-card-sec10-F14.teaching_text: Whether limiting speed or barring turns, crisp rectangular law signs carry ticket penalties rather than optional advice.

sec10-card-sec10-R24.question_text: How do Michigan's three warning colors—yellow, orange, and fluorescent pink—divide up road hazards?
sec10-card-sec10-R24.teaching_text: Separating everyday road geometry from scheduled construction and sudden crash scenes prepares you for what lies ahead.
sec10-card-sec10-R24.must_match_memory_hook: Yellow permanent, orange work, pink incidents

visual_sync.text_span: Yellow permanent, orange work, pink incidents

sec10-card-sec10-R25.question_text: Can you match blue, green, and brown guide signs to their three traveler topics?
sec10-card-sec10-R25.teaching_text: Scanning sign background color first lets you filter fuel stops, freeway exits, and campgrounds at highway speed.
sec10-card-sec10-R25.must_match_memory_hook: Blue services, green routes, brown parks

visual_sync.text_span: Blue services, green routes, brown parks

sec10-card-sec10-F07.question_text: Which four levels of highway networks do numbered route markers identify?
sec10-card-sec10-F07.teaching_text: Distinct shield outlines tell navigators instantly whether they are following a national interstate or a local county road.

sec10-card-sec10-F15.question_text: What has happened when an Incident Ahead sign appears, and what do follow-up signs provide?
sec10-card-sec10-F15.teaching_text: Crashes, spills, or downed lines block normal lanes unexpectedly, so temporary trailblazers route traffic safely past.

sec10-card-sec10-F16.question_text: What information do a blue gas-pump panel and a green Exit gore panel give freeway drivers?
sec10-card-sec10-F16.teaching_text: Blue symbol plaques announce fuel availability ahead before the green Exit panel marks the ramp gore itself.

sec10-card-sec10-F21.question_text: What does a green destination sign listing town names—like Brookfield and Onondaga—tell you?
sec10-card-sec10-F21.teaching_text: Directional arrows paired with community names confirm which turn or lane reaches each town.

sec10-card-sec10-F22.question_text: Who may park in a stall marked by a sign bearing the wheelchair symbol?
sec10-card-sec10-F22.teaching_text: Keeping accessible spaces open preserves ramp and aisle clearance for drivers and passengers with mobility permits.

sec10-card-sec10-F23.question_text: What road network does an M-numbered route marker—such as M-thirty-two—identify?
sec10-card-sec10-F23.teaching_text: Michigan prefixes its state trunkline highways with the letter M inside a diamond route marker.

sec10-card-sec10-F24.question_text: What kind of restriction can a Parking Permitted sign place on legal street parking?
sec10-card-sec10-F24.teaching_text: Green parking signs often allow curb stops only up to a set duration—like two hours—within posted daytime windows.

sec10-card-sec10-F36.question_text: What do a blue Rest Area sign and a pentagon School Crossing sign each point out?
sec10-card-sec10-F36.teaching_text: Blue highway boards announce roadside rest stops while five-sided crossing panels demand sharp scanning for kids.

sec10-card-sec10-F25.question_text: What two obligations must you fulfill at every red octagonal stop sign before moving on?
sec10-card-sec10-F25.teaching_text: Rolling stops miss pedestrians stepping off the curb and cross-street cars holding right-of-way.

sec10-card-sec10-F26.question_text: What speed and priority actions does a red-and-white triangular yield sign require?
sec10-card-sec10-F26.teaching_text: Approaching slow enough to stop smoothly ensures vehicles already crossing your path never have to brake.

sec10-card-sec10-F27.question_text: What maneuvers do No Turn On Red and red-circle slash turn signs prohibit?
sec10-card-sec10-F27.teaching_text: Checking intersection posts before turning catches bans on red-light turns, right turns, or mid-corridor U-turns.

sec10-card-sec10-F28.question_text: What do lane-use turn signs and a Center Lane Left Turn Only sign assign?
sec10-card-sec10-F28.teaching_text: Dedicated turn markings pull slowing left-turning vehicles out of fast straight-through lanes to prevent rear-ends.

sec10-card-sec10-F18.question_text: How does traffic move across all lanes where a One Way sign is posted?
sec10-card-sec10-F18.teaching_text: Checking One Way arrows before turning onto city streets prevents turning straight into opposing bumpers.

sec10-card-sec10-F19.question_text: What legal rule does a Speed Limit fifty sign establish on that roadway stretch?
sec10-card-sec10-F19.teaching_text: Posted maximums cap speed under ideal dry conditions, and worse weather still requires slowing below fifty.

sec10-card-sec10-R10.question_text: Why are Roundabout Ahead, Stop Ahead, and Yield Ahead diamonds posted upstream?
sec10-card-sec10-R10.teaching_text: Curves, hills, or foliage can hide the control itself until braking distance gets tight.

sec10-card-sec10-F30.question_text: On which side of a median island or roadway obstruction must you pass at a Keep Left sign?
sec10-card-sec10-F30.teaching_text: Channelizing islands and work zones use directional Keep Left arrows when the right side is closed or opposing.

sec10-card-sec10-F31.question_text: What simple command does a square Do Not Enter sign enforce?
sec10-card-sec10-F31.teaching_text: Exit ramps, one-way street mouths, and restricted lanes post Do Not Enter to block head-on entry.

sec10-card-sec10-F32.question_text: Who may use a freeway median strip marked Authorized Vehicles Only—and how must everyday drivers reverse direction?
sec10-card-sec10-F32.teaching_text: Pulling a civilian U-turn across a gravel freeway median cuts into seventy-mile-per-hour left-lane traffic.

sec10-card-sec10-F33.question_text: What dangerous situation has already happened if you face a Wrong Way sign, and what must you do?
sec10-card-sec10-F33.teaching_text: Pulling off and getting out safely at once avoids a high-speed head-on crash with approaching traffic.

sec10-card-sec10-F34.question_text: What vehicles are barred wherever a No Trucks sign stands?
sec10-card-sec10-F34.teaching_text: Residential streets, weak bridges, and tight parkways ban heavy trucks to protect pavement and clearance.

sec10-card-sec10-R05.question_text: When a yellow Obstacle in Roadway diamond shows arrows splitting left and right, where may you pass?
sec10-card-sec10-R05.teaching_text: Unlike Keep Right or Keep Left, split-arrow diamonds mean same-direction lanes flank both sides of the divider.

sec10-card-sec10-R27.question_text: How does your position differ when facing Do Not Enter versus facing Wrong Way?
sec10-card-sec10-R27.teaching_text: Do Not Enter stands at the threshold to stop entry, while Wrong Way catches drivers who already crossed inside.

sec10-card-sec10-F29.question_text: What does Do Not Pass forbid, and what does Pass With Care on the right announce?
sec10-card-sec10-F29.teaching_text: Even after Pass With Care restores legal passing, you still wait for clear sightlines and oncoming space.

sec10-card-sec10-F35.question_text: When a number plaque under a railroad crossbuck displays three tracks, what lies at the grade crossing?
sec10-card-sec10-F35.teaching_text: Multiple parallel tracks mean a departing train on track one can hide a fast locomotive on track two or three.

sec10-card-sec10-F37.question_text: What top speed defines vehicles wearing a rear orange slow-moving triangle, and what examples use it?
sec10-card-sec10-F37.teaching_text: Closing at fifty-five behind a twenty-five-mile-per-hour tractor or Amish buggy eats up football fields in seconds.

sec10-card-sec10-R03.question_text: What hazard ahead does a warning sign bearing the letters R-R announce?
sec10-card-sec10-R03.teaching_text: Spotting advance RR warnings gives you time to ease off the gas, silence distractions, and scan the tracks.

sec10-card-sec10-R08.question_text: Which side of the highway mounts the yellow No Passing Zone pennant, and what does it warn?
sec10-card-sec10-R08.teaching_text: Mounting the pennant on the left puts it right in your line of sight as you peek out to pass.

sec10-card-sec10-R26.question_text: How do Do Not Pass and right-side Pass With Care work together along a two-lane highway?
sec10-card-sec10-R26.teaching_text: Together they bracket blind hills, curves, or intersections where oncoming cars could appear suddenly.

sec10-card-sec10-F17.question_text: Why does a Bridge Ices Before Road sign matter when normal pavement still feels dry and grippy?
sec10-card-sec10-F17.teaching_text: Cold air circulating underneath bridge spans freezes moisture into invisible black ice long before insulated soil roads.

sec10-card-sec10-F20.question_text: How must you drive—and whom must you obey—where a School Children Present sign stands?
sec10-card-sec10-F20.teaching_text: Kids dart unexpectedly near school curbs, and adult crossing guards hold legal authority to halt traffic.

sec10-card-sec10-R01.question_text: How does a Road Turns Left diamond differ from a Road Curves Ahead reverse-curve diamond?
sec10-card-sec10-R01.teaching_text: Reading the arrow kink tells you whether steering recovers straight after one corner or swings immediately opposite.

sec10-card-sec10-R02.question_text: What does a small speed plaque—like thirty-five miles per hour—mounted beneath a Winding Curve Ahead sign advise?
sec10-card-sec10-R02.teaching_text: Slowing to the advisory number before the first bend keeps lateral forces from pushing tires across the centerline.

sec10-card-sec10-R04.question_text: What do Watch for Bicyclists and Watch for Pedestrians warning diamonds alert you to?
sec10-card-sec10-R04.teaching_text: Trailheads, village centers, and campus corridors post diamond alerts where unprotected users share or cross pavement.

sec10-card-sec10-R06.question_text: What measurement does a Maximum Height sign—such as twelve feet six inches—display?
sec10-card-sec10-R06.teaching_text: Box-truck, camper, and rooftop-cargo drivers check clearance diamonds early to avoid wedging under low bridges.

sec10-card-sec10-R07.question_text: How fast should you take a freeway off-ramp marked Exit twenty-five miles per hour?
sec10-card-sec10-R07.teaching_text: Tight cloverleaf loops shed highway speed fast, where entering hot risks rolling top-heavy SUVs or sliding off-ramp.

sec10-card-sec10-R09.question_text: How does a cross-shaped Intersection Ahead symbol differ from a Side Road Ahead symbol?
sec10-card-sec10-R09.teaching_text: Cross symbols warn traffic cuts all the way across from both sides, while side-road stems warn of right-hand entries.

sec10-card-sec10-R11.question_text: What lies ahead when you pass an orange Road Work Ahead diamond?
sec10-card-sec10-R11.teaching_text: Slowing and scanning early spots flaggers, narrowed shoulders, and equipment entering live lanes.

sec10-card-sec10-R15.question_text: What terrain does a Hill sign warn of, and what two actions should drivers—especially heavy trucks—take?
sec10-card-sec10-R15.teaching_text: Shifting into a lower gear before descending uses engine braking so friction pads do not overheat and fade.

sec10-card-sec10-R16.question_text: When does the pavement hazard marked by a Slippery When Wet sign kick in?
sec10-card-sec10-R16.teaching_text: Polished bridge decks, shaded curves, and oily asphalt lose traction rapidly as soon as storms wet them.

sec10-card-sec10-R18.question_text: What kind of crossing does a combined Bicyclists and Pedestrians sign identify?
sec10-card-sec10-R18.teaching_text: Multi-use rail trails cross rural and suburban roads at speed, bringing fast bikes alongside walking families.

sec10-card-sec10-R12.question_text: From which side will vehicles blend in when you pass a Merging Traffic diamond?
sec10-card-sec10-R12.teaching_text: Spotting the angled right-side arrow lets you move left a lane or open a clean gap early.

sec10-card-sec10-R13.question_text: Which lane is disappearing at a Lane Ends Merge Left sign, and who holds right-of-way during the merge?
sec10-card-sec10-R13.teaching_text: Drivers whose right lane runs out must match speed and yield to vehicles already established in the left lane.

sec10-card-sec10-R14.question_text: What highway transition do Divided Highway Ends and Two-Way Traffic signs announce?
sec10-card-sec10-R14.teaching_text: Forgetting the median ended is a classic trap where drivers drift left into newly opposing traffic.

sec10-card-sec10-R17.question_text: How much distance remains before the right lane disappears at Michigan's Right Lane Ends notice?
sec10-card-sec10-R17.teaching_text: At highway speeds five hundred feet vanishes in roughly six seconds, so check mirrors and merge left promptly.

sec10-card-sec10-R19.question_text: Which two paint colors form standard lane markings, and what three jobs do they perform?
sec10-card-sec10-R19.teaching_text: Painted lines work right alongside upright signs to separate directions, ban unsafe passes, and guide lane choice.

sec10-card-sec10-R20.question_text: What traffic flow do white lane lines—and specifically broken white lines—separate?
sec10-card-sec10-R20.teaching_text: Seeing white dashes beside both doors confirms adjacent lanes travel your way and permits safe lane changes.

sec10-card-sec10-R21.question_text: What lane-keeping rule applies to a broken white line versus a double yellow line?
sec10-card-sec10-R21.teaching_text: Riding astride dashed white paint hogs two lanes, while crossing double yellow invades blind opposing traffic.

sec13-card-sec13-F01.question_text: Alongside vehicle controls and traffic laws, what five personal traits does safe driving require?
sec13-card-sec13-F01.teaching_text: Passing a written quiz gives you rules, yet real traffic survival depends on calm judgment and common sense.

sec13-card-sec13-F02.question_text: Through what three practice stages does a teen driver develop real road skill and confidence?
sec13-card-sec13-F02.teaching_text: Starting on a closed range before supervised adult miles prevents throwing beginners straight into fast solo traffic.

sec13-card-sec13-F03.question_text: What mental habit can dull hazard awareness even among experienced middle-aged drivers?
sec13-card-sec13-F03.teaching_text: Years of incident-free commuting tempt seasoned drivers into zoning out right when road conditions change.

sec13-card-sec13-F04.question_text: How can older drivers sharpen changing driving skills, and which two national programs does Michigan highlight?
sec13-card-sec13-F04.teaching_text: Refresher classes from AAA RoadWise Driver or AARP Driver Safety help older motorists adapt smoothly over time.

sec13-card-sec13-F05.question_text: Which reckless traffic maneuvers and hostile signals characterize aggressive drivers?
sec13-card-sec13-F05.teaching_text: Running red lights, passing on the right shoulder, honking, and flashing beams turn one impatient driver into everyone's hazard.

sec13-card-sec13-F06.question_text: What dangerous escalation can happen if you retaliate against an aggressive driver, and what makes it road rage?
sec13-card-sec13-F06.teaching_text: Matching anger with anger can push a traffic dispute into a criminal assault using a weapon or the car itself.

sec13-card-sec13-F07.question_text: What percentage of all traffic fatalities have federal safety officials linked to aggressive driving behaviors?
sec13-card-sec13-F07.teaching_text: Two-thirds of deadly crashes trace back to speeding, tailgating, red-light running, and other aggressive choices.

sec13-card-sec13-F08.question_text: How should you respond when another motorist merges or turns poorly in front of you?
sec13-card-sec13-F08.teaching_text: Trying to defend your lane to prove a point turns someone else's mistake into a preventable collision.

sec13-card-sec13-F09.question_text: What should you do if someone tailgates you while you are passing in the left lane, and why?
sec13-card-sec13-F09.teaching_text: Blocking the passing lane tempts impatient drivers behind you into reckless right-side weaving.

sec13-card-sec13-F10.question_text: How should you handle a tailgater on an ordinary road, and why is putting them ahead safer?
sec13-card-sec13-F10.teaching_text: Keeping an erratic tailgater in front of your windshield lets you control the cushion instead of getting rear-ended.

sec13-card-sec13-F11.question_text: What rule applies to angry hand gestures—and how should you respond if another driver gestures after your mistake?
sec13-card-sec13-F11.teaching_text: A quick apologetic wave defuses tension immediately when you accidentally cut someone close.

sec13-card-sec13-F12.question_text: What four actions protect you when an aggressive driver tries to confront you on the road?
sec13-card-sec13-F12.teaching_text: Locking eyes feels like a challenge to an enraged driver, so create distance, ignore insults, and phone police safely.

sec13-card-sec13-F13.question_text: How should you handle the scene if an aggressive driver crashes farther up the road ahead of you?
sec13-card-sec13-F13.teaching_text: Parking well back keeps you clear of both secondary collisions and potential confrontation while giving officers witness facts.

sec13-card-sec13-F14.question_text: Which roadway location accounts for more traffic deaths and serious injuries than any other?
sec13-card-sec13-F14.teaching_text: Crossing paths and high-angle T-bone impacts make intersections deadlier than straight highway stretches.

sec13-card-sec13-F15.question_text: What elements must you scan approaching an intersection, and what rule applies whenever another driver's move looks uncertain?
sec13-card-sec13-F15.teaching_text: Giving up a second of right-of-way beats guessing wrong when a cross-street car rolls fast toward a stop sign.

sec13-card-sec13-F16.question_text: Why should you look twice specifically for motorcycles, bicycles, and mopeds at intersections?
sec13-card-sec13-F16.teaching_text: A quick single glance registers empty asphalt where a narrow bike is closing faster than your eyes estimate.

sec13-card-sec13-F17.question_text: How should you handle an intersection where trees, buildings, or winter snowbanks block your cross-traffic view?
sec13-card-sec13-F17.teaching_text: Inching out after your legal stop lets you peek past snowbanks without launching blind across live lanes.

sec13-card-sec13-F18.question_text: How do freeways move traffic, and which six road users or small vehicles are barred from using them?
sec13-card-sec13-F18.teaching_text: High-speed limited-access lanes exclude walkers, cyclists, mopeds, ATVs, slow farm rigs, and motorcycles of one twenty-four cc or smaller.

sec13-card-sec13-F19.question_text: Why must you scan carefully for Do Not Enter, Wrong Way, and speed signs at freeway interchanges?
sec13-card-sec13-F19.teaching_text: Side-by-side ramp mouths make one wrong turn at night put you head-on onto an off-ramp.

sec13-card-sec13-F20.question_text: What steps take you smoothly from the acceleration lane onto the freeway—and whom must you yield to?
sec13-card-sec13-F20.teaching_text: Never assume through traffic will shift left for you—build highway speed on the ramp and merge into a verified gap.

sec13-card-sec13-F24.question_text: How should freeway drivers respond near entrance merge signs, and what sudden exit mistake should they watch for?
sec13-card-sec13-F24.teaching_text: Easing pace or moving left helps ramp cars blend, while staying alert catches drivers diving across lanes for exits.

sec13-card-sec13-F26.question_text: Under Michigan's merge law, which driver holds the legal duty to yield and adjust speed when entering or leaving a freeway?
sec13-card-sec13-F26.teaching_text: Drivers on the ramp—never through freeway traffic—carry the statutory duty to yield to immediate hazards.

sec13-card-sec13-R19.question_text: Between the merging ramp driver and existing freeway traffic, who must adjust speed and lane placement?
sec13-card-sec13-R19.teaching_text: Test traps claim freeway drivers must make room, when Michigan law places speed and gap adjustment on the merger.

sec13-card-sec13-F21.question_text: On a freeway with two lanes in your direction, when may you legally use the left lane?
sec13-card-sec13-F21.teaching_text: Left lanes on two-lane freeways are reserved for passing, left exits, helping merges, heavy congestion, or roadside emergency and work crews.

sec13-card-sec13-F22.question_text: Which lanes may you use when a freeway has three or more lanes in your direction, and what if you drive near minimum speed?
sec13-card-sec13-F22.teaching_text: Wider urban freeways open every lane to normal flow, provided minimum-speed drivers stay with slower right-side traffic.

sec13-card-sec13-F23.question_text: How many occupants do high-occupancy vehicle lanes require during peak hours—and who can use them off-peak or anytime?
sec13-card-sec13-F23.teaching_text: Solo cars qualify outside posted rush-hour windows, and motorcycles ride HOV lanes legally around the clock.

sec13-card-sec13-F25.question_text: When is stopping on a freeway permitted, and how must you pull off?
sec13-card-sec13-F25.teaching_text: Stopping on live freeway lanes or half-on the stripe for directions invites high-speed rear-end crashes.

sec13-card-sec13-F27.question_text: Where should you begin braking when exiting a freeway, and why must you respect the ramp speed sign?
sec13-card-sec13-F27.teaching_text: Braking early in the main travel lane surprises seventy-mile-per-hour traffic behind you, and tight exit loops flip fast cars.

sec13-card-sec13-F28.question_text: What must you never do if you miss your freeway exit—including at paved median crossovers—and what is the right move?
sec13-card-sec13-F28.teaching_text: Median turnarounds belong exclusively to emergency responders and highway crews, never to motorists who missed an off-ramp.

sec13-card-sec13-R17.question_text: How does Michigan's lane-selection rule change when a freeway expands from two lanes to three or more in your direction?
sec13-card-sec13-R17.teaching_text: Check lane count carefully on exam scenarios before applying the strict keep-right rule.

sec13-card-sec13-R18.question_text: During what time window do HOV occupancy limits apply, and which vehicle type is exempt at all hours?
sec13-card-sec13-R18.teaching_text: Motorcyclists never need a passenger to use high-occupancy lanes even in peak rush-hour traffic.

sec13-card-sec13-F29.question_text: Why does freeway driving trigger drowsiness and highway hypnosis so easily?
sec13-card-sec13-F29.teaching_text: Monotonous engine drone and unbroken pavement lull alert brains toward sleep without stop-and-go city stimulation.

sec13-card-sec13-F30.question_text: Why avoid trusting coffee or stay-awake pills on long drives, and what break schedule works instead?
sec13-card-sec13-F30.teaching_text: Stimulants mask exhaustion briefly before wearing off, whereas swapping drivers or stopping ten minutes every two hours protects focus.

sec13-card-sec13-F31.question_text: How should you use your eyes if you must continue driving briefly while feeling tired until reaching a stop?
sec13-card-sec13-F31.teaching_text: Actively shifting gaze across mirrors, far horizon, and both shoulders breaks the fixed tunnel stare of highway hypnosis.

sec13-card-sec13-F32.question_text: In what traffic and road setting does cruise control work best, and how high should you set it?
sec13-card-sec13-F32.teaching_text: Open rural stretches let steady speed control shine without exceeding the posted limit.

sec13-card-sec13-F33.question_text: How do pressing the gas pedal versus pressing the brake pedal affect active cruise control?
sec13-card-sec13-F33.teaching_text: Accelerating briefly to pass lets the car settle back to cruise speed afterward, whereas touching the brake disengages cruise.

sec13-card-sec13-F34.question_text: Under which four traffic, ramp, weather, or towing conditions should you keep cruise control switched off?
sec13-card-sec13-F34.teaching_text: Spinning tires on rain, snow, or ice—or constantly resetting speed around ramps and heavy trailers—steals control and focus.

sec13-card-sec13-R20.question_text: What happens to your cruise-control setting if you tap the accelerator compared with tapping the brake?
sec13-card-sec13-R20.teaching_text: Exam questions flip these pedals—remember only the brake tap switches cruise off.

sec13-card-sec13-R01.question_text: What three emergency responses help you survive an oncoming vehicle drifting into your lane?
sec13-card-sec13-R01.teaching_text: Sounding the horn wakes a distracted oncoming driver while controlled braking and steering toward the right shoulder open space.

sec13-card-sec13-R02.question_text: Why should you avoid swerving into the left lane to dodge an oncoming car in your lane?
sec13-card-sec13-R02.teaching_text: When that startled driver snaps back into their own lane, swerving left puts both bumpers head-on again.

sec13-card-sec13-R03.question_text: When stopping in time is impossible, how should you steer around a vehicle ahead?
sec13-card-sec13-R03.teaching_text: Yanking the wheel farther than needed triggers a violent skid or rollover at highway speed.

sec13-card-sec13-R12.question_text: Which two abrupt driver inputs cause most skids on slick roads, and how can you feel surface grip early?
sec13-card-sec13-R12.teaching_text: Testing the brake pedal lightly when safe reveals icy or slick grip before an intersection forces hard braking.

sec13-card-sec13-R14.question_text: What sequence of pedal and steering moves recovers your car from a skid—including any counter-skid?
sec13-card-sec13-R14.teaching_text: Keep your foot off the gas, aim front wheels smoothly down your intended lane, catch the rebound swing, and straighten.

sec13-card-sec13-R15.question_text: How does emergency braking with anti-lock brakes differ from threshold braking without anti-lock?
sec13-card-sec13-R15.teaching_text: Pumping anti-lock brakes defeats their computer pulsing, whereas non-ABS cars need firm pressure right below lockup.

sec13-card-sec13-R16.question_text: How should you apply the brake pedal to slow and stop under normal dry-road conditions?
sec13-card-sec13-R16.teaching_text: Smooth, firm braking alerts drivers behind you early and keeps cabin weight balanced.

sec13-card-sec13-R13.question_text: Why must standard brakes stay unlocked during a hard stop, and how do full anti-lock brakes let you steer?
sec13-card-sec13-R13.teaching_text: Locked front tires slide straight ahead regardless of wheel angle, whereas anti-lock brakes prevent lockup while you press firmly.

sec13-card-sec13-R04.question_text: Which fluids should you inspect before Michigan winter arrives, including a smart windshield-washer upgrade?
sec13-card-sec13-R04.teaching_text: Summer washer fluid freezes solid on subzero windshields unless swapped for winter antifreeze washer blend alongside fresh coolant.

sec13-card-sec13-R05.question_text: How should you adjust trip time, speed, and gap in fog, rain, or snow—and what freezes first?
sec13-card-sec13-R05.teaching_text: Cold air circulates both above and beneath elevated bridge decks and underpasses, icing them while regular pavement stays wet.

sec13-card-sec13-R06.question_text: When during a rainfall is pavement slickest, why, and how much following distance should you leave?
sec13-card-sec13-R06.teaching_text: Fresh rain floats unwashed engine oil to the surface during the first thirty minutes, requiring at least double your normal gap.

sec13-card-sec13-R07.question_text: Why must you test your brakes after driving through deep puddles or heavy downpours, and how do you dry them?
sec13-card-sec13-R07.teaching_text: Soaked linings can pull sideways or fail to bite until gentle slow-speed pedal pressure warms them dry.

sec13-card-sec13-R08.question_text: What happens to your tires during hydroplaning, and which three factors make it much more likely?
sec13-card-sec13-R08.teaching_text: Bald tread, underinflated tires, and excess speed trap a wedge of water beneath the rubber and erase steering.

sec13-card-sec13-R09.question_text: Why must you never drive around flood barricades—and why avoid deep standing water even without barricades?
sec13-card-sec13-R09.teaching_text: Murky floodwater hides downed wires, debris, or washed-out roadbeds while stalling and destroying engines.

sec13-card-sec13-R10.question_text: Which headlights belong on in fog, and what should you do if visibility drops to zero?
sec13-card-sec13-R10.teaching_text: High beams bounce blinding white glare off fog droplets, and zero visibility demands pulling completely off with four-way flashers.

sec13-card-sec13-R11.question_text: How should you adjust speed and braking on snow and ice—and what winter crossing hazard does Michigan highlight?
sec13-card-sec13-R11.teaching_text: Reduced winter traction stretches every stop right where rural snowmobile trails cross Michigan highways.

sec02-card-sec02-F01.question_text: How many driver-education segments and licensing tiers make up Michigan's Graduated Driver Licensing, and when does GDL end?
sec02-card-sec02-F01.teaching_text: Graduated Driver Licensing adds freedom step by step as teens prove safe habits until turning eighteen.

sec02-card-sec02-F02.question_text: What is the earliest age you may begin driver-education Segment one, and whose permission is required?
sec02-card-sec02-F02.teaching_text: Enrolling four months before fifteen gives teens time to finish Segment one right before learner eligibility.

sec02-card-sec02-F03.question_text: How many classroom, behind-the-wheel, and observation hours are required in driver-education Segment one?
sec02-card-sec02-F03.teaching_text: Missing even one hour of classroom, driving, or back-seat observation holds back your Segment one completion certificate.

sec02-card-sec02-F04.question_text: What minimum percentage score is required to pass the Segment one state exam?
sec02-card-sec02-F04.teaching_text: Logging every class and driving hour still requires hitting seventy percent on the written Segment one state check.

sec02-card-sec02-F12.question_text: What logged driving hours—including night hours—and Level one holding period are required before starting Segment two?
sec02-card-sec02-F12.teaching_text: Rushing into Segment two early fails check-in unless your log shows thirty hours—two after dark—across three straight months.

sec02-card-sec02-F13.question_text: How many classroom hours does Segment two include, and what score passes its state exam?
sec02-card-sec02-F13.teaching_text: Segment two reinforces hazard judgment after real road practice with six classroom hours and a seventy-percent exam bar.

sec02-card-sec02-R10.question_text: What passing score do the Segment one and Segment two driver-education state exams have in common?
sec02-card-sec02-R10.teaching_text: Remembering one single seventy-percent passing mark covers both Michigan driver-education segment exams.

sec02-card-sec02-F05.question_text: What minimum age, office accompaniment, and screening apply to getting a Level one Learner's License?
sec02-card-sec02-F05.teaching_text: Showing up alone at fourteen years and nine months will not work because a parent or guardian must accompany you.

sec02-card-sec02-F06.question_text: Alongside your Segment one certificate, which four identity and residency proofs must you bring for Level one?
sec02-card-sec02-F06.teaching_text: Bring your Segment one certificate plus Social Security proof, lawful presence, identity, and Michigan residency in one trip.

sec02-card-sec02-F07.question_text: What convenience do teens issued a photo hard card at Level one get at Level two and at age eighteen?
sec02-card-sec02-F07.teaching_text: Getting photographed onto a hard card early lets qualified teens advance without another counter line and receive their adult card by mail.

sec02-card-sec02-F08.question_text: Who must sit in the front passenger seat whenever a Level one driver is behind the wheel?
sec02-card-sec02-F08.teaching_text: Driving solo or putting your supervising adult in the back row violates Level one supervision rules.

sec02-card-sec02-F09.question_text: What written proof must a designated adult aged twenty-one or older have to supervise a Level one driver?
sec02-card-sec02-F09.teaching_text: Verbal permission from home will not satisfy a traffic stop if a non-parent supervisor lacks signed parent authorization.

sec02-card-sec02-F10.question_text: How many total supervised hours—and how many night hours—must a Level one driver log before taking the skills test?
sec02-card-sec02-F10.teaching_text: Logging at least ten hours after dark builds real headlight and depth-perception confidence before road testing.

sec02-card-sec02-F11.question_text: What restriction does Kelsey's Law place on a Level one learner behind the wheel?
sec02-card-sec02-F11.teaching_text: Named to prevent teen distraction tragedies, Kelsey's Law bans cell-phone use while operating on a learner credential.

sec02-card-sec02-R01.question_text: How far apart are the minimum age to begin Segment one and the minimum age to receive a Level one license?
sec02-card-sec02-R01.teaching_text: Do not mix those two milestones up because Segment one starts one month earlier than Level one issuance.

sec02-card-sec02-R08.question_text: What three requirements must a non-parent adult meet to supervise a Level one teen legally?
sec02-card-sec02-R08.teaching_text: An older sibling aged nineteen or an adult missing the signed authorization letter cannot legally supervise.

sec02-card-sec02-F14.question_text: What four age, coursework, logged-hour, and holding-time rules must a teen satisfy before taking the driving skills test?
sec02-card-sec02-F14.teaching_text: Even after finishing Segment two and fifty hours, you must still reach age fifteen and six months on Level one.

sec02-card-sec02-F15.question_text: Which documents must you bring to your driving skills test, and who administers the test in Michigan?
sec02-card-sec02-F15.teaching_text: Approved private testing firms verify your fifty-hour log, learner card, Segment two certificate, and active car insurance and registration.

sec02-card-sec02-R02.question_text: How do the supervised driving hours required to enter Segment two compare with those required for the skills test?
sec02-card-sec02-R02.teaching_text: Watch both total and night numbers climb from thirty with two at night up to fifty with ten at night.

sec02-card-sec02-F16.question_text: What age, Level one holding time, and clean-record window are required for a Level two Intermediate License?
sec02-card-sec02-F16.teaching_text: Catching a ticket, at-fault crash, or suspension resets your ninety-day clean countdown before moving to Level two.

sec02-card-sec02-F17.question_text: How do teens who hold a Level one photo hard card advance to Level two once qualified?
sec02-card-sec02-F17.teaching_text: Passing your skills test and hitting the clean-record mark triggers automatic system advancement when your photo is already on file.

sec02-card-sec02-F18.question_text: What must teens holding a paper Level one credential do—and bring—to move up to Level two?
sec02-card-sec02-F18.teaching_text: Paper-card learners must appear in person with their learner card, Segment two and skills certificates, plus full identity and residency proofs.

sec02-card-sec02-F19.question_text: During what nighttime hours may a Level two driver not drive solo, and what exceptions allow driving then?
sec02-card-sec02-F19.teaching_text: Unlike zero-exception states, Michigan permits ten p.m. to five a.m. Level two trips with a twenty-one-plus supervisor, for work, or authorized activities.

sec02-card-sec02-F20.question_text: How many passengers under twenty-one may ride with a Level two driver, and what four exceptions lift that cap?
sec02-card-sec02-F20.teaching_text: Carrying multiple friends under twenty-one is barred unless a twenty-one-plus supervisor rides along, riders are immediate family, or it is work or authorized.

sec02-card-sec02-F21.question_text: When may a Level two driver use a phone under Kelsey's Law, and what penalties can a violation bring?
sec02-card-sec02-F21.teaching_text: Non-emergency calls or texts on Level two bring a civil infraction carrying fines, community service, or both.

sec02-card-sec02-R03.question_text: How many months on Level one are required before Segment two versus before the skills test and Level two?
sec02-card-sec02-R03.teaching_text: Segment two opens halfway through your mandatory six-month learner holding period so coursework bridges early and late practice.

sec02-card-sec02-R06.question_text: How does the clock for Level two's driving curfew differ from the clock for its young-passenger cap?
sec02-card-sec02-R06.teaching_text: Teens often assume the one-friend cap applies only after dark, when it actually governs daytime trips too.

sec02-card-sec02-R07.question_text: Does carrying immediate family members excuse a Level two driver from the ten p.m. to five a.m. night limit?
sec02-card-sec02-R07.teaching_text: Classic test trap—siblings lift the passenger count cap at noon, yet they do not unlock solo driving after ten p.m.

sec02-card-sec02-R09.question_text: How does advancing to Level two differ between hard-card teens and paper-card teens?
sec02-card-sec02-R09.teaching_text: Whether you skip the Secretary of State line at sixteen depends on whether you already hold a photo hard card.

sec02-card-sec02-F22.question_text: What age, Level two time, and clean-driving window are required for a Level three Full License?
sec02-card-sec02-F22.teaching_text: Even a GDL curfew or passenger violation resets the twelve-month clean streak required before reaching Level three.

sec02-card-sec02-F23.question_text: How is a Level three license issued and priced, what state limits remain, and can parents hold it back?
sec02-card-sec02-F23.teaching_text: State GDL curfews drop away automatically at zero cost once authorized, unless a parent or guardian asks to delay advancement.

sec02-card-sec02-R04.question_text: How does the clean-record window for entering Level two compare with the clean-record and holding rules for Level three?
sec02-card-sec02-R04.teaching_text: Moving into Level two checks ninety clean days, whereas graduating to Level three demands six intermediate months and twelve clean months.

sec02-card-sec02-R05.question_text: What are the minimum ages for the driving skills test, Level two, and Level three?
sec02-card-sec02-R05.teaching_text: Each milestone steps up cleanly by one birthday from fifteen on the skills test to sixteen and seventeen.

sec02-card-sec02-F24.question_text: What two major steps must a never-licensed applicant aged eighteen or older complete to earn a Michigan license?
sec02-card-sec02-F24.teaching_text: Turning eighteen skips teen driver-education segments, yet first-time adults still need a temporary instruction permit and passed road test.

sec02-card-sec02-F25.question_text: Which four document proofs must first-time adult applicants bring, and how can they shorten their counter visit?
sec02-card-sec02-F25.teaching_text: Starting your application online ahead of time speeds up counter review of identity, residency, legal presence, and Social Security proofs.

sec02-card-sec02-F26.question_text: How much does the written knowledge test cost at a Secretary of State office versus online from home?
sec02-card-sec02-F26.teaching_text: Testing in person costs zero dollars, whereas taking the convenience exam from home charges six dollars and fifty cents.

sec02-card-sec02-F27.question_text: Which three steps must an adult finish before the temporary instruction permit is issued?
sec02-card-sec02-F27.teaching_text: Clearing both written knowledge and vision checks, paying the permit fee, and taking your photo unlocks supervised practice.

sec02-card-sec02-F28.question_text: How long must an adult practice with a licensed adult before the skills test, and when does the license arrive afterward?
sec02-card-sec02-F28.teaching_text: You cannot book a same-week road test on a brand-new adult permit because thirty practice days must pass first.

sec02-card-sec02-R11.question_text: How does an adult TIP holder's pre-test practice requirement differ in measurement from a GDL teen's requirement?
sec02-card-sec02-R11.teaching_text: Adults satisfy a thirty-calendar-day permit wait, whereas GDL teens must document fifty logged supervised hours.

sec02-card-sec02-R13.question_text: When do you pay the six-dollar-and-fifty-cent fee on Michigan's written knowledge test?
sec02-card-sec02-R13.teaching_text: Choosing an in-office testing terminal avoids the optional home convenience charge completely.

sec02-card-sec02-F29.question_text: For what two statutory purposes does the Secretary of State collect Social Security numbers?
sec02-card-sec02-F29.teaching_text: State and federal mandates link Social Security records to both lawful-presence checks and child-support enforcement.

sec02-card-sec02-F30.question_text: What document must an applicant without a Social Security number present, and how recent must it be?
sec02-card-sec02-F30.teaching_text: An Social Security ineligibility letter dated sixty-one days ago gets turned away until a fresh letter is issued.

sec02-card-sec02-F31.question_text: Which official documents are accepted to prove United States citizenship or legal presence?
sec02-card-sec02-F31.teaching_text: Hospital souvenir birth certificates lack a raised government seal—bring a certified vital record, unexpired passport, or valid federal immigration card.

sec02-card-sec02-F32.question_text: What personal details must match across your application documents, and how do you bridge any name change?
sec02-card-sec02-F32.teaching_text: Bringing photocopied paperwork stalls your visit when surname differences require original court, divorce, or marriage records linking your identity.

sec02-card-sec02-F33.question_text: What rule governs copies or faxes for identity proof, and might one document not be enough?
sec02-card-sec02-F33.teaching_text: Showing a photocopy or faxed scan stops your application immediately, and some identity combinations require multiple originals.

sec02-card-sec02-F34.question_text: How long after expiration can an out-of-state or Canadian driver's license still count as identity proof?
sec02-card-sec02-F34.teaching_text: Once an out-of-state or Canadian card hits four full years expired, it stops qualifying as standalone identity proof.

sec02-card-sec02-F35.question_text: How many residency documents are required, and what date limit applies to utility, credit, or bank statements?
sec02-card-sec02-F35.teaching_text: Bring at least two separate address proofs, making sure utility, credit, or account statements come from the last ninety days.

sec02-card-sec02-F36.question_text: When can an applicant prove Michigan residency using bills or leases printed in a family member's name?
sec02-card-sec02-F36.teaching_text: Teens and spouses who have zero utility bills in their own name qualify by pairing parent or spouse bills with relationship proof.

sec02-card-sec02-R12.question_text: How does the freshness limit on a Social Security ineligibility letter compare with residency bills and statements?
sec02-card-sec02-R12.teaching_text: Do not swap those two expiration clocks—the Social Security letter ages out thirty days sooner than utility bills.

sec03-card-sec03-F01.question_text: What happens at the counter if staff have doubts about your physical fitness to drive safely?
sec03-card-sec03-F01.teaching_text: General health screening protects road safety by holding questionable applications until medical evidence and reexamination confirm fitness.

sec03-card-sec03-F02.question_text: How does using eyeglasses or contact lenses to pass the vision screening affect your Michigan license?
sec03-card-sec03-F02.teaching_text: Passing the eye chart with glasses prints a corrective-lens requirement on your card that applies every trip.

sec03-card-sec03-F03.question_text: What step is required after failing the counter vision test, and what kind of restriction can follow?
sec03-card-sec03-F03.teaching_text: Falling short at the counter sends you to an eye specialist whose evaluation may restrict you to daylight driving.

sec03-card-sec03-F04.question_text: How early before closing time must you arrive for an original operator, chauffeur, or commercial knowledge test?
sec03-card-sec03-F04.teaching_text: Walking in thirty minutes before closing turns you away from starting an original written exam.

sec03-card-sec03-F05.question_text: On which written knowledge exams are foreign-language interpreters allowed—and where are they barred?
sec03-card-sec03-F05.teaching_text: Federal commercial rules prohibit interpreters on CDL written exams even though standard car and chauffeur exams allow them.

sec03-card-sec03-F21.question_text: What rules govern using an interpreter during a driving skills test—and which license class forbids one?
sec03-card-sec03-F21.teaching_text: Road-test interpreters may translate examiner directions without coaching, and commercial tests forbid interpreters completely.

sec03-card-sec03-R03.question_text: May a non-fluent passenger-car applicant bring an interpreter to assist on the written knowledge test?
sec03-card-sec03-R03.teaching_text: Only commercial license testing blocks language interpreters, leaving regular operator applicants clear to use one.

sec03-card-sec03-F06.question_text: How many days is a temporary instruction permit valid, and what privilege does it grant?
sec03-card-sec03-F06.teaching_text: Six months of supervised adult practice gives adult beginners time to build skills before road testing.

sec03-card-sec03-F07.question_text: Which three groups of applicants are issued a Michigan temporary instruction permit?
sec03-card-sec03-F07.teaching_text: First-time adults, non-exempt foreign drivers, and anyone expired four-plus years all enter through a temporary instruction permit.

sec03-card-sec03-F08.question_text: What proofs, screenings, written exams, and counter steps are required to receive a temporary instruction permit?
sec03-card-sec03-F08.teaching_text: Expect both written knowledge and road-sign exams alongside vision screening, four document proofs, payment, and a photo.

sec03-card-sec03-F09.question_text: How long must you practice on a temporary instruction permit before taking the skills test, and how is adult driver ed treated?
sec03-card-sec03-F09.teaching_text: Calendar practice for thirty days is mandatory on the permit page while formal adult driver education stays optional.

sec03-card-sec03-F10.question_text: How can you drive legally after your passed skills test results reach the state while your hard card is in the mail?
sec03-card-sec03-F10.teaching_text: Once your examiner uploads passing results, printing your temporary operator's permit from MiLogin bridges mail delivery.

sec03-card-sec03-R06.question_text: On a temporary instruction permit, how does the thirty-day practice rule differ legally from taking an adult driver-ed course?
sec03-card-sec03-R06.teaching_text: Do not let test choices swap them—thirty practice days are required whereas adult driver-ed classes are merely encouraged.

sec03-card-sec03-F12.question_text: What does a motorcycle temporary instruction permit allow, and does it ever replace earning a CY endorsement?
sec03-card-sec03-F12.teaching_text: Treating a motorcycle permit like a permanent endorsement fails the moment your temporary practice window runs out.

sec03-card-sec03-F13.question_text: How long does a motorcycle instruction permit last, and how many can one rider get in ten years?
sec03-card-sec03-F13.teaching_text: Capping riders at two permits per decade stops people from renewing learner permits endlessly instead of earning the endorsement.
sec03-card-sec03-F13.must_match_memory_hook: One eighty days, two per decade

visual_sync.text_span: One eighty days, two per decade

sec03-card-sec03-F14.question_text: What minimum age, base credential, exams, and payment are required to get a motorcycle instruction permit?
sec03-card-sec03-F14.teaching_text: You must already hold a valid Michigan driver's license at sixteen or older before adding a motorcycle permit.

sec03-card-sec03-F15.question_text: Who must watch a motorcycle TIP rider on the road, and which two riding conditions are banned?
sec03-card-sec03-F15.teaching_text: Staying within visual sight of a licensed eighteen-plus motorcyclist—with zero night riding and zero passengers—protects novice balance.

sec03-card-sec03-R01.question_text: Why can a motorcycle TIP act only as a short bridge rather than a permanent substitute for the endorsement?
sec03-card-sec03-R01.teaching_text: With each permit lasting one hundred eighty days and a strict two-permit decade cap, riders must advance to CY.

sec03-card-sec03-R02.question_text: How does the minimum age for holding a motorcycle TIP compare with the minimum age for supervising that rider?
sec03-card-sec03-R02.teaching_text: Note that motorcycle visual supervision starts at eighteen rather than twenty-one, while the learner rider starts at sixteen.

sec03-card-sec03-F16.question_text: Which four categories of applicants must pass a Michigan driving skills test?
sec03-card-sec03-F16.teaching_text: Skipping the road test works only for active state transfers or licenses from Canada, Germany, or South Korea.

sec03-card-sec03-F17.question_text: What coursework, holding time, and fifty-hour log options prepare an under-eighteen applicant for the skills test?
sec03-card-sec03-F17.teaching_text: Families can record those fifty hours—including ten at night—inside either the printed guide or the free RoadReady app.

sec03-card-sec03-F18.question_text: What clean driving record must an under-eighteen applicant show right before the skills test and Level two application?
sec03-card-sec03-F18.teaching_text: Any conviction, civil infraction, suspension, or at-fault crash inside ninety days blocks both the skills test and advancement.

sec03-card-sec03-F19.question_text: What permit must an applicant aged eighteen or older hold before taking the driving skills test, and what wait may apply?
sec03-card-sec03-F19.teaching_text: Adult road-test examiners check for a valid temporary instruction permit and any required thirty-day practice period.

sec03-card-sec03-F20.question_text: Who administers driving skills tests in Michigan, and why should you ask about fees before booking?
sec03-card-sec03-F20.teaching_text: Private state-approved testers compete on their own fee schedules because Michigan does not fix a uniform road-test price.

sec03-card-sec03-F22.question_text: Which portion of the driving skills test comes first, and what unlocks the driving skills receipt?
sec03-card-sec03-F22.teaching_text: You must pass basic off-street parking and control maneuvers on the closed lot before heading onto public streets.

sec03-card-sec03-F23.question_text: Which four types of road environments are covered during the on-road portion of the driving skills test?
sec03-card-sec03-F23.teaching_text: Examiners watch how you handle city traffic, highway merges, rural speeds, and neighborhood intersections in one drive.

sec03-card-sec03-R04.question_text: Which three foreign countries skip Michigan's driving skills test—and what happens with any other country's license?
sec03-card-sec03-R04.teaching_text: Every foreign driver outside those three treaty partners must complete the driving skills test.

sec03-card-sec03-R05.question_text: How does the pre-skills-test record requirement for teens under eighteen contrast with the prerequisite for adults?
sec03-card-sec03-R05.teaching_text: Under-eighteen testers prove ninety violation-free days alongside GDL logs, whereas eighteen-plus testers present a temporary instruction permit.

sec03-card-sec03-F24.question_text: When can the Secretary of State ask for a Physician's Statement of Examination?
sec03-card-sec03-F24.teaching_text: Any physical or mental condition that could impair vehicle control may prompt medical clearance during initial licensing or renewal.

sec03-card-sec03-F25.question_text: How recent a seizure, blackout, or fainting episode triggers a mandatory physician's statement?
sec03-card-sec03-F25.teaching_text: Any suspected fainting spell, seizure, or blackout inside the past six months requires medical evaluation before driving continues.

sec03-card-sec03-F26.question_text: How long must chauffeur and commercial license holders stay free of blackouts, fainting spells, or seizures?
sec03-card-sec03-F26.teaching_text: Driving heavy trucks or passengers for hire doubles the episode-free window to a full twelve months.

sec03-card-sec03-F27.question_text: Who is authorized to fill out the physician's statement, and which state unit reviews it?
sec03-card-sec03-F27.teaching_text: Out-of-state doctors or physician assistants still qualify to complete the medical form before state Driver Assessment staff review your medications.

sec03-card-sec03-F28.question_text: Why should a driver reporting a serious medical condition start renewal several weeks early, and what can follow?
sec03-card-sec03-F28.teaching_text: Serious health disclosures trigger reexaminations before renewal clears, and illness-restricted cards may require periodic follow-up checks.

sec03-card-sec03-F11.question_text: Where are special licensing restrictions displayed, and how long does new-driver probation last?
sec03-card-sec03-F11.teaching_text: Officers read any special conditions right off your card, and every newly licensed Michigan driver enters at least three years of probation.

sec03-card-sec03-F29.question_text: Do GDL teens fall under Michigan's three-year new-driver probation, and is probation part of GDL?
sec03-card-sec03-F29.teaching_text: Turning eighteen ends GDL restrictions yet leaves a newly licensed teen inside Michigan's separate three-year probationary monitoring.

sec03-card-sec03-R07.question_text: How does the blackout look-back window for a general physician's statement compare with the rule for chauffeur and commercial drivers?
sec03-card-sec03-R07.teaching_text: Standard drivers trigger review for episodes inside six months, while chauffeur and CDL holders need twelve episode-free months.

sec03-card-sec03-R08.question_text: How are three-year driver probation and Graduated Driver Licensing related for teen drivers?
sec03-card-sec03-R08.teaching_text: Test questions check that three-year probation is an independent safety-monitoring program, never just another name for GDL.

sec03-card-sec03-F30.question_text: What exact sequence and waiting period apply when changing your legal name on a Michigan license?
sec03-card-sec03-F30.teaching_text: Heading straight to a Secretary of State branch fails verification unless Social Security updated your name at least three business days ago.

sec03-card-sec03-F31.question_text: What two records must your license address match under Michigan law, and what does an address update cost?
sec03-card-sec03-F31.teaching_text: Michigan aligns your residence and voter registration address at zero fee whether you update online, by mail, or in person.

sec03-card-sec03-F32.question_text: Which credentials update automatically when you change your address online, and what extra option appears?
sec03-card-sec03-F32.teaching_text: One online submission refreshes your license or ID and voter registration while prompting you to update linked vehicle titles and registrations.

sec03-card-sec03-F33.question_text: When do vehicles not linked to your license account get a new address, and what penalty can hit if you skip reporting a move?
sec03-card-sec03-F33.teaching_text: Failing to report a residential move can suspend or revoke your license, and unlinked cars update only during a vehicle transaction.

sec03-card-sec03-R11.question_text: How does updating your name differ from updating your address in both starting agency and cost?
sec03-card-sec03-R11.teaching_text: Name updates start at Social Security and charge a replacement fee, whereas address updates start at Secretary of State for free.
sec03-card-sec03-R11.must_match_memory_hook: Name Social Security paid, address free

visual_sync.text_span: Name Social Security paid, address free

sec03-card-sec03-F34.question_text: How long is a standard Michigan license valid, and how do under-twenty-one licenses expire differently?
sec03-card-sec03-F34.teaching_text: Adult cards run four years to your birthday, whereas under-twenty-one licenses always expire right on your twenty-first birthday.

sec03-card-sec03-F35.question_text: Where are renewal notices mailed, may you drive once expired, and what happens to pricing if you renew late?
sec03-card-sec03-F35.teaching_text: An outdated address can make you miss your notice, and driving expired is illegal while renewing late tacks on a penalty fee.

sec03-card-sec03-F36.question_text: Which license statuses or missing legal proofs stop you from renewing a Michigan license?
sec03-card-sec03-F36.teaching_text: Suspended, revoked, or denied credentials cannot renew, nor can applicants lacking Social Security or legal-presence verification.

sec03-card-sec03-F37.question_text: Which three remote channels can you use to renew when an in-person office visit is not required?
sec03-card-sec03-F37.teaching_text: Eligible drivers skip counter lines by renewing through postal mail, the online portal, or a self-service station.

sec03-card-sec03-F38.question_text: How often must every Michigan driver renew in person at an office, and what two updates happen there?
sec03-card-sec03-F38.teaching_text: Even drivers who renew online twice must visit an office every twelfth year for fresh vision screening and a new photo.

sec03-card-sec03-F39.question_text: What should a Michigan driver do with their license when they decide to stop driving permanently?
sec03-card-sec03-F39.teaching_text: Turning in your driver's license at a branch lets you switch cleanly to an official state identification card.

sec03-card-sec03-F40.question_text: Which three groups of residents qualify for a free Michigan state ID card?
sec03-card-sec03-F40.teaching_text: Fee waivers cover legally blind residents, drivers sixty-five-plus voluntarily surrendering licenses, and drivers losing privileges from disability.

sec03-card-sec03-R09.question_text: Why does an under-twenty-one Michigan license not follow the standard four-year cycle?
sec03-card-sec03-R09.teaching_text: Whether issued at seventeen or nineteen, an under-twenty-one card ends on your twenty-first birthday so horizontal adult credentials replace it.

sec03-card-sec03-R10.question_text: What long-term limit prevents a driver from renewing remotely by mail, online, or kiosk forever?
sec03-card-sec03-R10.teaching_text: Every twelve years the remote cycle resets with a mandatory branch visit for a vision check and updated photo.

sec03-card-sec03-R12.question_text: How does qualifying for a free state ID differ between drivers aged sixty-five-plus and legally blind residents?
sec03-card-sec03-R12.teaching_text: Turning sixty-five alone does not waive the ID fee unless you voluntarily surrender your license, whereas blindness qualifies at any age.

sec08-card-sec08-F01.question_text: Which lane should you normally drive in, and what must you do first if stopped cars, a crash, or an obstacle forces you across the center line?
sec08-card-sec08-F01.teaching_text: Pulling around a blocked lane into oncoming territory without yielding first invites a head-on collision.

sec08-card-sec08-F02.question_text: Which multi-lane road layouts or traffic controls also permit leaving the right-hand lane?
sec08-card-sec08-F02.teaching_text: Roads with three or more marked lanes, multi-lane one-way streets, or signs directing traffic left open extra lane choices.

sec08-card-sec08-F03.question_text: For which off-street entrances or exits may you legally cross the center line?
sec08-card-sec08-F03.teaching_text: Turning left into or out of a private road, alley, or driveway is a standard legal exception to crossing center markings.

sec08-card-sec08-F04.question_text: How do stopped emergency vehicles or nearby road construction affect your duty to stay in the right lane?
sec08-card-sec08-F04.teaching_text: Once safe, shifting left gives stopped emergency crews and right-shoulder construction zones essential protective space.

sec08-card-sec08-F07.question_text: Where must slow-moving vehicles travel, and what are their only two reasons to leave that lane?
sec08-card-sec08-F07.teaching_text: Camping in faster lanes backs up traffic and triggers risky passes, so leave the right lane only to pass or turn left.

sec08-card-sec08-F09.question_text: Which vehicles — and under what active warning equipment — are the only ones allowed to drive against the flow of traffic?
sec08-card-sec08-F09.teaching_text: Civilian drivers may never travel against traffic flow, an exemption reserved strictly for police and emergency rigs running lights and sirens.

sec08-card-sec08-F05.question_text: On an interstate or full-access controlled freeway, what congestion, weather, or right-lane hazard situations allow left-lane travel?
sec08-card-sec08-F05.teaching_text: Interstates default to keeping right unless heavy traffic, bad weather, or a right-lane obstacle justifies moving left.

sec08-card-sec08-F06.question_text: Besides congestion, weather, or hazards, which two additional conditions make driving in a Michigan freeway's left lane legal?
sec08-card-sec08-F06.teaching_text: Giving space to emergency or work crews — or cruising when nobody is directly ahead or behind in that lane — is allowed.

sec08-card-sec08-F08.question_text: What is Michigan's rule on weaving back and forth between lanes to speed through traffic?
sec08-card-sec08-F08.teaching_text: Zigzagging rapidly across lanes eliminates reaction buffers and sparks multi-car freeway spinouts.

sec08-card-sec08-F10.question_text: How does Michigan law distinguish driving across a median strip or barrier from using a paved median cut-through?
sec08-card-sec08-F10.teaching_text: Grass medians and barriers are off-limits, whereas paved median turnouts allow left turns unless a sign forbids them.

sec08-card-sec08-F11.question_text: Where are the only legal places to enter or leave a controlled-access highway?
sec08-card-sec08-F11.teaching_text: Cutting across ditches or shoulders onto high-speed freeways creates sudden speed differentials that cause rear-end wrecks.

sec08-card-sec08-R05.question_text: When is turning left across a divided highway's center divider legal, and when is it illegal?
sec08-card-sec08-R05.teaching_text: Look for both pavement and the absence of a prohibitory sign before turning through a median opening.

sec08-card-sec08-R06.question_text: Contrast cruising in an empty freeway left lane with weaving between lanes to move faster?
sec08-card-sec08-R06.teaching_text: Test writers contrast Michigan's legal empty-left-lane allowance against the strict ban on weaving through traffic.

sec08-card-sec08-F13.question_text: Before and as you begin a right turn, what lane, signal, yielding, and side-check steps apply?
sec08-card-sec08-F13.teaching_text: Checking that your left side is clear while yielding to walkers and emergency rigs prevents corner collisions.

sec08-card-sec08-F14.question_text: What path should your vehicle trace around the corner during a right turn?
sec08-card-sec08-F14.teaching_text: Swinging wide across adjacent lanes sideswipes oncoming or parallel drivers who expect you to hug the curb.

sec08-card-sec08-F15.question_text: What extra space allowance do trucks and buses need when making right turns?
sec08-card-sec08-F15.teaching_text: Long wheelbases track inward toward the corner curb, forcing buses and semis to swing wider on right turns.

sec08-card-sec08-F16.question_text: When turning from an intersection with multiple right-turn lanes, which lane must you finish in and why?
sec08-card-sec08-F16.teaching_text: Drifting sideways mid-corner cuts right across the nose of the vehicle turning beside you.

sec08-card-sec08-F17.question_text: What lane, signal, control, and four-group yielding steps make up a proper left turn?
sec08-card-sec08-F17.teaching_text: Watch for bicyclists alongside walkers, emergency units, and cars before cutting across opposing lanes.

sec08-card-sec08-F18.question_text: How must your front wheels be aimed while paused waiting to turn left?
sec08-card-sec08-F18.teaching_text: Pre-turning your wheels left means a rear-end tap shoves you directly into oncoming traffic.

sec08-card-sec08-F19.question_text: Where must you complete your turn when turning from multiple left-turn lanes?
sec08-card-sec08-F19.teaching_text: Holding your corresponding arc through the intersection keeps side-by-side left turners from colliding.

sec08-card-sec08-F20.question_text: Before turning left across approaching traffic, which smaller road users hidden beside or behind larger vehicles must you scan for?
sec08-card-sec08-F20.teaching_text: Slim profiles let motorcycles, scooters, and bicycles vanish behind SUVs until the moment you turn across them.

sec08-card-sec08-R08.question_text: What crash hazard does staying in your matching lane prevent inside a double turn lane?
sec08-card-sec08-R08.teaching_text: Side-by-side turning leaves only a few feet of lateral margin, so drifting wide clips your neighbor.

sec08-card-sec08-R09.question_text: At what exact moment during a left turn should you finally turn the steering wheel left?
sec08-card-sec08-R09.teaching_text: Keeping tires aimed straight ahead until your turn actually starts protects you from getting pushed into oncoming lanes.

sec08-card-sec08-F12.question_text: What is the rule on signaling turns, and which riders rely most on hand signals today?
sec08-card-sec08-F12.teaching_text: Know arm signals for left, right, and stop so you immediately read bicyclists, moped riders, scooter riders, and motorcyclists.

sec08-card-sec08-F21.question_text: What sequence of checks and signaling do you use to move one lane to the left?
sec08-card-sec08-F21.teaching_text: Mirrors leave a rear-quarter blind spot, making a shoulder head check behind and left essential before drifting over.

sec08-card-sec08-F22.question_text: What sequence of checks and signaling do you use to move one lane to the right?
sec08-card-sec08-F22.teaching_text: Passenger-side blind spots are even wider than driver-side ones, so check behind and right before signaling over.

sec08-card-sec08-R07.question_text: How do the blind-spot checks for a left lane change and a right lane change mirror each other?
sec08-card-sec08-R07.teaching_text: Glancing behind toward whichever side you plan to enter spots cars lurking outside mirror coverage.

sec08-card-sec08-F23.question_text: Which direction does traffic circulate around a roundabout's center island, and whom must entering drivers yield to?
sec08-card-sec08-F23.teaching_text: Circulating traffic — along with cyclists and pedestrians — approaches from your left as you reach the yield line.

sec08-card-sec08-F25.question_text: What four steps prepare you cleanly as you approach a roundabout's yield line?
sec08-card-sec08-F25.teaching_text: Reading lane signs early, slowing down, keeping right of the splitter island, and scanning left sets up a smooth entry.

sec08-card-sec08-F26.question_text: How do you merge into a roundabout when a gap opens, and what wrong-way mistake must you never make?
sec08-card-sec08-F26.teaching_text: Turning left at the entrance sends your car clockwise straight into approaching roundabout traffic.

sec08-card-sec08-F31.question_text: Whom must you watch out for at both the entry and exit legs of a roundabout?
sec08-card-sec08-F31.teaching_text: Crosswalks sit just outside the circulating ring on both entry and exit legs where drivers focus on car gaps.

sec08-card-sec08-F27.question_text: Once inside a roundabout, where do you position relative to the island, who holds right of way, and when is stopping allowed?
sec08-card-sec08-F27.teaching_text: Halting inside the ring triggers chain-reaction rear-enders, so stop only when unavoidable to prevent a crash or danger.
